about: a compact symmetric operator on any Hilbert space has a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors, and applied to the solution operator of L u = −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u on a bounded open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ this gives L²(Ω) an orthonormal basis of Dirichlet eigenfunctions, with the solution expansion L⁻¹f = Σ κ⁻¹⟨eₖ, f⟩eₖ — upgrading the density of eigenfunctions announced with TauCeti#5632 (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I*; Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).
name: An orthonormal basis of Dirichlet eigenfunctions

about: for the same operators, κ₁ is the minimum of the Rayleigh quotient a(u, u)/‖u‖² over nonzero u ∈ H¹₀(Ω), ‖·‖ the L²(Ω) norm, equivalently the greatest constant in the Poincaré-type inequality C‖u‖² ≤ a(u, u), with the minimum attained via Rellich–Kondrachov (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).
name: The Rayleigh characterisation of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue

about: every pointed connected cover of (X, x₀) is the quotient of the universal cover by a unique subgroup of π₁(X, x₀), so the parametrisation is a bijection under which unpointed isomorphism is conjugacy and regularity is normality (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 1.38) — the subgroup form of the classification, beside the monodromy equivalence of categories announced earlier.
name: Subgroups classify the pointed connected covers

about: ℂ ⊗ S^μ is simple, distinct shapes give non-isomorphic modules, and every simple object of FDRep ℂ Sₙ arises for exactly one partition of n, so the irreducible complex characters of Sₙ are exactly the χ^μ — carrying the rational classification announced earlier across the base change, by absolute irreducibility and flatness of intertwiner spaces (James–Kerber, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Group*).
name: The complex Specht modules classify the irreducible representations of Sₙ

about: on an elliptic curve over any field the isogeny [n] has degree n² for every nonzero integer n, via the division-polynomial computation that x ∘ [n] = Φₙ/ΨSqₙ has degree n² as a rational map — the multiplication-by-n half of the degree theory the Hasse bound consumes (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.6.4(a)).
name: The degree of multiplication by n is n²

about: every graphon W on a probability carrier satisfies t(C₄, W) ≥ t(K₂, W)⁴: the homomorphism density of the four-cycle is at least the fourth power of the edge density, the C₄ case of Sidorenko's conjecture, by the classical Cauchy–Schwarz argument (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*).
name: Sidorenko's inequality for the 4-cycle

about: at a prime Q of a finite Galois extension of number fields, unramified over 𝔭 below, an arithmetic Frobenius induces the residue-field Frobenius, has order the inertia degree f(Q/𝔭), generates the decomposition group, and is conjugated along the fibre by the Galois action (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §9).
name: The Frobenius generates the decomposition group

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ the finite-moment Wasserstein space is separable when X is separable and complete when X is complete and separable, by the classical path-space gluing of near-optimal couplings, so P_p of a Polish space is Polish (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 6.18).
name: The Wasserstein space P_p(X) is complete and separable

about: for x′ = v(x) with v of class C^(n+1) and globally Lipschitz, the solution is jointly C^(n+1) in initial condition and time near t = 0, packaged as a genuine local flow with the law Φ(x, t + s) = Φ(Φ(x, t), s) for a field smooth only near a point — the C^k dependence extending Mathlib's Lipschitz estimate, by a time rescaling that turns the initial condition into a parameter (Lang, *Differential and Riemannian Manifolds*).
name: Smooth dependence of an ODE solution on its initial condition

about: a finite-dimensional irreducible module of highest weight λ over a split semisimple Lie algebra carries a nonzero invariant bilinear form exactly when −(w₀ • λ) = λ for the longest Weyl element w₀, the dual being irreducible of highest weight −(w₀ • λ) (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §21.6; Bourbaki, *Groupes et algèbres de Lie*, VIII §7.5).
name: The self-duality criterion for irreducible highest-weight modules

about: the absolute determinant of the Gram matrix of the Néron–Tate pairing on a basis of the points modulo torsion, independent of the chosen basis, with Reg = 1 at rank zero — completing the canonical-height strand the pairing opened; positivity awaits positive-definiteness on the real span (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VIII §9).
name: The regulator of an elliptic curve

about: the vector field (x, v) ↦ (v, −Γₓ(v, v)) on the tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold, whose integral curves are proved to be exactly the velocity lifts t ↦ (γ(t), γ′(t)) of geodesics — the object that feeds the exponential map and Hopf–Rinow, with smoothness of the spray itself the next step (do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3).
name: The geodesic spray

about: a finite group of order pᵃqᵇ, for primes p and q, is solvable, by the classical character-theoretic route: a conjugacy class of prime-power size larger than one forces a proper nontrivial normal subgroup, which spends the vanishing theorem of TauCeti#5578, and an induction on the order with a Sylow argument finishes; this closes the milestone that bullet left open (Burnside 1904; Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 3.10).
name: Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem

about: a densely defined self-adjoint operator A on a complex Hilbert space is the generator of exactly one strongly continuous unitary group e^{itA}, and an operator is self-adjoint exactly when iA generates such a group; this is the converse direction that the generator bullet of TauCeti#5185 left open, obtained by gluing the Lumer–Phillips contraction semigroups of iA and −iA into a group (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I*, Thm VIII.8; Engel–Nagel, Thm II.3.24).
name: Stone's theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators

about: in an arbitrary Coxeter system, if a reflection t shortens w then t·w is spelled by any word for w with one letter deleted, with the exchange and deletion conditions as corollaries and the inversion sequence of a reduced word listing exactly the inversions of its element; TauCeti#2823 had this for Weyl groups from the geometry of positive roots, and this is the general case by the reflection cocycle, with Matsumoto's theorem the next milestone (Björner–Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, §1.4; Humphreys §5.8).
name: The strong exchange condition for Coxeter systems

about: the polytabloids of the standard Young tableaux of shape μ form a basis of the Specht module S^μ over ℚ, so dim S^μ = f^μ, the number of standard tableaux of shape μ; linear independence is triangularity in the dominance order and spanning is the straightening algorithm through the Garnir relations (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, §8; Sagan, *The Symmetric Group*, Thm 2.5.2).
name: The standard basis theorem for Specht modules

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree, real or imaginary, the 2-rank of the narrow class group Cl⁺(K) is exactly t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes: the lower bound is the independence of the genus characters, every sign pattern of product one being realised by a degree-one prime from Dirichlet's theorem, and it closes the real case that the first-inequality bullet of TauCeti#4222 left open; the narrow ambiguous class number 2^(t−1) and |Gal(K_gen/K)| = |Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²| for the narrow genus field follow (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2; Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).
name: Gauss's 2-rank formula for quadratic fields of either signature

about: for a monic separable polynomial over a field of characteristic other than 2, the discriminant is a square in the base field exactly when the Galois group permutes the roots evenly, via σ(δ) = sign(σ)·δ for the root-difference product δ = ∏_{i<j}(rᵢ − rⱼ); in characteristic 2 every such discriminant is a square, so the test is vacuous there (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, §6.3; Dummit–Foote §14.6).
name: The discriminant test for the alternating group

about: at a place P′ over P in a finite separable extension of function fields whose residue extension is separable and whose ramification index e is prime to the residue characteristic, the different exponent is exactly e − 1; Mathlib has the divisibility P′^(e−1) ∣ 𝔇, and the new content is the non-divisibility P′^e ∤ 𝔇, proved for any extension of Dedekind domains through the trace of B/P^e being e times the residue trace (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.5.1; Serre, *Local Fields*, III §6).
name: Dedekind's different theorem, the tame case

about: over a field K of characteristic other than 2, adjoining square roots of units d₁, …, dₙ gives an extension of degree 2^r, r the 𝔽₂-rank of the subgroup of K^×/(K^×)² generated by the classes of the dᵢ, so each independent multiplicative relation among the radicands halves the degree; the exponent-two case of Kummer theory with no independence hypothesis, following Michael Stoll's QuadraticIterates formalisation (Lang, *Algebra*, VI §8).
name: The degree of a multiquadratic extension

about: h(M) = |Ĥ⁰(G, M)| / |Ĥ⁻¹(G, M)| on Mathlib's Tate cohomology, with Ĥ⁻¹(G, M) identified as ker N / I_G M, h(M) = 1 for a finite module over a finite cyclic group and h(ℤ) = |G| for the trivial integral representation; multiplicativity in short exact sequences is the next milestone (Serre, *Local Fields*, VIII §4).
name: The Herbrand quotient

about: the rational polyhedral cones of toric geometry as a predicate on a Mathlib pointed cone relative to a lattice map: generated by finitely many lattice vectors and containing no line, closed under faces, products and injective compatible linear maps, with a counterexample showing that intersections need not be toric when the lattice image is not discrete (Cox–Little–Schenck, *Toric Varieties*, §1.2; Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §1.2).
name: Toric cones

about: at a place P′ over P in a finite separable extension of function fields whose residue extension is separable and whose ramification index e is prime to the residue characteristic, the different exponent is exactly e − 1; Mathlib has the divisibility P′^(e−1) ∣ 𝔇, and the new content is the non-divisibility P′^e ∤ 𝔇, proved for any extension of Dedekind domains through the trace of B/P^e being e times the residue trace (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.5.1; Serre, *Local Fields*, III §6).
name: Dedekind's different theorem, the tame case

about: over any commutative ring R of characteristic 2, the endomorphism τ of Sp₄(R) given in coordinates by the 2×2 minors on the four form-free index pairs (the exterior-square construction Λ²R⁴ ⊃ ker φ ⧸ ⟨ω⟩, which exists only in characteristic 2) exchanges the two root lengths, τ(x_{e₀−e₁}(t)) = x_{2e₁}(t²) and τ(x_{2e₁}(t)) = x_{e₀−e₁}(t), and [squares to the Frobenius](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Symplectic/SpecialIsogeny.html#TauCeti.specialIsogeny_specialIsogeny), τ² = Frob₂; it is transported to the rank-two type-C Chevalley carrier in TauCeti#5920, and the fixed points of its odd powers, which cut out the Suzuki groups ²B₂(2^(2m+1)), are the next step (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, §12.3, §13.4; Steinberg, *Endomorphisms of Linear Algebraic Groups*, §11).
name: The special isogeny of Sp₄ in characteristic two

about: for a semisimple ring R, any presentation R ≃ ∏ᵢ Matₙᵢ(Dᵢ) has, after one permutation of its blocks, its blocks in bijection with the isomorphism classes of simple R-modules Sᵢ, with nᵢ the multiplicity of Sᵢ in the regular module (the length of its isotypic component) and Dᵢ ≃ (End_R Sᵢ)ᵒᵖ; the uniqueness clause of TauCeti#2718 compared two presentations, and this says what the surviving data are (Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, Ch. 1).
name: The intrinsic invariants of an Artin–Wedderburn presentation

about: for an arbitrary Coxeter system, u ≤ w when w is reached from u by successively multiplying by reflections that increase the length; this is a partial order with the identity as least element, invariant under inversion, and if u ≤ w then [u is spelled by a subword of every word for w](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Bruhat.html#CoxeterSystem.BruhatLE.exists_sublist_wordProd_eq), reduced or not — the necessary half of the subword property, from the strong exchange condition of TauCeti#5472; the converse, that a subword of a reduced word spells an element below w, is the next step (Björner–Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, §2.1–2.2; Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §5.9).
name: The Bruhat order on a Coxeter group

about: for independent Z ~ N(0, 1) and V ~ χ²_ν, the variable Z / √(V/ν) has Student's t law with ν degrees of freedom, at the level of measures (the pushforward of N(0, 1) ⊗ χ²_ν under (z, v) ↦ z/√(v/ν) is t_ν), by identifying the squared law with Fisher's F(1, ν) and using reflection symmetry; the density of TauCeti#5354 defined the law, and this is its classical construction (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 2, ch. 28).
name: Student's t as a Gaussian–chi-squared ratio

about: for an integral primitive element θ of a number field K (θ ∈ 𝓞_K with K = ℚ(θ)), disc(minpoly_ℤ θ) = [𝓞_K : ℤ[θ]]² · disc K; hence a prime modulo which the minimal polynomial is squarefree does not divide the index, and [a prime divides the index exactly when it divides the conductor exponent](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Index/Exponent.html#TauCeti.NumberField.IntegralPrimitiveElement.dvd_index_iff_dvd_exponent) of ℤ[θ], which is the hypothesis of Kummer–Dedekind in checkable form (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I (2.12)).
name: The index formula

about: in a finite Galois extension F′/F of function fields, the stabiliser G_Z of a place P has order e(P | F) · f(P | F), [P is the only place of F′ above its restriction](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Decomposition.html#TauCeti.Place.setOf_restrict_decompositionField_eq_eq_singleton) to the fixed field Z of G_Z, and e = f = 1 below Z, so all of the ramification and of the residue extension of P over F happen above the decomposition field; the surjection of G_Z onto the residue automorphisms with kernel the inertia group is the next step (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Def. 3.8.1, Thm 3.8.2).
name: The decomposition group and decomposition field of a place

about: for x ~ N(0, S) and a real symmetric Θ, E exp(t⟨x, Θx⟩) is finite exactly when 1 − 2t·√S Θ √S is positive definite, with no hypothesis on S, and for positive-semidefinite S equals det(1 − 2t ΘS)^(−1/2) there, the cumulant-generating function being −½ log det; this is the factor from which the Wishart moment-generating function is assembled (Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, Thm 3.2.3; Mathai–Provost, *Quadratic Forms in Random Variables*).
name: The moment-generating function of a Gaussian quadratic form

about: over any commutative ring, every skew-zigzag parameter on a forest is gauge equivalent to the constant parameter, so on a finite nontrivial tree every skew-zigzag algebra is isomorphic to the ordinary zigzag algebra; that gauge-equivalent parameters present isomorphic algebras is TauCeti#5891 (Couture, *Skew-Zigzag Algebras*, Thm 4.8, Cor. 4.13).
name: Skew-zigzag algebras on trees are ordinary

about: for a modulus 𝔪 of a number field K, a nonzero integral ideal together with a finite set of real places, the quotient of the fractional ideals prime to 𝔪 by the principal ideals (x) with x ≡ 1 mod× 𝔪 (the prescribed congruence at each prime of the finite part, positivity at the listed real places); an ideal has trivial ray class exactly when it is generated by such an x, the transition maps between moduli compose, and the trivial modulus recovers the class group; finiteness and the ray-class exact sequence are the next milestones (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §1).
name: The ray class group of a modulus

about: for a finite abelian extension L/K of number fields and a finite set S of primes outside which L/K is unramified, the homomorphism from the fractional ideals of K supported away from S to Gal(L/K) that sends each prime 𝔭 ∉ S to its Frobenius, the Artin symbol of TauCeti#5346, and is extended multiplicatively; it is determined by those values and is compatible with enlarging S and with restriction to intermediate fields; its kernel, and reciprocity, are the next milestones (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §7).
name: The Artin map on ideals

about: graphons on a fixed probability space modulo cut distance zero, in particular modulo measure-preserving rearrangement, made a genuine metric space by the cut metric δ_□, on which every homomorphism density t(F, ·) descends and is [Lipschitz with constant the number of edges of F](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Combinatorics/DenseGraphLimits/GraphonSpace/HomDensity.html#TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.lipschitzWith_homDensityOnSpace), hence continuous; density of step graphons and compactness are the next steps (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, §8.2; Janson, *Graphons, cut norm and distance, couplings and rearrangements*, §6).
name: The metric space of graphons

about: for x ~ N(0, S) and a real symmetric Θ, E exp(t⟨x, Θx⟩) is finite exactly when 1 − 2t·√S Θ √S is positive definite, with no hypothesis on S, and for positive-semidefinite S equals det(1 − 2t ΘS)^(−1/2) there, the cumulant-generating function being −½ log det; this is the factor from which the Wishart moment-generating function is assembled (Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, Thm 3.2.3; Mathai–Provost, *Quadratic Forms in Random Variables*).
name: The moment-generating function of a Gaussian quadratic form

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree, and K_gen the compositum of the quadratic fields of the prime discriminants dividing disc K, Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)², and ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)² for d < 0, via [the principal genus theorem](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/PrincipalGenus.html#TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isSquare_iff_forall_genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom_eq_one): a narrow ideal class is a square exactly when every genus character is trivial on it; the summit of the 2-rank formula of TauCeti#5899, with the identification of the isomorphism with the inverse Artin map not yet proved (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Thm 3.15, §6.A).
name: The genus field of a quadratic field has Galois group Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²

about: for X path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected, π₁(X, x₀) is the automorphism group of the functor sending a covering space of X, finite or not, to its fibre over x₀, a loop class acting by monodromy; the input is a [reconstruction of a monoid from its G-sets](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Action/Tannaka.html#TauCeti.endForgetActionMulEquiv) as the endomorphisms of the forgetful functor (Lenstra, *Galois theory for schemes*, §3; Szamuely, *Galois Groups and Fundamental Groups*, Ch. 2).
name: The fundamental group is the automorphism group of the fibre functor

about: a path-connected, locally path-connected space admits a simply connected covering space if and only if it is semilocally simply connected; the construction was in place, adapted from Kim Morrison's open mathlib4#38292, and the new half is necessity, via a local section of any local homeomorphism whose source has only null-homotopic loops (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, after Prop. 1.36).
name: A universal cover exists exactly when the base is semilocally simply connected

about: an irreducible unitary representation of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex space has ν₂ = −1 exactly when it carries a conjugate-linear J commuting with the action with J² = −1, completing the structure-map reading of the trichotomy of TauCeti#4313, where ν₂ = 1 is a real structure, equivalently realizability over ℝ (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II §6).
name: Frobenius–Schur indicator −1 means a quaternionic structure

about: the determinant of Burau(b) − 1 with its last row and column deleted is unchanged by conjugation and multiplied by a unit under the two Markov stabilizations, so Markov-equivalent braids have the same value up to a unit of ℤ[T, T⁻¹]; on σ₀³, the trefoil braid, it is associated to the T − 1 + T⁻¹ of the Seifert-matrix route of TauCeti#3948, and at t = −1 it separates the trefoil braid from the trivial one; Markov's theorem itself is not formalized (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*, Thm 3.11).
name: The Alexander polynomial of a braid closure from the Burau representation

about: for G finite cyclic with generator g and any representation M over a commutative ring, every even Tate degree is the homology of M →N→ M →ρ(g)−1→ M and every odd degree that of the same maps in the other order, in all of ℤ including Ĥ⁰ and Ĥ⁻¹, so Ĥ^m(G, M) ≅ Ĥ^n(G, M) whenever m ≡ n mod 2; read off Mathlib's Tate groups, and the periodicity behind the Herbrand quotient of TauCeti#5764 (Serre, *Local Fields*, VIII §4).
name: Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group is two-periodic

about: every continuous character of ℝ/Tℤ is a Fourier monomial x ↦ e^(2πinx/T) for a unique integer n, with modulus one falling out rather than assumed, so n ↦ fourier n is an isomorphism ℤ ≅ PontryaginDual(ℝ/Tℤ); the exhaustion half of the circle's Peter–Weyl worked example (Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Ch. 1).
name: The Pontryagin dual of the circle is ℤ

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, an additive Haar measure on a finite-dimensional real normed space and Banach-space-valued f ∈ Lᵖ, averaging against a normalized smooth bump, as a Bochner integral in Lᵖ itself, is a contraction of Lᵖ and converges strongly to f as the radii of the bumps tend to zero; the Lᵖ input for Meyers–Serrin (Brezis, *Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDE*, Prop. 4.21).
name: Mollification converges in Lᵖ

about: for independent X, Y ~ N(0, 1), X/Y has the standard Cauchy law, at the level of measures the pushforward of N(0, 1) ⊗ N(0, 1) under (x, y) ↦ x/y, through Student's t with one degree of freedom from TauCeti#5935 (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 1).
name: The ratio of two independent standard Gaussians is Cauchy

about: over every field, in every rank and every characteristic, Sp₂ₘ is smooth and geometrically connected with no nontrivial connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup over an algebraic closure, because its standard representation is faithful and simple; the symplectic companion of GLₙ in TauCeti#4394 (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §§19.b, 24.6).
name: The symplectic group is reductive

about: for a function field F/k with k finite and R any Dedekind k-subalgebra of F with fraction field F, ClassGroup R is finite, with no separability hypothesis and no chosen rational subfield, since R has a place at infinity whose class dies in ClassGroup R and Cl⁰(F) is finite; with a rational place at infinity the class number of R divides h_F; Mathlib has the integral closure of 𝔽_q[X] under separability, by a Minkowski-style route (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Prop. 5.1.3).
name: The ideal class group of an affine model of a function field is finite

about: a jointly exchangeable array X_{ij} is dissociated, blocks over disjoint index sets being independent, exactly when the corner tail ⋂ₙ σ(X_{ij} : i, j ≥ n) is trivial; the zero-one law was known and the converse is new and representation-free, separating the ergodic form of the Aldous–Hoover representation from the general one (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).
name: Joint dissociation is corner-tail triviality

about: the integer table χ^μ(ν) of Specht character values on cycle types is the complex character table of Sₙ, rows reindexed by the classification of TauCeti#5649, so over ℤ the columns satisfy Σ_μ χ^μ(ν)χ^μ(ν′) = z_ν δ_{νν′}, the rows Σ_ν χ^μ(ν)χ^{μ′}(ν)/z_ν = δ_{μμ′}, and Σ_{μ ⊢ n} (dim S^μ)² = n!; the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule is the next step (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, Ch. 6).
name: The character table of Sₙ and its orthogonality relations

about: for an algebraic function field F/k with exact constant field k there is a divisor W with ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g + ℓ(W − D) for every divisor D, namely the divisor (ω) of any nonzero Weil differential, with the [duality L(W − D) ≃ Ω_F(D)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/CanonicalDivisor.html#TauCeti.riemannRochSpaceEquivWeilDifferentialFiltration), x ↦ xω, giving ℓ(W − D) = i(D); so the canonical class is well defined, of degree 2g − 2 with ℓ(W) = g, and [a divisor is canonical exactly when](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/CanonicalDivisor.html#TauCeti.divisorClass_eq_canonicalClass_iff) deg D = 2g − 2 and ℓ(D) ≥ g; the summit above Riemann's theorem of TauCeti#4463 (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.5.15, Prop. 1.6.2).
name: The Riemann–Roch theorem

about: for a Dirichlet series L(s) = Σ f(n) n^(−s) converging absolutely on Re s = c > 0 and an integer N ≥ 1, (2πi)⁻¹ ∫_(c−iT)^(c+iT) L(s) N^s s⁻¹ ds → Σ_(n<N) f(n) + f(N)/2 as T → ∞, the endpoint entering with half weight, and [for non-integer x](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Perron/Formula.html#TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_sub_sum_le) the truncated integral differs from Σ_(n<x) f(n) by at most Σ |f(n)| (x/n)^c / (πT |log(x/n)|), the truncated Perron formula with its explicit error term (Davenport, *Multiplicative Number Theory*, Ch. 17).
name: Perron's formula

about: for X path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected, π̂₁(X, x₀) is isomorphic as a topological group to the automorphism group of the fibre functor on finite covering spaces of X, acting on each fibre by the unique continuous extension of monodromy; the finite-cover counterpart of TauCeti#6023, via Mathlib's Galois-category recognition theorem and the fact that [the profinite completion of any group](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Action/ProfiniteCompletion.html#TauCeti.ProfiniteCompletion.instIsFundamentalGroup) is the fundamental group of its finite G-sets (Szamuely, *Galois Groups and Fundamental Groups*, Ch. 2).
name: The profinite completion of π₁ is the automorphism group of the finite-cover fibre functor

about: over a field K with 2 ≠ 0, the Spin group of a split three-dimensional quadratic space, a hyperbolic plane plus a line, is isomorphic to SL₂(K), the even Clifford algebra being M₂(K) with Clifford reversal as the adjugate, and under this isomorphism the spin representation is the standard two-dimensional representation of SL₂; [over a separably closed field](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Spin/Exceptional/Three/Group.html#TauCeti.nonempty_spinGroup_mulEquiv_specialLinearGroup_of_finrank_eq_three) every nondegenerate ternary form qualifies (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Lecture 20).
name: Spin₃ ≅ SL₂

about: for X ~ N(m, S) on ℝ^(ι⊔κ) with S positive semidefinite and the observed block S₂₂ positive definite, the regular conditional distribution of X₁ given X₂ = x₂ is N(m₁ + S₁₂S₂₂⁻¹(x₂ − m₂), S₁₁ − S₁₂S₂₂⁻¹S₂₁), its covariance the Schur complement, as an identity of Markov kernels with Mathlib's condDistrib for almost every x₂; proved by splitting X₁ into its regression on X₂ and an independent Gaussian residual (Anderson, *An Introduction to Multivariate Statistical Analysis*, §2.5).
name: The conditional law of a multivariate Gaussian

about: for every modulus 𝔪 of a number field K, an integral ideal 𝔪₀ together with a set of real places, Cl_𝔪(K) is finite, and [the units congruent to 1 mod× 𝔪 have finite index](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Finite.html#TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.unitsCongruenceSubgroup_finiteIndex) in 𝓞_Kˣ; the proof follows the ray class exact sequence, the map to Cl(K) having finite image and kernel the principal ideals prime to 𝔪, in which the ray has finite index by reduction to (𝓞_K/𝔪₀)ˣ; the group was TauCeti#5842 (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §1).
name: The ray class group of a modulus is finite

about: in a finite Galois extension F′/F of function fields, the decomposition group G_Z(P) of a place P of F′ acts on the residue field F′_P over that of P ∩ F, the action is onto and its kernel is the inertia group G_T(P), so [G_Z/G_T ≅ Aut(F′_P / F_(P∩F))](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Inertia.html#TauCeti.Place.decompositionQuotientInertiaEquiv), of order the separable residue degree, and [|G_T| = e(P | P ∩ F)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Inertia.html#TauCeti.Place.card_inertiaSubgroup) when the residue extension is separable; the second half of the theorem whose first half, |G_Z| = e·f and the decomposition field, was TauCeti#5871 (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.8.2).
name: The inertia group of a place

about: for a C² function f on an open subset U of a finite-dimensional real normed space and almost every linear functional a, for Haar measure on the dual, every critical point of f − a in U is nondegenerate, because f − a has a degenerate critical point exactly when a is a critical value of df, a map between spaces of the same dimension to which the equal-dimensional Sard theorem applies; so Morse perturbations are [dense](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Calculus/Morse/Generic.html#TauCeti.dense_setOfPred_hasNondegenerateCriticalPointsOn_sub) and can be taken arbitrarily small (Guillemin–Pollack, *Differential Topology*, Ch. 1 §7).
name: Morse functions are generic

about: for a Weierstrass curve over the valuation ring 𝒪_v of the completion K_v of the fraction field of a Dedekind domain at a height-one prime, the parametrisation t ↦ (t/w(t), −1/w(t)) is an [injective homomorphism](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Point/Hom.html#WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHom_injective) from the formal group Ê(𝔪_v) on the maximal ideal to E(K_v) whose image is the point at infinity together with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole, so Ê(𝔪_v) ≅ E₁(K_v); the image is described through the valuation of x since no reduction map on points exists yet (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VII.2.2).
name: The formal group of an elliptic curve is E₁(K_v)

about: on a Noetherian integral scheme all of whose points have codimension at most one and whose codimension-one local rings are discrete valuation rings, [every Weil divisor is locally principal](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/Scheme/LocallyPrincipal.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.locallyPrincipalSubgroup_eq_top), and taking the orders of local equations at codimension-one points is an isomorphism of groups from Cartier divisors to Weil divisors, inverse to gluing the local equations of a Weil divisor (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6.11; Stacks Project, Tag 0BE9).
name: Weil divisors are Cartier divisors on a curve

about: for X ~ N(m, S) on ℝ^(ι⊔κ) with S positive semidefinite and the observed block S₂₂ positive definite, the regular conditional distribution of X₁ given X₂ = x₂ is N(m₁ + S₁₂S₂₂⁻¹(x₂ − m₂), S₁₁ − S₁₂S₂₂⁻¹S₂₁), its covariance the Schur complement, as an identity of Markov kernels with Mathlib's condDistrib for almost every x₂; proved by splitting X₁ into its regression on X₂ and an independent Gaussian residual (Anderson, *An Introduction to Multivariate Statistical Analysis*, §2.5).
name: The conditional law of a multivariate Gaussian

about: a function continuous on a closed ball of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, C² with Δu ≥ 0 inside, and differentiable at a boundary point where it attains a strict maximum over the closed ball has strictly positive outward derivative there; proved in every dimension by the classical radial barrier (Evans, *PDE*, §6.4.2; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Lemma 3.4).
name: Hopf's boundary-point lemma

about: every positive-definite real symmetric matrix A factors as A = L Lᵀ with L lower triangular and positive on the diagonal, built from Mathlib's LDL decomposition; uniqueness of L is the next step (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §7.2).
name: The Cholesky decomposition

about: a Markov exchangeable process on a countable state space (law invariant under permutations of finite paths preserving initial state and transition counts) that is recurrent and almost surely visits every state is a mixture of Markov chains, because its successor array is row exchangeable; the case of a process missing a state stays open (Diaconis–Freedman, "de Finetti's theorem for Markov chains", Ann. Probab. 8 (1980)).
name: The Diaconis–Freedman representation

about: for nonzero rationals d₁, …, dₙ, ℚ(√d₁, …, √dₙ) ⊆ ℚ(ζ_N) with N = 4∏ᵢ|num dᵢ · den dᵢ|, hence every finite Galois extension of ℚ of exponent dividing 2 embeds in a cyclotomic field; the engine is the quadratic Gauss sum, which places [√p* in ℚ(ζ_p)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Cyclotomic/GaussSum.html#TauCeti.Multiquadratic.exists_mem_sq_eq_oddPrimeDiscriminant) for p* = (−1)^((p−1)/2) p — the multiquadratic case of the Kronecker–Weber theorem, the general theorem untouched (Ireland–Rosen, Ch. 6).
name: Every multiquadratic field lies in a cyclotomic field

about: any two Sylow pro-p subgroups (closed pro-p subgroups of index prime to p in every finite quotient) are conjugate, so a normal one is unique; with [Lagrange's theorem for profinite groups](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Lagrange.html#Subgroup.profiniteOrder_eq_mul_profiniteIndex), |G| = |H|·[G : H] as supernatural numbers for closed H, and multiplicativity of the index in a tower; existence of Sylow pro-p subgroups is a separate open PR (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.3).
name: Sylow pro-p subgroups of a profinite group are conjugate

about: the degree-one coderivation b of the reduced tensor coalgebra built from suspended operations mₙ satisfies b ∘ b = 0 exactly when all the Stasheff identities Σ ± m_{r+1+t}(1^r ⊗ m_s ⊗ 1^t) = 0 hold, arity 1–4 written out with the Getzler–Jones/Keller signs; A∞-algebras are the next definition (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras*, §3.6).
name: The Stasheff identities are the square-zero condition on the bar construction

about: for K quadratic with t ramified rational primes, the ordinary class group Cl(K) has 2-rank t − 1 or t − 2, both occurring (ℚ(√10), ℚ(√3)): the narrow formula 2-rank Cl⁺(K) = t − 1 of TauCeti#5899 drops by at most one because the kernel of Cl⁺(K) → Cl(K) has at most two elements; and the isomorphism Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)² of TauCeti#6073 is now identified with [the inverse of the Artin map](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/CandidateGenusField/Relative/Artin.html#TauCeti.Multiquadratic.autCandidateGenusFieldEquivNarrowElementaryTwoQuotient_artinHomAway) on ideals prime to 2·disc K (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).
name: The 2-rank of the class group of a quadratic field is t − 1 or t − 2

about: complete Bernstein functions g(t) = a + bt + ∫₀^∞ t/(t + x) dμ(x) are Bernstein, and f is a Stieltjes function iff t ↦ t f(t) extends to a complete Bernstein function (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thms 6.2, 7.3; Pick-function form not formalised); and [f is a Bernstein function iff f ≥ 0 and every e^(−xf), x > 0, is completely monotone on (0, ∞) and continuous at 0](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/CompletelyMonotone/Bernstein/Exponential.html#TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_iff_nonneg_and_forall_isContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi_exp_neg_mul), the Laplace-exponent characterisation (Thm 3.7).
name: Complete Bernstein functions, and Bernstein functions through their exponentials

about: an isogeny φ : E₁ → E₂ of elliptic curves is separable iff φ*ω₂ ≠ 0, ω the invariant differential (Silverman II.4.2(c)); the pullback of ω is additive, (f + g)*ω = f*ω + g*ω (III.5.2), now that Hom(E₁, E₂) is an abelian group, so over a finite field [1 − π is separable](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/OneSubFrobenius/Separable.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.isSeparable_oneSubFrobeniusIsogeny) since Frobenius kills ω (III.5.5), the step by which #E(𝔽_q) becomes deg(1 − π) on the way to the Hasse bound, not yet proved.
name: The differential criterion for separability of an isogeny

about: the least number of transpositions whose product is a permutation σ of an n-element set is n minus the number of orbits of σ, fixed points counted, as multiplying by a transposition merges two orbits or splits one (Dénes, 1959).
name: The reflection length of a permutation

about: for a place P of a function-field extension F'/F, G_i(P) = {σ ∈ G_Z(P) : ord_P(σz − z) ≥ i + 1 for all z ∈ 𝒪_P} in lower numbering: G₀ is the inertia group, the G_i decrease, are normal in G_Z and meet in 1, G_{i+1}/G_{i+2} is elementary abelian in characteristic p, and [G₁ = 1 in characteristic zero](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/RamificationGroup.html#TauCeti.Place.ramificationGroup_one_eq_bot); Mathlib stops at the inertia group; G₀/G₁ cyclic of order prime to p and Hilbert's different formula are the next rungs (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, 3.8.4–3.8.5).
name: Higher ramification groups of a place

about: a finite family of toric cones closed under faces with pairwise intersections a face of each, with support, completeness, subfans, the fan of a single cone, and morphisms of fans determined by their lattice map; the zero cone lies in every nonempty fan, and gluing a toric variety from a fan is a later target (Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §1.4).
name: Fans of toric cones

about: Miyake's primitive form: a cusp form of level Γ₁(N), weight k and nebentypus χ, eigen for the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring at every index coprime to N, in the new subspace and normalised by a₁ = 1; multiplicity one and the eigenvalues at bad indices are the Atkin–Lehner theorems still to come (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, §4.6).
name: Newforms

about: the bounded continuous globally α-Hölder functions X → E with norm ‖f‖_∞ + [f]_α form a Banach space when E is; the zeroth member of the C^{k,α} scale for the Schauder estimates (Gilbarg–Trudinger, §4.1).
name: Hölder spaces

about: for an exact divisor Q ∥ N, the integral matrices [Qa, b; Nc, Qd] of determinant Q normalize Γ₀(N) and any two differ by an element of Γ₀(N), so slashing by one is a well-defined operator W_Q on M_k(Γ₀(N)) and S_k(Γ₀(N)), with W₁ = 1, W_N the Fricke operator and [W_Q² = Q^{k−2}](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/AtkinLehner/Operator.html#TauCeti.Nat.IsExactDivisor.atkinLehnerOperator_atkinLehnerOperator) in un-normalized form; the normalized involution and the newform eigenvalues ±1 are still to come (Atkin–Lehner, *Math. Ann.* 185 (1970); Diamond–Shurman §5).
name: Atkin–Lehner operators W_Q

about: every profinite group has a Sylow pro-p subgroup, a closed pro-p subgroup whose image in each finite quotient is a Sylow p-subgroup, built as the inverse limit of the finite Sylow subgroups; [every pro-p subgroup lies in a conjugate of any given Sylow pro-p subgroup](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Sylow/Containment.html#TauCeti.IsProP.exists_le_isProPSylow), and [the Sylow pro-p subgroups are exactly the maximal pro-p subgroups](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Sylow/Containment.html#TauCeti.isProPSylow_iff_isProP_and_maximal); with the conjugacy of TauCeti#6278 this completes the Sylow theory of profinite groups (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.3).
name: The Sylow theorems for profinite groups

about: over every field of characteristic ≠ 2 and for every n, the special orthogonal group scheme of the standard symmetric form is [geometrically connected](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/Connected.html#TauCeti.SpecialOrthogonal.geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty_coordinateHopfAlgebra) and reductive, connectedness coming from Cartan–Dieudonné, which writes a rotation as a product of pairs of reflections, each pair joined to the identity along an explicit Laurent-polynomial path; SOₙ joins GLₙ, SLₙ, Sp₂ₙ and the tori among the library's reductive groups (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §§18.c, 21).
name: SOₙ is connected and reductive

about: a jointly exchangeable array is jointly dissociated, its blocks on disjoint index sets independent, exactly when the diagonal action of the finitary permutations of ℕ, relabelling both coordinates at once, is ergodic for its law; this closes the triangle dissociation ↔ corner-tail triviality ↔ ergodicity, and is not the Aldous–Hoover representation itself (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).
name: Joint dissociation is ergodicity of diagonal relabelling

about: for n ≥ 2 the compact real Spin group is path-connected, since −1 and every product of two unit-vector reflections lie in the identity component; and over any field with 2 invertible [Spin(Q) is a double cover of the kernel of the spinor norm](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/SpinorNorm/DoubleCover.html#CliffordAlgebra.spinDoubleCoverSpinorNormKernel), packaged as the extension 1 → ℤ/2 → Spin(Q) → ker θ → 1 inside SO(Q); simple connectivity of Spin(n) for n ≥ 3 is the next step (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).
name: Spin(n) is path-connected

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, W^{1,p}_0(ℝⁿ) = W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ): every whole-space Sobolev function is a Sobolev-norm limit of smooth compactly supported functions, by mollification and cut-off; Mathlib has the density in Lᵖ, and the Meyers–Serrin theorem on a domain is the next milestone (Evans, *PDE*, §5.3.1; Brezis, §9.1).
name: Test functions are dense in W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ)

about: a homotopy equivalence e : X ≃ Y induces isomorphisms πₙ(X, x) ≅ πₙ(Y, e(x)) in every dimension, via the trace formula that freely homotopic maps induce the same map up to base-point change along the trace of the homotopy; hence [asphericity and the K(G, 1) property are homotopy invariants](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/EilenbergMacLane/HomotopyEquiv.html#TauCeti.IsEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne.of_homotopyEquiv). Mathlib has the fundamental-groupoid case; the higher πₙ are new (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §4.1).
name: Homotopy groups are homotopy invariants

about: for a finite quiver with positive definite Tits form q, the nonnegative integer vectors with q(d) = 1 are exactly the images of the standard basis vectors under finite sequences of simple reflections; the root-lattice input to the reflection-functor proof of Gabriel's theorem, which is not itself claimed (Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev; Assem–Simson–Skowroński, VII.5).
name: Every positive root is a Weyl reflection of a simple root

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d > 0, the narrow class number equals the class number exactly when 𝓞_K has a unit of norm −1, that is, when the negative Pell equation is solvable, and for every quadratic field [h⁺ ≤ 2h](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Quadratic/Conjugation/NarrowClassGroup.html#NumberField.card_narrowClassGroup_le_two_mul_card_classGroup); with the narrow 2-rank formula of TauCeti#5899 this decides when the ordinary class group has 2-rank t − 1 (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).
name: h⁺ = h for a real quadratic field iff a unit has norm −1

about: in a preadditive balanced category, two almost-split sequences whose left ends have local endomorphism rings and whose right ends are isomorphic are isomorphic as short complexes, and [any morphism between them that is invertible at the right end is invertible](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/AlmostSplit/Uniqueness.html#CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.IsAlmostSplit.isIso_of_isIso_τ₃); the uniqueness half of the Auslander–Reiten theorem, existence still open (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, Ch. V; Assem–Simson–Skowroński, IV.1).
name: Uniqueness of almost-split sequences

about: two newforms of level N, weight k and the same nebentypus whose Hecke eigenvalues (equivalently, q-expansion coefficients) agree at every index coprime to N outside a finite set are equal, nothing being assumed at the primes dividing the level; the engine is the [Atkin–Lehner Main Lemma at fixed nebentypus](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/MainLemma.html#TauCeti.mem_cuspFormsOld_of_forall_coprime_qExpansion_coeff_eq_zero), that a cusp form in S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) whose q-expansion vanishes at every index coprime to N is old, indeed Σ_{p∣N} V_p f_p with f_p of level N/p; the Main Lemma without a fixed character is not claimed (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Thm 4.6.12 and Lemma 4.6.8; Diamond–Shurman §5.7 and Thm 5.8.2).
name: Strong multiplicity one for newforms

about: over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, if q ⊥ q₁ ≅ q ⊥ q₂ with q regular and finite-dimensional then q₁ ≅ q₂, proved through hyperplane reflections; so the isometry classes of regular forms are cancellative under ⊥, the input the Witt ring needs (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, I.4.2).
name: Witt's cancellation theorem

about: a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over K becomes a matrix algebra over a finite subextension of the separable closure, by descending a matrix presentation over K^sep to the field its matrix units generate; with the separably closed case of TauCeti#4501 this closes the splitting-field milestone (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*, §2.2).
name: Every central simple algebra has a finite separable splitting field

about: π₁(X, x) acts on πₙ(X, x) by group automorphisms for n ≥ 1 (the π₁-module structure on πₙ for n ≥ 2, conjugation for n = 1), and [two classes lie in the same orbit exactly when they are freely homotopic](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/FundamentalGroupAction.html#TauCeti.homotopyGroup_mem_orbit_iff_exists_homotopyAlong), so the orbit set is the set of free homotopy classes of maps Sⁿ → X into the component of x and the action is trivial on a simply connected space (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §4.1).
name: The action of π₁ on the higher homotopy groups

about: over an infinite field in which d! ≠ 0, the images of the group algebras k[GLₙ] and k[S_d] in End((kⁿ)^{⊗d}) are each other's centralizers; the duality announced with TauCeti#5127 had the span of all diagonal operators f^{⊗d} in place of the image of k[GLₙ], now identified by the Zariski density of GLₙ, completing the classical statement (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 6; Procesi, *Lie Groups*, Ch. 9).
name: Schur–Weyl duality for the image of k[GLₙ]

about: for a finite separable extension of Dedekind domains A ⊆ B, with the relative discriminant ideal 𝔡_{B/A} defined as the norm of the different, a nonzero prime of A divides 𝔡_{B/A} exactly when some prime above it ramifies, [for number fields exactly when a prime above it has ramification index > 1](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Ramification.html#TauCeti.NumberField.dvd_relDiscr_iff_exists_one_lt_ramificationIdx), together with the tower formula and 𝔡_{𝓞_K/ℤ} = (disc K); Mathlib has the criterion for the absolute discriminant over ℤ, this is the relative one (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, III.2.10 and III.2.12).
name: Dedekind's discriminant theorem, relative form

about: for K = ℚ(√d), d > 0, with t ramified primes, the 2-rank of Cl(K) is t − 1 exactly when every prime discriminant dividing disc K is positive, that is, when no prime ≡ 3 (mod 4) divides d, and is t − 2 otherwise, by evaluating the genus characters on the narrow class of (√d), χ_P([√d]⁺) = sign P; this settles the t − 1 or t − 2 dichotomy of TauCeti#6270, extending the norm −1 criterion of TauCeti#6275 (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2; Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).
name: The 2-rank of the class group of a real quadratic field

about: every discrete subgroup of PSL(2, ℝ) acts properly discontinuously on the upper half-plane, descended from Mathlib's proper SL(2, ℝ) action; and in general [the free locus of a properly discontinuous action on a locally compact Hausdorff space is open and its orbit projection is a covering map](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/GroupAction/FreeLocus.html#TauCeti.isCoveringMap_quotientMk_freeLocus) (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, Ch. 2).
name: Fuchsian groups act properly discontinuously

about: for an elliptic curve over 𝔽_q the isogeny 1 − π_q, with π_q the q-power Frobenius, has degree the number of rational points, the first input of the Hasse bound; alongside it, multiplication by n [has kernel the rational n-torsion](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/MulByInt/Kernel.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.mem_ker_mulByIntIsogeny_iff), equals n·id in End(E), [is separable exactly when n ≠ 0 in the base field](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/MulByInt/Hom.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.isSeparable_mulByIntIsogeny_iff), and the degree satisfies deg(n·φ) = n²·deg φ; the order #E[n] = n² is the next step (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.4–III.6, V.1.1).
name: deg(1 − π_q) = #E(𝔽_q)

about: the normalization promised with yesterday's W_Q: 𝒲_Q = (√Q)^{2−k}·W_Q is an involution of M_k(Γ₀(N)) and of S_k(Γ₀(N)) at every weight, and [𝒲_Q ∘ 𝒲_R = 𝒲_{QR/gcd(Q,R)²}](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/AtkinLehner/Normalized.html#TauCeti.Nat.IsExactDivisor.normalizedAtkinLehnerOperator_normalizedAtkinLehnerOperator), so the exact divisors of N, a Boolean group ≅ (ℤ/2)^{ω(N)}, act through commuting involutions; the eigenvalues ε_Q on newforms wait on the newform theory (Atkin–Lehner, *Math. Ann.* 185 (1970)).
name: The normalized Atkin–Lehner involutions 𝒲_Q

about: nonunital, uncurved A∞-algebras on a ℤ-graded module: operations m_n of degree 2 − n packaged as a square-zero degree-one coderivation of the reduced tensor coalgebra, with the equivalence to the unsuspended Stasheff identities and a constructor from them (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §3).
name: A∞-algebras

about: the law W_p(ν, S) of Σ_r X_r X_rᵀ for ν independent centred Gaussian vectors of covariance S, defined for every degree and scale matrix so that the singular laws are included: degrees add under convolution, the law is carried by the positive semidefinite cone with rank ≤ min(ν, rank S), and below that rank threshold it is singular to Lebesgue measure on symmetric matrices (Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, Ch. 3).
name: The Wishart distribution

about: the law W_p(ν, S) of Σ_r X_r X_rᵀ for ν independent centred Gaussian vectors of covariance S, defined for every degree and scale matrix so that the singular laws are included: degrees add under convolution, the law is carried by the positive semidefinite cone with rank ≤ min(ν, rank S), and below that rank threshold it is singular to Lebesgue measure on symmetric matrices (Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, Ch. 3).
name: The Wishart distribution

about: over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, every regular quadratic form on a finite-dimensional space is isometric to m hyperbolic planes ⊥ an anisotropic form, and [m and the anisotropic summand are determined by the isometry class](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Witt/Decomposition.html#TauCeti.eq_of_nsmul_hyperbolicClass_add_eq), defining the Witt index and the anisotropic part, with rank q = 2·(Witt index) + rank(anisotropic part); the degenerate case and the maximal-totally-isotropic description of the index are still to come (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, I.4.1).
name: Witt decomposition

about: at a rational place P of a function field of genus g > 0 with integrally closed constants, exactly g positive integers are gaps, that is, are the pole order at P of no function regular elsewhere; 1 is a gap and every gap is at most 2g − 1, by counting the jumps of ℓ(nP) (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.6.8).
name: The Weierstrass gap theorem

about: if a measurable function f of finitely many i.i.d. coordinates changes by at most cᵢ when only the i-th coordinate changes, then f − 𝔼f is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy Σ cᵢ²/4, whence ℙ(f − 𝔼f ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/Σ cᵢ²) through Mathlib's sub-Gaussian API; the concentration engine for the sampling convergence of graphons (McDiarmid, *On the method of bounded differences*, 1989).
name: McDiarmid's bounded-differences inequality

about: for subgroups H, K of an arbitrary group G and a representation A of H over any commutative ring, Res_K Ind_H^G A ≅ ⨁_{KsH ∈ K\G/H} Ind_{K ∩ sHs⁻¹}^K Res(ˢA), naturally in A; the character form of TauCeti#2087 needed a finite group and gave an equality of characters, this is the isomorphism itself with no finiteness assumed (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §7.3).
name: The Mackey decomposition as an isomorphism of representations

about: over an algebraically closed field in which n is invertible, the kernel of multiplication by n on a Weierstrass curve has exactly n² points, the step flagged yesterday, from [n] having separable degree n² and the converse that a nonsingular point where the division polynomial ψₙ vanishes is killed by n; and for an affine Weierstrass curve with Dedekind coordinate ring [the point group is the degree-zero divisor class group of the function field](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/FunctionField/DivisorClass.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.pointEquivDegreeZeroDivisorClass), P ↦ [(P) − (O)], the input the divisor construction of the Weil pairing consumes (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3.4, III.6.4).
name: E[n] has n² points, and E(F) ≅ Cl⁰(F(E))

about: over any field of characteristic ≠ 2, every isometry of an n-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic space is a product of at most n reflections, a determinant-one isometry of an even number of them; the generation form of TauCeti#2492 carried no bound, and Mathlib has the bound for real inner-product spaces only; hence [Spin(n) is compact](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/Compact.html#CliffordAlgebra.instCompactSpaceRealCliffordSpinGroupZero), a continuous image of a fixed finite product of unit spheres (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).
name: Cartan–Dieudonné with the sharp bound, and Spin(n) is compact

about: homotopy rel boundary of generalized loops is path-connectedness in the compact-open loop space, so πₙ(X, x) is the set of path components of ΩⁿX and the cubical currying Ω^M(Ω^N X) ≃ Ω^{M⊔N} X descends to [group isomorphisms π_M(Ω^N X) ≅ π_{M⊔N}(X)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/LoopSpace.html#HomotopyGroup.loopSpaceMulEquiv), in particular πₘ₊₁(ΩX) ≅ πₘ₊₂(X) and π₀(ΩX) ≅ π₁(X); Mathlib has the homeomorphism of loop spaces but not its effect on homotopy groups (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §4.1).
name: The loop-space shift πₙ₊₁(ΩX) ≅ πₙ₊₂(X)

about: for a finite Galois extension L/k and a lattice M with any action of Gal(L/k), the invariants of L[M] under the simultaneous action on coefficients and exponents are the coordinate ring of a torus over k split by L, in any characteristic, and [its characters over L recover M with its Galois action](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GroupAlgebra/Galois/Character.html#TauCeti.GaloisDescent.groupAlgebraInvariantsCharacterEquiv); the existence half of the anti-equivalence between tori split by L and Gal(L/k)-lattices, whose inverse is still to come (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.23).
name: Galois descent produces a torus

about: for an irreducible separable p over F with a root α, the Galois group is 2-transitive on the roots exactly when p/(X − α) stays irreducible over F(α), and since [the blocks containing α correspond, order-reversingly, to the intermediate fields of F(α)/F](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/Blocks.html#TauCeti.rootBlockIntermediateFieldOrderIso), the action is primitive exactly when F(α)/F has no proper intermediate field, as in prime degree (Wielandt, *Finite Permutation Groups*, Thm 7.5).
name: Primitivity and 2-transitivity of polynomial Galois groups

about: Dir(a) on the standard simplex, the law of independent Gamma(aᵢ) variables divided by their sum; [the total of any block s of coordinates is Beta(Σ_s aᵢ, Σ_{sᶜ} aᵢ)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Dirichlet/Marginal.html#TauCeti.Probability.map_sum_dirichletMeasure), merging coordinates along a surjection gives the Dirichlet law with summed parameters, and the mean aᵢ/a₀ and covariance −aᵢaⱼ/(a₀²(a₀ + 1)) are computed; the density on the simplex is next (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Multivariate Distributions*, ch. 49).
name: The Dirichlet distribution

about: Γ_p(a) = π^{p(p−1)/4} ∏_{i<p} Γ(a − i/2), with Γ_{p+q}(a) = π^{pq/2} Γ_p(a) Γ_q(a − p/2), Γ₁ = Γ, positivity for a > (p − 1)/2 and the exact vanishing locus outside it; the cone integral ∫_{A>0} det(A)^{a−(p+1)/2} e^{−tr A} dA = Γ_p(a) that makes it the Wishart normalizing constant is proved in dimension 0 only so far (Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, §2.1).
name: The multivariate Gamma function

about: on an open preconnected set U in a finite-dimensional real inner product space, a C² function with Δu ≥ 0 that attains its maximum over U at a point of U is constant on U, proved through Hopf's boundary-point lemma (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 3.5), together with the strong minimum and comparison principles and their versions for functions continuous up to the boundary; this extends the planar harmonic case of TauCeti#1724 to subharmonic functions in every dimension.
name: The strong maximum principle for subharmonic functions

about: over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, an isometry between two subspaces of a finite-dimensional quadratic space on which the form is nondegenerate extends to an isometry of the whole space, with no nondegeneracy assumed of the ambient form (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, I.4.9); it joins the cancellation and decomposition theorems of TauCeti#6439 and TauCeti#6544.
name: Witt's extension theorem

about: for a modulus 𝔪 of a number field K, h_𝔪 · [𝓞_Kˣ : U_𝔪] = h · #(𝓞_K/𝔪₀)ˣ · 2^#𝔪_∞, read off the now complete ray class exact sequence 1 → U_𝔪 → 𝓞_Kˣ → (𝓞_K/𝔪₀)ˣ × {±1}^𝔪_∞ → Cl_𝔪 → Cl → 1, with the narrow case h⁺ · [𝓞_Kˣ : 𝓞_K^{ˣ,+}] = h · 2^{r₁} (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI (1.10)–(1.11)).
name: The ray class number formula

about: the signature of V + Vᵀ for a Seifert matrix V is unchanged by unimodular congruence and by the two enlargements that record adding a tube to the Seifert surface, so it is an invariant of the knot and not of the chosen surface; the trefoil has signature −2 and the figure-eight 0 (Lickorish, *An Introduction to Knot Theory*, Ch. 8; Murasugi 1965), complementing the Alexander polynomial of TauCeti#3948.
name: The signature of a knot is an S-equivalence invariant

about: an injective integral extension R → S satisfies dim S = dim R (incomparability plus going up, Atiyah–Macdonald 5.9 and 5.11), and for a finitely generated algebra A over a field k and any field extension K/k, dim(K ⊗_k A) = dim A, through Noether normalisation (Stacks 00OW).
name: Krull dimension is invariant under integral extensions and under base field extension

about: for a profinite group G and a prime p, the intersection Φ_p(G) of the open normal subgroups of index p is the closure of the subgroup generated by the p-th powers and the commutators; G/Φ_p(G) is elementary abelian, Φ_p(G) is characteristic and is carried onto Φ_p(H) by any continuous surjection G → H, and Φ_p(G) = 1 exactly when G itself is elementary abelian (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.8).
name: The pro-p Frattini subgroup is the closure of Gᵖ[G,G]

about: for finite Galois subextensions K, L of a field extension of F, a pair (σ, τ) ∈ Gal(K/F) × Gal(L/F) comes from Gal(KL/F) exactly when σ and τ agree on K ∩ L, so Gal(KL/F) ≅ Gal(K/F) ×_{Gal(K∩L/F)} Gal(L/F); for separable polynomials p and q this describes the image of Gal(pq) → Gal(p) × Gal(q), which is onto precisely when the two splitting fields meet in F.
name: The Galois group of a compositum is a fibre product

about: for L/K a finite Galois extension of fraction fields of Dedekind domains, P a prime above p with inertia field E and 𝔓_E = P ∩ 𝓞_E, and the residue field at p perfect: P is the only prime above 𝔓_E, e(P/𝔓_E) = e(P/p) and f(P/𝔓_E) = 1, while 𝔓_E is unramified over p with the full residue degree f(P/p) (Neukirch I (9.6)); Mathlib has the decomposition-field row of Hilbert's table, and this supplies the inertia-field row.
name: Splitting of a prime in the inertia field

about: for M/K finite Galois with group G, a subgroup H with fixed field E, and a prime Q of 𝓞_M above p with decomposition group D, the primes of 𝓞_E above p are in bijection with the double cosets H\G/D via σ ↦ σQ ∩ 𝓞_E (Neukirch I §9, where the proof is left to the reader; Janusz, *Algebraic Number Fields*, Ch. I).
name: The double coset law for splitting in a non-Galois subfield

about: the Monge value of a cost c between measures μ and ν is the infimum of ∫ c(x, T x) dμ over measurable maps T pushing μ to ν (and ∞ when there is none); it dominates the Kantorovich value of TauCeti#3875, a transport map attains the Kantorovich value exactly when its graph coupling is an optimal plan, and the inequality is strict for a Dirac source and an atomless target (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1).
name: The Monge problem

about: a # b = √a · √(√a⁻¹ b √a⁻¹) · √a in an algebra with a continuous functional calculus; for a strictly positive and b ≥ 0 it is the unique nonnegative solution of the Riccati equation x a⁻¹ x = b, it is symmetric in a and b, commutes with inversion, and satisfies the operator arithmetic–geometric mean inequality 2(a # b) ≤ a + b (Pusz–Woronowicz 1975; Ando, *Topics on operator inequalities*); for matrices, A S A = T has exactly one positive semidefinite solution A when S is positive definite and T positive semidefinite.
name: The operator geometric mean

about: X_ℂ = X ⊕ iX with the Taylor norm ‖z‖ = sup_{|w|=1} ‖Re(wz)‖, which contains X isometrically, is complete when X is, and gives every bounded real operator T a unique complex-linear extension T_ℂ with ‖T_ℂ‖ = ‖T‖ (Muñoz–Sarantopoulos–Tonge, *Studia Math.* 134 (1999)).
name: The normed complexification of a real Banach space

about: for M/K finite Galois with group G, a subgroup H with fixed field E, and a prime Q of 𝓞_M above p with decomposition group D, the primes of 𝓞_E above p are in bijection with the double cosets H\G/D via σ ↦ σQ ∩ 𝓞_E (Neukirch I §9, where the proof is left to the reader; Janusz, *Algebraic Number Fields*, Ch. I).
name: The double coset law for splitting in a non-Galois subfield

about: for n ≥ 3 and Gₙ(x) = ‖x‖^(2−n)/(n(n−2)ωₙ), ∫ Δf · Gₙ = −f(0) for every C² function f of compact support on ℝⁿ, i.e. −ΔGₙ = δ₀; on the way, [integration in polar coordinates](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Constructions/HaarToSphere.html#TauCeti.integral_eq_integral_toSphere_integral_Ioi) for every integrable function, where Mathlib had radial functions only (Evans, *PDE*, §2.2.1).
name: The Newtonian kernel is a fundamental solution of −Δ

about: over a field with 2 invertible, two diagonal forms ⟨a₁, …, aₙ⟩, ⟨b₁, …, bₙ⟩ of rank n ≥ 2 are isometric exactly when a chain of binary changes, each an isometry of two coefficients, connects them (Lam, I.5.2); and over ℝ, [two nondegenerate forms are isometric exactly when their signatures agree](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Real.html#QuadraticForm.equivalent_iff_sigPos_eq_and_sigNeg_eq); Mathlib has both halves of Sylvester's law of inertia but not the isometry criterion.
name: Witt's chain equivalence theorem, and real forms are classified by signature

about: for an arbitrary real cost c on X × Y, every c-cyclically monotone set lies in the c-superdifferential of a c-concave potential, and conversely the contact set of a dual feasible pair is c-cyclically monotone; no measure or topology enters, and the measure-theoretic half of the Schachermayer–Teichmann optimality criterion is what remains (Rockafellar 1966; Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, §2.3).
name: The Rockafellar–Rüschendorf theorem

about: for F/k with exact constant field: in genus one with a divisor of degree one, each degree-one divisor is equivalent to exactly one degree-one place, and P ↦ [P − P₀] is a bijection from the degree-one places onto Cl⁰(F) whose transported addition satisfies P ⊕ Q = R ↔ P + Q ∼ R + P₀, the intrinsic group law of an elliptic function field, no Weierstrass equation needed, beside the E(F) ≅ Cl⁰(F(E)) of TauCeti#6497; and [in genus zero with a divisor of degree one, F ≅ k(x)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/GenusZero.html#TauCeti.nonempty_algEquiv_ratFunc_of_genus_eq_zero_of_divisor_degree_eq_one) (Stichtenoth, Props 1.6.3, 6.1.6, 6.1.7).
name: Genus zero and genus one function fields

about: for an effective Hodge structure of weight one with Weil operator C, a nondegenerate alternating integral form Q with Q(Cx, Cy) = Q(x, y) and Q(Cx, x) > 0 on nonzero real vectors is a polarization, and both relations are necessary, so they characterise the Riemann forms of a lattice with a complex structure (Voisin, *Hodge Theory I*, §7.1.2).
name: The Riemann bilinear relations in weight one

about: the discriminant of every number field is ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4: with P and N the even and odd halves of the Leibniz expansion of the embedding determinant, P + N and PN are Galois-fixed algebraic integers and disc = (P + N)² − 4PN; Mathlib has this for quadratic fundamental discriminants only (Stickelberger 1897; Narkiewicz, Ch. 4).
name: Stickelberger's congruence

about: ∫_(A > 0) det(A)^(a−(p+1)/2) e^(−tr A) dA = Γ_p(a) over the positive-definite p × p matrices for a > (p−1)/2, announced two days ago in dimension 0 only and now in every dimension: [Lebesgue measure on the cone is the pushforward under L ↦ LLᵀ](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/SymmetricMatrix/Cholesky.html#TauCeti.map_cholesky_symmetricLebesgue) of Lebesgue measure on positive-diagonal lower-triangular L weighted by 2^p ∏ L_ii^(p−i); the Wishart normalising constant (Muirhead, Thms 2.1.9, 2.1.14).
name: The multivariate Gamma integral

about: a subset of a pro-p group G topologically generates G exactly when its image topologically generates G/Φ_p(G), since a proper closed subgroup lies in an open normal subgroup of index p; the theorem the Frattini subgroup Φ_p(G) of TauCeti#6649 exists for (Ribes–Zalesskii, §2.8).
name: Burnside's basis theorem for pro-p groups

about: a continuous surjective endomorphism of such a group has trivial kernel and is a topological automorphism, by counting the open subgroups of each index; the shift on ∏_ℕ F shows finite generation cannot be dropped (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, Prop. 2.5.2).
name: Topologically finitely generated profinite groups are Hopfian

about: the diagonal copy of K in 𝔸_K is a discrete closed subgroup and 𝔸_K/K is Hausdorff, the neighbourhood of 0 meeting K only in 0 being the adeles of norm < 1 at every infinite place and integral at every finite place; compactness of 𝔸_K/K is the next step (Cassels–Fröhlich, II §14).
name: A number field is discrete in its adele ring

about: a functional φ on a finite-dimensional algebra A with (a, b) ↦ φ(ab) nondegenerate, making A a Frobenius algebra: one exists exactly when A ≅ Hom_k(A, k) as right A-modules, the [Nakayama automorphism](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Algebra/Frobenius/Basic.html#LinearMap.IsFrobeniusFunctional.nakayamaAut) ν with φ(ab) = φ(b ν(a)) is a unique algebra automorphism, trivial exactly when φ is symmetric, and A is injective as a left and as a right module over itself (Lam, *Lectures on Modules and Rings*, §16).
name: Frobenius functionals and the Nakayama automorphism

about: F_μ⁻¹(t) = inf{x | t ≤ F_μ(x)} for a law μ on ℝ, and F_μ⁻¹ pushes the uniform law on (0, 1) forward to μ; reading two quantile functions off one uniform variable gives the [monotone coupling](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Quantile.html#MeasureTheory.Measure.quantileCoupling) of two real laws, whence W_p(μ, ν) ≤ ‖F_μ⁻¹ − F_ν⁻¹‖_(L^p(0,1)) for every p ∈ [1, ∞]; equality is still to come (Villani, §2.2).
name: The quantile function and inverse transform sampling

about: a linear code as a subspace of Fⁿ presented by a generator matrix (row space) or a parity-check matrix (kernel), compatible exactly when HGᵀ = 0; monomial and permutation equivalence of codes, preserving Hamming weight, distance, dimension and weight distribution; and the [Euclidean dual C^⊥](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/InformationTheory/Coding/EuclideanDual.html#Submodule.euclideanDual) with (C^⊥)^⊥ = C, dim C + dim C^⊥ = n and #C · #C^⊥ = qⁿ (Huffman–Pless, §§1.2–1.6).
name: Linear codes

about: for a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝓀 of order q, the unique multiplicative section 𝓀ˣ → 𝒪ˣ of reduction with values in the (q−1)-torsion, whose image is exactly μ_(q−1), so reduction identifies μ_(q−1)(K) with 𝓀ˣ; built from Hensel's lemma via μₙ(R) ≅ μₙ(R/𝔪) for a Henselian local domain R with n invertible, unlike Mathlib's `Perfection.teichmuller` (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, II §4).
name: The Teichmüller lift of a local field

about: for a function field of genus g with infinite exact constant field and a divisor D with 0 ≤ deg D ≤ 2g − 2, 2ℓ(D) ≤ deg D + 2, via ℓ(A) + ℓ(B) ≤ 1 + ℓ(A + B) for nonzero Riemann–Roch spaces; the finite-constant-field case waits on constant field extension (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.6.13).
name: Clifford's theorem for function fields

about: for every Galois extension L/K, finite or infinite, the continuous cohomology H¹(Gal(L/K), Lˣ) vanishes, so H¹(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) = 0 and, for n invertible in K, a ↦ [g ↦ g(α)/α] with αⁿ = a is an isomorphism [Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ ≅ H¹(G_K, μₙ)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.html#TauCeti.kummerIso); Mathlib's finite-layer Hilbert 90 is the input at each finite level (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, 6.2.1).
name: Hilbert 90 for infinite Galois extensions, and the Kummer isomorphism

about: over a field K with 2 invertible and a, b ∈ Kˣ, the following are equivalent: ℍ[K,a,b] ≅ M₂(K); b is a norm from K[T]/(T² − a); b = x² − ay² is solvable; ⟨1, −a, −b⟩ is isotropic; the norm form ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩ is isotropic; and every such algebra is either split or a division algebra (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, III.2.7, III.4.2; Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III.1).
name: The splitting criterion for quaternion algebras

about: a recurrent Markov exchangeable process on a countable state space started at a fixed state is a mixture of Markov chains; the version announced for TauCeti#6231 needed every state to be visited almost surely, and that hypothesis is now gone by passing to the visited successor array (Diaconis–Freedman, *de Finetti's theorem for Markov chains*, Ann. Probab. 8 (1980)).
name: The Diaconis–Freedman representation, for every recurrent process

about: for real degree n > p − 1, if the entries of a lower-triangular p × p matrix L are independent with L_ii ~ χ(n − i) and L_ij ~ N(0, 1) for j < i, then LLᵀ has the standard Wishart density det(A)^((n−p−1)/2) e^(−tr A/2) / (2^(np/2) Γ_p(n/2)) on the positive-definite cone; reading this off the Cholesky factor of a Wishart matrix is the remaining step. Underneath it, the [nonsingular Wishart law W_p(n, S)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Wishart/Nonsingular.html#TauCeti.nonsingularWishartMeasure) of real degree is defined by that density with scale S, has total mass one, is carried by A ↦ CACᵀ to scale CSCᵀ, and has the [inverse-Wishart law](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Wishart/Inverse.html#TauCeti.inverseWishartMeasure) as its image under inversion, with the classical density; the Gaussian–Gram law of TauCeti#6449 gets its characteristic function (Bartlett, Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh 53 (1933); Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, Ch. 3).
name: The Bartlett decomposition, and the Wishart density family

about: over an Artinian ring R the indecomposable projective classes form a ℤ-basis of K₀(proj R) with Krull–Schmidt multiplicities as coordinates, the pairing ⟨[P_i], [M]⟩ = [M : S_i] against the simple-class basis of G₀(mod R) is perfect, the Cartan map has matrix C_ij = [P_j : S_i], and [det C = ±1](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/UnimodularCartanMatrix.html#TauCeti.cartanMatrix_det_eq_one_or_neg_one) whenever every finitely generated module has a finite projective resolution, Eilenberg's theorem, with the sign left open (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, III.3).
name: The Cartan matrix of an Artinian ring

about: for a subgroup S ≤ G of finite index, the transfer Hⁿ(S, Res A) → Hⁿ(G, A) in every degree, built through Shapiro's lemma and the trace Coind Res A → A, natural in A and with cor ∘ res = [G : S]; on the way Mathlib's Shapiro isomorphism is identified as restriction followed by evaluation at 1 (Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, III §9).
name: Corestriction in group cohomology

about: the scheme-theoretic center of a semisimple affine group scheme over a field is finite over that field, in every characteristic and with no reducedness assumption on the center, the finiteness input for the central isogeny onto the adjoint group (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*; Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §8.1).
name: The center of a semisimple group is finite

about: for a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of order q, a uniformizer ϖ gives a topological isomorphism Kˣ ≅ ℤ × 𝒪ˣ, x ↦ (v(x), xϖ^(−v(x))), and the Teichmüller lift gives the canonical 𝒪ˣ ≅ μ_(q−1) × U⁽¹⁾, so Kˣ ≅ ℤ × μ_(q−1) × U⁽¹⁾ (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, II §§4–5; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II.5.3). Beside it, [a finite extension of a nonarchimedean local field is again one](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/FiniteExtension.html#TauCeti.finiteExtension_isNonarchimedeanLocalField), the spectral norm being its unique extended absolute value, and the containment half of the local square theorem: [every unit of depth 2v(2) + 1 is a square](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Squares.html#TauCeti.unitFiltration_le_range_powMonoidHom_two), so (Kˣ)² is open, dyadic fields included (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 63:1).
name: The structure of the multiplicative group of a local field

about: on a finite-dimensional boundaryless manifold, [the maximal flow of a C^(n+1) vector field is jointly C^(n+1) in initial point and time near (x₀, 0)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/IntegralCurve/SmoothDependence.html#TauCeti.contMDiffAt_maximalIntegralCurve), the local half of the fundamental theorem on flows, and the geodesic spray of a Riemannian manifold has a jointly smooth local flow on TM whose projections are the geodesics with prescribed initial data; the interface follows the open mathlib4#26394, and the global flow and exponential map come next (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 9.12; do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3 §2).
name: The smooth local geodesic flow

about: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over any field F, F(W) has genus one with exact constant field F, read off from L(n·O) = {p + qy : 2 deg p ≤ n, 2 deg q + 3 ≤ n} and Riemann's theorem; so Mathlib's elliptic curves are elliptic function fields in the sense of yesterday's TauCeti#6812 (Stichtenoth, Prop 6.1.3; Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3).
name: The function field of an elliptic curve has genus one

about: the state sum ⟨D⟩ = Σ_s a^(A(s)−B(s)) δ^(loops(s)−1), δ = −(a² + a⁻²), of a planar-diagram code, invariant under relabelling, the mirror image inverting a, ⟨c circles⟩ = δ^(c−1) and ⟨kink⟩ = −a³; invariance under the Reidemeister moves, and with it the Jones polynomial, is not yet there (Kauffman, *State models and the Jones polynomial*, Topology 26 (1987)).
name: The Kauffman bracket

about: for a function field of genus g with infinite exact constant field and a divisor D with 0 ≤ deg D ≤ 2g − 2, 2ℓ(D) ≤ deg D + 2, via ℓ(A) + ℓ(B) ≤ 1 + ℓ(A + B) for nonzero Riemann–Roch spaces; the finite-constant-field case waits on constant field extension (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.6.13).
name: Clifford's theorem for function fields

about: for real degree n > p − 1, if the entries of a lower-triangular p × p matrix L are independent with L_ii ~ χ(n − i) and L_ij ~ N(0, 1) for j < i, then LLᵀ has the standard Wishart density det(A)^((n−p−1)/2) e^(−tr A/2) / (2^(np/2) Γ_p(n/2)) on the positive-definite cone; reading this off the Cholesky factor of a Wishart matrix is the remaining step.
