about: for a separable isogeny φ : E₁ → E₂ of elliptic curves over a separably closed field, [#ker φ = deg φ](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/PointHom/Kernel.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.card_ker_eq_degree) and the function field of E₁ is Galois over that of E₂ with group ker φ acting by translations, so there is a unique φ̂ : E₂ → E₁ with φ̂ ∘ φ = [deg φ], and then φ ∘ φ̂ = [deg φ] and deg φ̂ = deg φ; the Weil pairing of TauCeti#8613 is alternating, e_N(T, T) = 1, hence nondegenerate on both sides, and [e_N(φS, T) = e_N(S, φ̂T)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Dual/WeilPairing.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.weilPairing_eq_weilPairing_dual); inseparable isogenies and descent to a general base field remain (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.4.10, III.6, III.8).
name: The dual isogeny, for separable isogenies over a separably closed field

about: a function φ : ℤ → ℂ is positive definite exactly when φ(n) = ∫ zⁿ dμ(z) for a finite positive measure μ on the unit circle, by Fejér means and Prokhorov's theorem; this is Bochner's theorem for the group ℤ, after the case of ℝⁿ in TauCeti#2611, and uniqueness of μ is not claimed (Herglotz 1911; Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, §1.4).
name: Herglotz's theorem

about: on a proper integral curve X of genus one over a field k, regular in codimension one, with k integrally closed in k(X) and a point x₀ of residue degree one, x ↦ [𝒪_X(x − x₀)] is a bijection from the points of residue degree one onto the Pic⁰ X of TauCeti#7803, under which x + y = z exactly when x + y ∼ z + x₀; the comparison with the group law of a Weierstrass curve is not yet made (Silverman III.3.4; Hartshorne IV.4).
name: Pic⁰ of a curve of genus one is its set of points of degree one

about: the Poisson integral of a circle-integrable function g is harmonic in the disc, and if g is continuous on the circle it tends to g(z) at every boundary point z, so it solves the Dirichlet problem with boundary values g; this is the Poisson integral theorem left open with TauCeti#9666, in the plane only; balls in ℝⁿ and Perron's method remain (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §2.2.4).
name: The Dirichlet problem on a disc, by the Poisson integral

about: if A, B and A ∩ B are path connected and contain x, and the interiors of A and B cover X, then π₁(X, x) is the pushout of π₁(A, x) ← π₁(A ∩ B, x) → π₁(B, x), the amalgamated free product; this is the statement for fundamental groups that the groupoid version of TauCeti#10096 had left open, and it gives [π₁(ℂ ∖ {0, 1}) free on the loops around 0 and 1](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/ThricePuncturedSphere/FundamentalGroup.html#TauCeti.ThricePuncturedSphere.fundamentalGroupMulEquivFreeGroup); covers by more than two sets remain, and a cosheaf formulation is in progress upstream as mathlib4#41603 (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 1.20).
name: The Seifert–van Kampen theorem for fundamental groups

about: in a class formation, the layer of an open normal subgroup V and its maximal abelian sublayer, that of V times the closed commutator subgroup, have the same norm group, so that the norm group of a finite Galois extension is that of its maximal abelian subextension; by counting with the reciprocity isomorphism of TauCeti#10127, and still with no local or global class formation constructed (Artin–Tate, *Class Field Theory*, Ch. XIV; Serre, *Local Fields*, XI).
name: The norm limitation theorem for class formations

about: for a field K with n invertible and a, b ∈ Kˣ with a + b = 1, the cup product (a) ∪ (b) of the Kummer classes vanishes in H²(G_K, P) for every equivariant pairing μₙ × μₙ → P, by Tate's argument, which writes 1 − a as a product of norms from the fields K[X]/(f), f the irreducible factors of Xⁿ − a; the invariant map that would turn this into the Hilbert symbol of a local field is not yet constructed (Tate, *Relations between K₂ and Galois cohomology*, 1976).
name: The Steinberg relation for Kummer classes

about: the analytic realization of a finite regular fan, glued from the affine charts of its cones, is a complex manifold in which every chart inclusion is a biholomorphism onto an open subset, and the complex torus acts on it holomorphically; the atlas comes from a general statement that a space covered by open embeddings of manifolds with Cⁿ transition maps is a Cⁿ manifold (Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §§1.4, 2.1).
name: The complex manifold of a regular fan

about: if a Jordan curve C in ℂ coincides with a line near one of its points, as a simple closed polygon does, then points on opposite sides of that line lie in different components of ℂ ∖ C, and the bounded part of the filled hull of C is a nonempty Jordan domain with frontier C, by Borsuk's criterion; the Jordan curve theorem for arbitrary curves is not claimed (Borsuk 1932; Munkres, *Topology*, §§61–63).
name: The inside of a Jordan curve with a straight piece

about: for a monic f over a proper algebraically closed normed field such as ℂ and ε > 0, there is δ > 0 such that the roots of every monic g of the same degree with coefficients within δ of those of f can be matched bijectively, with multiplicity, to those of f at distances below ε; alongside, the subresultant criterion: deg gcd(p, q) is the least j whose principal subresultant coefficient is nonzero (Basu–Pollack–Roy, *Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry*, §5.1, Prop. 4.25).
name: Continuity of the roots of a polynomial, with multiplicities

about: for a monic separable f of degree n and a resolvent attached to a subgroup H of Sₙ whose specialization at f is separable, the irreducible factors of the resolvent correspond to the orbits of the Galois group of f on Sₙ/H, with degrees the orbit sizes; and the table for quartics is complete away from characteristic 2: an irreducible quartic with nonsquare discriminant whose cubic resolvent has a root has group D₄ or C₄ according to whether it stays irreducible over F(√disc f) (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, §6.3).
name: The factorization theorem for resolvents

about: the ring of profinite integers of TauCeti#10044 is isomorphic, as a topological ring, to the product of the rings ℤ_ℓ over all primes ℓ, by the Chinese remainder theorem at each finite level; with it, Ẑ is the inverse limit of the rings ℤ/n, and an element x of a profinite group has powers x^a for a ∈ Ẑ (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §§2.3, 4.1).
name: Ẑ ≅ ∏_ℓ ℤ_ℓ

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p with ramification index e and an integer i with (p − 1)i > e, the logarithm is an isomorphism of topological groups from the units 1 + 𝔪^i onto the additive group 𝔪^i, with inverse the exponential (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II (5.5)).
name: The logarithm on deep units

about: for the Hecke characters of TauCeti#8468: the infinity type, read off the characters of ℝˣ and ℂˣ at the archimedean places; algebraicity in the sense of Weil's type A₀, which holds for characters of finite order and fails for ‖·‖^{it} with t ≠ 0; and the conductor of a character of finite order, the least modulus through whose ray class group it factors (Weil, *Basic Number Theory*, VII §3).
name: Algebraic Hecke characters

about: the subsets of Rⁿ, for an ordered commutative ring R, that are finite Boolean combinations of sets {p = 0} and {p > 0} with p a polynomial, with closure under Boolean operations, polynomial preimages, products and sections; closure under projection, the Tarski–Seidenberg theorem, is not yet proved (Basu–Pollack–Roy, Ch. 2).
name: Semialgebraic sets

about: a nontrivial finite p-group G with minimal number of generators d(G) and relation rank r(G) = dim H²(G, 𝔽_p) satisfies d(G)² < 4·r(G), so a finite p-group needs more than a quarter of the square of its generator count in relations; the proof follows Roquette through the group algebra 𝔽_p[G] and a minimal pro-p presentation (Cassels–Fröhlich, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Ch. IX §4; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (3.9.7)).
name: The Golod–Shafarevich inequality

about: for a number field K, unconditionally, the number π_K(x) of prime ideals of norm at most x is asymptotic to Li(x), [equivalently to x/log x](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Prime/DedekindZeta.html#TauCeti.primeCount_univ_isEquivalent_div_log), together with ψ_K(x) ~ x and ϑ_K(x) ~ x; the Wiener–Ikehara route is fed by the simple pole of ζ_K at 1 and its nonvanishing on Re s = 1 (Landau 1903; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VII §5).
name: The prime ideal theorem

about: a closed subgroup K of a finite-dimensional real Lie group is an embedded Lie subgroup: it carries a smooth structure for its subspace topology making it a Lie group whose inclusion is a smooth immersion, modelled on the Lie algebra {X : exp(tX) ∈ K for all t}, which TauCeti#10693 [identifies](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/Subgroup/Differential.html#TauCeti.Lie.EmbeddedLieSubgroupData.lieEquivLieSubalgebraOfSubgroup) with the Lie algebra of K as a Lie group (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 20.12).
name: Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem

about: a finite-type commutative Hopf algebra over a field of characteristic zero is smooth, hence reduced: every affine group scheme of finite type in characteristic zero is smooth, and nonreduced groups such as μ_p and α_p occur only in positive characteristic; the proof shows the nilradical lies in the square of the augmentation ideal and compares Lie algebra dimensions (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 3.23; Waterhouse §11.4).
name: Cartier's theorem

about: a random array (X_{ij})_{i,j∈ℕ} in a standard Borel space has law invariant under simultaneous permutation of rows and columns exactly when it has the law of X_{ij} = F(U, U_i, U_j, U_{{i,j}}) for one measurable F and independent uniform variables attached to the whole array, to each vertex and to each unordered pair; this is the joint form, after the separately exchangeable form X_{ij} = F(U, U_i, V_j, U_{ij}) of TauCeti#9789 (Aldous 1981; Hoover 1979; Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).
name: The Aldous–Hoover representation for jointly exchangeable arrays

about: in the upper half-plane a triangle with vertices A, B, C ∈ ℍ has area π − α − β − γ, and a [compact convex n-gon](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/Polygon/GaussBonnet.html#TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.CompactConvexPolygon.volume_carrier) with all vertices in ℍ has area (n − 2)π minus the sum of its interior angles, the Gauss–Bonnet formula for hyperbolic polygons; ideal vertices are not yet covered (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, Thm 5.4; Walkden, *Hyperbolic Geometry*, Thm 7.2.2).
name: The area of a hyperbolic triangle is its angle defect

about: for a weakly regular measure μ, a measurable map into a second-countable space, a measurable set s of finite measure and ε > 0, there is a closed F ⊆ s with μ(s ∖ F) < ε on which the map is continuous; with [Vitali's convergence theorem for maps into a pseudometric space](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Function/UniformIntegrable.html#TauCeti.tendsto_eLpNorm_dist_iff_tendstoInMeasure_and_unifIntegrable) it gives the theorem that the graph plans (id, Tₙ)_#μ converge narrowly exactly when Tₙ → T in measure (Rudin, *Real and Complex Analysis*, Thm 2.24; Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Lemma 5.4.1).
name: Lusin's theorem

about: over a nonarchimedean local field K with 2 invertible, every regular quadratic form of rank at least five is isotropic, a form of rank three is isotropic exactly when its Hasse invariant is (−1, −d)_K, a form of rank four exactly when d ≠ 1 or s = (−1, −1)_K, and an [anisotropic form of rank four exists](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/QuadraticForm/Isotropy.html#TauCeti.RegularFormClass.exists_rank_eq_four_and_anisotropic), so the u-invariant of K is 4 (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, IV §2.2, Thm 6).
name: Isotropy of quadratic forms over a local field, and u(K) = 4

about: an infinite Demushkin group G has cd_p G = 2, because Tate's duality maps Hⁱ(G, M) → Hom(H²⁻ⁱ(G, M^∨), H²(G, 𝔽_p)) are [bijective](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/Duality/Basic.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.dualityMap2_bijective) for every finite 𝔽_p[G]-module M; hence every [open subgroup](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/OpenSubgroup.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.openSubgroup) U is Demushkin with n(U) − 2 = [G : U](n(G) − 2) and canonical character χ|_U, and the Andozhskii and Dummit–Labute [recognition criteria](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/Recognition.html#TauCeti.isDemushkin_iff_finrank_cohomFp_two_openSubgroup) hold as equivalences (Serre, Bourbaki exposé 252, §9; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (3.9.15)).
name: Demushkin groups have cohomological dimension two

about: two Demushkin groups of the same rank whose canonical characters χ : G → ℤ_pˣ have the same image are topologically isomorphic, now at every prime and every rank: the dyadic even-rank families with image {±1}, {±1} × U^(f) and Labute's twisted U^[f] join the q ≠ 2 and odd-rank cases announced earlier, and [Labute's Theorem 2](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/NormalForm/Uniqueness.html#TauCeti.freeProP.exists_continuousMulEquiv_apply_eq_of_range_demushkinCharacter_eq) carries any two relators with the same invariants to each other by a continuous automorphism of the free pro-p group (Labute, *Classification of Demushkin groups*, Canad. J. Math. 19 (1967)).
name: Labute's classification of Demushkin groups, uniqueness in full

about: for a weak solution of a divergence-form equation −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = 0 with bounded measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients in dimension n ≥ 3, the oscillation on B(x₀, r) is at most C (r/R)^α times the oscillation on B(x₀, R), with α, C depending only on the ellipticity constants and n; this is the a-priori estimate behind the Hölder continuity of De Giorgi–Nash–Moser, whose Hölder continuous representative is the next step (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Ch. 8).
name: De Giorgi's oscillation decay

about: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a class function on a finite group is a virtual character exactly when its restriction to every elementary subgroup, a product of a cyclic group and a p-group, is one; it is the projection formula run against Brauer's induction theorem of TauCeti#9171 (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §11.1).
name: Brauer's characterization of characters

about: over a separably closed field in which ℓ is invertible, T_ℓ E = lim E[ℓⁿ] is a free ℤ_ℓ-module of rank 2 with its profinite topology, built on a [general Tate module](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/Torsion/TateModule.html#TauCeti.TateModule) lim A[pⁿ] of an abelian group; the ℓ-adic Weil pairing and the Galois representation on T_ℓ E are the next steps (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.7.1).
name: The Tate module of an elliptic curve is free of rank two

about: a function φ on a discrete abelian group G is positive definite exactly when φ(g) = ∫ χ(g) dμ(χ) for a finite positive measure μ on the Pontryagin dual of G, by the GNS construction and the spectral theorem for commuting unitaries; this extends Herglotz's theorem for ℤ to ℤᵈ, ℚ, ℚ/ℤ and finite groups, after ℝⁿ; uniqueness of μ on Polish duals is TauCeti#10394 (Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, §1.4).
name: Bochner's theorem on discrete abelian groups

about: over a field, the transferred projection A → H(A) is an A∞-quasi-isomorphism inducing the identity on cohomology, so any quasi-isomorphism between a minimal A∞-algebra and A composes with it to an A∞-isomorphism with the minimal model; with the existence half of TauCeti#10208 this is Kadeishvili's theorem in full (Kadeishvili 1980; Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §3.3).
name: Kadeishvili's theorem, the uniqueness half

about: j = E₄³/Δ satisfies j(τ) = q⁻¹ + Σ_{m≥0} c_{m+1} qᵐ on all of ℍ, q = e^{2πiτ}, with the coefficients pinned by the power-series identity (q·j)·Δ = q·E₄³, giving the constant term 744 and the coefficient 196884 of q, so j − q⁻¹ → 744 at i∞ (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §3).
name: The q-expansion of the modular invariant j

about: on a separable real inner product space, between finite measures with finite second moments, a coupling is optimal for the cost ‖x − y‖²/2 exactly when it is concentrated on the subdifferential graph of a proper lower semicontinuous convex function, so gradients of convex functions are optimal maps, the converse of Brenier's theorem; for absolutely continuous μ and ν the [inverse Brenier map](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Brenier.html#TauCeti.exists_isKantorovichOptimalTransportMap_gradient_and_gradient_fenchelConjugate) is the gradient of the Legendre conjugate u* (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Thm 2.12).
name: The Knott–Smith optimality criterion

about: Tits' representation of a Coxeter system on the real span of the simple roots, with B(αᵢ, αⱼ) = −cos(π/mᵢⱼ) and simple reflections acting as orthogonal reflections, shows that sᵢsⱼ has order exactly mᵢⱼ (infinite when mᵢⱼ = ∞), so the presentation does not collapse, the input the braid moves of Matsumoto's theorem need; faithfulness is not claimed (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §§5.3–5.4).
name: The geometric representation of a Coxeter group

about: for a finite Galois extension of nonarchimedean local fields with group G and a normal subgroup H, (G/H)^v = G^v H/H for every v ≥ −1, read from Herbrand's theorem for the lower numbering and the transitivity of the Herbrand functions; this is what lets upper numbering be defined on infinite Galois groups and transports upper breaks in the Hasse–Arf argument (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, IV §3, Prop. 14).
name: The upper numbering filtration passes to quotients

about: isomorphism classes of connected degree-n covers of ℂ ∖ {0, 1} correspond bijectively to isomorphism classes of transitive triples (σ₀, σ₁, σ_∞) in Sₙ with σ₀σ₁σ_∞ = 1, at the numbered, bare and pointed levels, since π₁ is free on two peripheral loops; this is the combinatorial side of dessins d'enfants, not Belyi's theorem (Girondo–González-Diez, Thm 2.61; Lando–Zvonkin, §1.5).
name: Covers of the thrice-punctured sphere are classified by permutation triples

about: over a Dedekind domain O with fraction field K in which 2 and 3 are invertible, a pair (c₄, c₆) is the pair of c-invariants of a nonsingular Weierstrass equation with coefficients in O exactly when Kraus's local condition, integrality of c₄, c₆, Δ with congruence witnesses above 2 and 3, holds at every height-one prime, by patching the local criterion of TauCeti#9705 (Kraus, Acta Arith. 54 (1989)).
name: Kraus's criterion for the c-invariants

about: Wedhorn's category (Adic): pre-adic spaces whose structure presheaf is a sheaf, covered by open affinoid subspaces Spa(A, A⁺), with open immersions and restriction to opens; Spa(A, A⁺) is an adic space whenever its structure presheaf is a sheaf, and sheafiness for strongly noetherian Tate pairs (Tate acyclicity) is still in progress (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Def. 8.22; Huber).
name: Adic spaces

about: the entropically regularised cost inf_π ∫ c dπ + ε·KL(π ‖ μ ⊗ ν) and the static Schrödinger problem inf_π KL(π ‖ R) over couplings of μ and ν, with the Gibbs identity showing they are the same problem for the reference R = Z⁻¹e^{−c/ε}(μ ⊗ ν), up to the free energy −ε log Z (Léonard, *A survey of the Schrödinger problem*, 2014; Nutz, *Introduction to Entropic Optimal Transport*).
name: Entropic optimal transport and the Schrödinger problem

about: for a scheme X over a ring R, the sheafification of U ↦ Ω_{𝒪(U)/R}, with its universal derivation d : 𝒪_X → Ω_{X/R} and the universal property (Ω_{X/R} → M) ≃ Der_R(𝒪_X, M), built on Mathlib's presheaf of differentials; for a smooth curve it is the dualizing sheaf of Serre duality (Hartshorne II.8; Stacks 01UM).
name: The sheaf of relative differentials Ω_{X/R}

about: an affine group scheme over a commutative ring R is reductive when it is smooth with connected reductive geometric fibres, with split maximal torus data as extra structure, validated on SLₙ; and [PGLₙ](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/ProjectiveGeneralLinear/Basic.html#TauCeti.ProjectiveGeneralLinear.pointsMulEquiv) is constructed over R as the automorphism group scheme of the matrix algebra Mₙ, with GLₙ → PGLₙ surjective on field points by Skolem–Noether (Conrad, *Reductive Group Schemes*, Def. 3.1.1).
name: Reductive group schemes over a ring

about: for a finite Galois extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the norm residue isomorphism Kˣ/N(Lˣ) ≅ Gal(L/K)^ab, obtained by proving that (G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) is a class formation; the [absolute Artin map](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Local/ArtinMap.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.artinMap) Kˣ → G_K^ab is continuous with dense image and kernel the intersection of all norm groups, and on unramified extensions Art(x) = Frob^{v(x)}; the existence theorem is not yet proved (Serre, *Local Fields*, XI–XIII; Artin–Tate, XIV).
name: Local reciprocity for nonarchimedean local fields

about: every finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an arbitrary field has a faithful finite-dimensional representation, so it embeds in some 𝔤𝔩ₙ(K); assembled from Ado's theorem in characteristic zero and Iwasawa's in characteristic p, with Hochschild's strengthening that every ad-nilpotent element can be made to act nilpotently (Fulton–Harris, App. E; Iwasawa 1948; Hochschild 1966).
name: The Ado–Iwasawa theorem

about: for a uniformly elliptic operator in divergence form with merely measurable coefficients on an open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, n ≥ 3, every weak solution u ∈ H¹(Ω) of −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = 0 has a precise representative that is α-Hölder on compact subsets of Ω, with α depending only on n and the ellipticity constants; this completes the chain of TauCeti#9933 and TauCeti#10522; lower-order terms and Harnack's inequality are not included (De Giorgi 1957; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 8.22).
name: De Giorgi's theorem on Hölder continuity of weak solutions

about: for a Lie algebra L over any commutative ring with a basis indexed by a linear order, the ordered monomials in the basis form a basis of U(L); in graded form, Sym(L) ≅ gr U(L) for L free as a module, so L embeds in U(L), which is a domain when the base ring is; as an application Verma modules are free of rank one over U(𝔫⁻) (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §17.4; Bourbaki, *Lie* I §2.7).
name: The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem

about: for a finite connected quiver with no pair of opposite arrows, over any field: finite representation type ⇔ positive definite Tits form ⇔ the underlying graph is a Dynkin diagram of type A, D or E; the new direction exhibits infinite families of indecomposables on cycles and on the extended Dynkin diagrams, completing the half Dynkin ⇒ finite type of TauCeti#9480 (Gabriel 1972; Assem–Simson–Skowroński, Ch. VII).
name: Gabriel's theorem, both directions

about: for a finite-dimensional relative CW complex (C, D), with coefficients in any abelian category in which coproducts over the cells are exact, the homology of the cellular chain complex is isomorphic to Hₙ(C, D); consequently the singular Euler characteristic of a finite CW complex is the alternating count of its cells (Hatcher, Thm 2.35).
name: Cellular homology computes singular homology

about: the Jones polynomial of an oriented planar-diagram code, defined as the writhe-normalised Kauffman state sum, is unchanged by relabelling and by the three Reidemeister moves in their oriented forms, so the right-handed trefoil diagram, with value t + t³ − t⁴, is not Reidemeister-equivalent to the unknot or to its mirror image; this is at the level of diagrams, as Reidemeister's theorem is not formalized; on the braid side a Markov trace on the Temperley–Lieb algebras gives an invariant of Markov classes of braids (Lickorish, *An Introduction to Knot Theory*, Ch. 3).
name: The Jones polynomial is invariant under Reidemeister moves

about: over a field of characteristic zero the solvable radical of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra L has a complementary subalgebra S, and L ≅ rad(L) ⋊ S with S semisimple; existence only, without conjugacy of Levi complements; along the way Weyl's complete reducibility theorem now holds over every field of characteristic zero, not only algebraically closed ones (Jacobson, *Lie Algebras*, III §9; Fulton–Harris, App. E).
name: Levi's theorem

about: over a nonarchimedean local field in which 2 is invertible, dyadic fields included, two nondegenerate quadratic forms are isometric exactly when these three invariants agree, now in every rank (rank ≤ 3 was TauCeti#8747); hence quaternion algebras (a,b) and (c,d) are isomorphic iff their Hilbert symbols agree, and there is one quaternion division algebra and one anisotropic quaternary form; Serre's formula for the Hilbert symbol of ℚ₂ is TauCeti#10560 (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, IV Thm 7; O'Meara §63).
name: Quadratic forms over a local field are classified by rank, discriminant and Hasse invariant

about: on any locally compact abelian group G, with no countability hypothesis, φ : G → ℂ is continuous and positive definite exactly when φ(g) = ∫ χ(g) dμ(χ) for a finite inner regular Borel measure μ on the Pontryagin dual, and μ is unique; this extends the cases ℝⁿ and discrete G, through a spectral theorem for strongly continuous unitary representations (Folland, *A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis*, Thm 4.18; Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, §1.4).
name: Bochner's theorem on locally compact abelian groups

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K every class of Br K = H²(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) is split by an unramified extension, so the Frobenius-normalised invariant, defined on the unramified part in TauCeti#9858, is an isomorphism inv_K : Br K ≅ ℚ/ℤ; moreover inv_L ∘ res = [L:K]·inv_K and inv_K ∘ cor = inv_L, and Hⁱ(G_K, A) is finite for i ≤ 2 when A is a finite Galois module of exponent invertible in K (Serre, *Local Fields*, XIII §3; *Galois Cohomology*, II §5.2).
name: The local invariant Br K ≅ ℚ/ℤ

about: on a real locally convex space, a lower semicontinuous convex function f : E → [−∞, ∞] that never takes the value −∞ equals its biconjugate f∗∗, and conversely f∗∗ = f forces f to be convex and lower semicontinuous; this is the theorem left open when the Legendre–Fenchel conjugate was introduced in TauCeti#9586 (Rockafellar, *Convex Analysis*, §12; Ekeland–Témam, Ch. I).
name: The Fenchel–Moreau theorem

about: the modular invariant j extends to a holomorphic map of degree one from the compactified quotient PSL₂(ℤ)∖ℍ ∪ {∞} to the Riemann sphere, hence a biholomorphism X(1) ≅ ℙ¹(ℂ) sending the cusp to ∞, ρ to 0 and i to 1728 (Diamond–Shurman, §2.4; Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §3).
name: The modular curve X(1) is the Riemann sphere

about: for a function field F/k of genus g ≥ 2 with exact constant field k, a finite group G of k-automorphisms of F such that F is tamely ramified over the fixed field of G has |G| ≤ 84(g − 1); tameness is automatic in characteristic zero, and over a perfect field of characteristic p when p ∤ |G|; finiteness of the full automorphism group is not part of the statement (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Ex. 3.18).
name: The Hurwitz bound 84(g − 1)

about: for any field K the Brauer group of central simple K-algebras is isomorphic to the continuous cohomology group H²(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ), the class of a crossed product going to the inflation of its cocycle (TauCeti#9858 had taken H² as the definition); when 2 is invertible the quaternion algebra (a,b) corresponds to the cup product (a) ∪ (b) of Kummer classes in H²(G_K, 𝔽₂), which vanishes iff b is a norm from K(√a) (Gille–Szamuely, §4.4 and §4.7; Serre, *Local Fields*, X §5).
name: The Brauer group is H²(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ)

about: for a matrix K with strictly positive entries and positive row and column targets a, b of equal mass there are positive vectors u, v such that (uᵢKᵢⱼvⱼ) has row sums a and column sums b; the scaled matrix is unique and is the minimiser of relative entropy against K among matrices with these marginals; in the measure setting the static Schrödinger problem of TauCeti#10733 has exactly one minimiser whenever its value is finite (Sinkhorn 1964; Csiszár 1975).
name: Sinkhorn's theorem

about: for a Noetherian ring R and a quasi-coherent sheaf M on Spec R, Hⁿ(Spec R, M) = 0 for all n > 0, by dimension shifting through injective modules, whose associated sheaves are flasque; the same holds on Noetherian affine opens of any scheme (Hartshorne III.3.4–3.5).
name: Serre's vanishing theorem on Noetherian affine schemes

about: for finite-dimensional real spaces E, F and a C¹ map f : E × F → L(E, F), the total differential equation Du(x) = f(x, u(x)) has a local solution through every initial point near (x₀, y₀) exactly when f satisfies the Frobenius integrability condition near (x₀, y₀), and solutions are unique; equivalently a graph distribution on E × F is involutive iff it is integrable; the statement for foliations of a manifold is still to come (Dieudonné, *Foundations of Modern Analysis*, §10.9).
name: The Frobenius theorem, local form

about: for an elliptic curve E over F, a separably closed extension K and a prime ℓ invertible in K, Aut(K/F) acts continuously on T_ℓE with determinant the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character, read off from the ℓ-adic Weil pairing T_ℓE × T_ℓE → ℤ_ℓ(1), which is alternating, nondegenerate and Galois-equivariant (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.7–8).
name: The determinant of the ℓ-adic representation of an elliptic curve is the cyclotomic character

about: for a finite group G of exponent e, every irreducible complex representation of G is realisable over ℚ(ζₑ), and more generally over any field of characteristic zero containing a primitive e-th root of unity; one input is that irreducible representations of finite nilpotent groups are monomial (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §12.3 Thm 24).
name: Brauer's theorem on splitting fields

about: for a newform f of level Γ₁(N) and weight k ≥ 2 the Fourier coefficients aₙ(f) are algebraic integers and ℚ(aₙ(f) : n ≥ 1) is finite over ℚ; the proof shows that the modular-symbol period map is injective, so periods determine a cusp form, and hence that the Hecke algebra on cusp forms is a finite ℤ-module, the route of the LeanModularForms development; weight one is not covered (Shimura, *Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions*, Ch. 3 and §8.2).
name: The coefficient field of a newform is a number field

about: for the tableau-defined Schur polynomial s_μ in finitely many variables over any commutative ring, s_μ = det(h_{μᵢ−i+j}) with hₘ the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials; the dual identity in the elementary symmetric polynomials is not yet proved (Macdonald, I.(3.4); Stanley, EC2, Thm 7.16.1).
name: The Jacobi–Trudi identity

about: in an arbitrary Coxeter system any two reduced words for the same element are connected by braid moves, so for generators of any monoid satisfying the braid relations the product along a reduced word depends only on the element (Matsumoto 1964; Björner–Brenti, Thm 3.3.1).
name: Matsumoto's theorem

about: Spin(3,1) ≅ SL₂(ℂ), together with Spin(3) ≅ SU(2), Spin(4) ≅ SU(2) × SU(2) and Spin(2,2) ≅ SL₂(ℝ) × SL₂(ℝ), each from an explicit model of the even Clifford algebra; these are isomorphisms of abstract groups, with no topology yet (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §4).
name: Exceptional isomorphisms of low-dimensional Spin groups

about: every continuous group homomorphism between finite-dimensional real Lie groups is C^∞, by one-parameter subgroups and the Lie–Trotter product formula, so it induces a homomorphism of Lie algebras (Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, Ch. 3).
name: Continuous homomorphisms of Lie groups are smooth

about: for a Lie group G that is locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected, the universal cover of G based at the identity is again a Lie group (a topological group by TauCeti#11629), the covering projection is a homomorphism and a local diffeomorphism inducing a bijection of Lie algebras, and its kernel is π₁(G, 1), which is abelian, as for every topological monoid (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Ch. 7).
name: The universal covering group of a Lie group

about: W₂²(N(m₁,S₁), N(m₂,S₂)) = |m₁ − m₂|² + tr S₁ + tr S₂ − 2 tr (S₁^{1/2} S₂ S₁^{1/2})^{1/2} on ℝⁿ, for S₁ positive definite and S₂ positive semidefinite, with an affine optimal transport map (Givens–Shortt 1984).
name: The Wasserstein distance between Gaussian measures

about: an injective, locally collared map f : N → M from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is collared, that is, extends to an open embedding N × [0,1) → M; likewise a two-sided locally bicollared map is bicollared; compact domains only, and not yet applied to boundaries of manifolds (Brown 1962; Connelly 1971).
name: Brown's collaring theorem

about: over an arbitrary field every morphism of elliptic curves fixing the origin is additive on points, and End(E) is a ring without zero divisors under addition of morphisms and composition; the degree form on End(E) in the inseparable case is still open (Silverman III.4.8).
name: Isogenies are homomorphisms, and End(E) is a ring

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K with residue field of order q, the quotient of G_K by wild inertia is isomorphic as a topological group to the profinite group ⟨σ, τ | στσ⁻¹ = τ^q⟩, with σ a Frobenius lift and τ a generator of tame inertia (Iwasawa 1955; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (7.5.3)).
name: Iwasawa's presentation of the tame Galois group of a local field

about: for a finite group G and a prime p, with no coprimality assumption, two finitely generated projective ℤ_p[G]-modules whose rationalisations M ⊗ ℚ_p and N ⊗ ℚ_p are isomorphic are themselves isomorphic (Swan 1960; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (5.6.10)).
name: Swan's theorem for p-adic group rings

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ and an arbitrary open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, with no boundary regularity, the functions smooth on Ω are dense in W^{1,p}(Ω); higher orders remain (Meyers–Serrin 1964; Evans, §5.3.2).
name: The Meyers–Serrin theorem, first order

about: for a properly discontinuous isometric action on a proper metric space, the Dirichlet domain {x : d(x,p) ≤ d(x,gp) for all g} of a point with trivial stabilizer is a fundamental domain as soon as the bisectors are null sets; in particular every Fuchsian group has a Dirichlet fundamental domain in ℍ; convexity and side pairings are not yet proved (Beardon, §9.4; Katok, Thm 3.2.2).
name: Dirichlet domains are fundamental domains

about: L(m; ℓ₀,…,ℓₖ) = S^{2k+1}/(ℤ/m) is a compact analytic manifold covered by the sphere, with π₁ ≅ ℤ/m for k ≥ 1, so homeomorphic lens spaces have the same m; no finer classification is proved (Hatcher, Example 2.43).
name: Lens spaces and their fundamental groups

about: if every polynomial in the Collins projection of a finite family F of polynomials in y over ℝ[x₁,…,xₙ] is sign-invariant on a connected S ⊆ ℝⁿ, then over S the real roots of F are the graphs of finitely many continuous, strictly ordered functions with constant multiplicities; this is the lifting step of cylindrical algebraic decomposition, not yet the algorithm (Collins 1975; Basu–Pollack–Roy, Thm 5.16).
name: Collins' delineability theorem

about: for an absolutely continuous curve γ in a metric space the limit |γ′|(t) = lim d(γ(s), γ(t))/|s − t| exists for almost every t, is integrable, satisfies d(γ(s), γ(u)) ≤ ∫ₛᵘ |γ′|, and is the smallest such density; the p-energy ∫|γ′|ᵖ is lower semicontinuous (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Thm 1.1.2).
name: The metric derivative of an absolutely continuous curve

about: for f complex differentiable on a closed polydisc in ℂⁿ, the iterated integral of f(z)/∏(zᵢ − wᵢ) over the distinguished boundary equals (2πi)ⁿ f(w), so a complex differentiable function on an open subset of a finite-dimensional complex space is analytic; this extends Mathlib's one-variable statements and assumes joint differentiability, so it is not Hartogs' theorem (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, §2.2).
name: Cauchy's integral formula on polydiscs

about: for a Cᵏ section s of a Banach bundle over M × Λ, with M a Banach manifold and Λ a Banach space of parameters, whose linearisation along M is Fredholm of index d and whose full linearisation is surjective at every zero, the regular parameters form a residual set, and for those λ the zero set of s(·, λ) is a d-dimensional manifold; k must exceed a bound in the kernel dimension inherited from Sard–Smale (McDuff–Salamon, Thm A.3.6).
name: Parametric transversality for Fredholm sections

about: for an affine group scheme over a field and a closed subgroup scheme with finitely generated ideal, there are a finite-dimensional representation V and a line L in an exterior power of V such that, on points in every commutative algebra, the subgroup is exactly the stabilizer of L, on which it acts through a unique character (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 4.27).
name: Chevalley's theorem on closed subgroups

about: for a reduced Noetherian ring A, a finitely generated A-algebra B and a finite B-module M, the set of primes of A at which M is free contains a dense open subset of Spec A; as an application a dominant homomorphism onto a reduced affine group of finite type over an algebraically closed field is faithfully flat (Matsumura, Thm 24.1; Stacks 051R).
name: Generic freeness

about: for every field k, each k-automorphism of the rational function field k(X) is a Möbius substitution, giving a group isomorphism PGL₂(k) ≅ Aut(k(X)/k) (Stichtenoth, Ex. 1.2).
name: Aut(k(X)/k) ≅ PGL₂(k)

about: over a field K with 2 invertible, w₁(q) ∈ H¹(G_K, 𝔽₂) and w₂(q) ∈ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂) are isometry invariants, w₁ is the discriminant and the Whitney sum formulas hold, and w₂(q) is the image of the Hasse invariant under Br(K)[2] ≅ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂) (Delzant 1962).
name: The second Stiefel–Whitney class of a quadratic form is its Hasse invariant

about: S³, E³, H³, S² × ℝ, H² × ℝ, SL₂ℝ~ (in a coordinate model on ℝ³), Nil and Sol as analytic Riemannian 3-manifolds, each with transitive isometry group and simply connected; a geometric structure on a space is a homeomorphism with the quotient of a model by a group of isometries acting freely and properly discontinuously, and three-dimensional lens spaces are spherical; no classification is claimed, and the geometrization conjecture is only stated (Scott, *The geometries of 3-manifolds*).
name: Thurston's eight model geometries

about: for a scheme X and a quasi-coherent commutative 𝒪_X-algebra 𝒜, the scheme over X glued from the Spec 𝒜(U) over affine opens U; its structure morphism is affine and restricts to Spec 𝒜(U) → U, and the construction is functorial in 𝒜; the universal property is not yet proved (Stacks 01LL; EGA II §1.3).
name: The relative spectrum Spec_X(𝒜)

about: the pairing Hᵖ(X) ⊗ Hₙ(X) → H_{n−p}(X) on singular cohomology and homology, with general coefficient pairings, defined through the Alexander–Whitney diagonal, with the projection formula f_∗(x ⌢ f^∗α) = f_∗x ⌢ α and, over a commutative ring, (x ⌢ α) ⌢ β = x ⌢ (α ⌣ β); the cup product was TauCeti#10081 (Hatcher, §3.3).
name: The cap product

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ and an arbitrary open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, with no boundary regularity, the functions smooth on Ω are dense in W^{1,p}(Ω); higher orders remain (Meyers–Serrin 1964; Evans, §5.3.2).
name: The Meyers–Serrin theorem, first order

about: for an elliptic curve E over a finite field with q elements, (#E(𝔽_q) − q − 1)² ≤ 4q, the integer form of |#E(𝔽_q) − q − 1| ≤ 2√q, the point at infinity included; the proof computes deg(rπ − s) = qr² − a_q·rs + s², with a_q = q + 1 − #E(𝔽_q), on the pencil spanned by the Frobenius π and the identity and uses that a degree is never negative (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, V.1.1).
name: The Hasse bound

about: for every continuous injection Sⁿ⁻¹ → Sⁿ the complement of the image has exactly two path components, and more generally the complement of an embedded Sᵈ⁻¹ in Sⁿ has the [reduced singular homology](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/JordanBrouwer.html#TauCeti.reducedSingularHomologySphereComplRangeSphereIso) of Sⁿ⁻ᵈ; that each component has the embedded sphere as its frontier is not yet proved, and the statement is for spheres in spheres, not in ℝⁿ (Hatcher, Prop. 2B.1 and Cor. 2B.2).
name: The Jordan–Brouwer separation theorem

about: for simplicial sets K and L the Alexander–Whitney map C(K × L) → C(K) ⊗ C(L) and the shuffle map are inverse chain homotopy equivalences, both homotopies coming from acyclic models (the first in TauCeti#11903), and [the same holds](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/EilenbergZilber.html#TopCat.eilenbergZilberHomotopyEquiv) for the singular chains of a product of topological spaces; on unnormalized chains, with the Künneth theorem still to be derived (Eilenberg–Zilber 1953; Weibel, §8.5).
name: The Eilenberg–Zilber theorem

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K containing a primitive p-th root of unity, the maximal pro-p quotient G_K(p) of the absolute Galois group is a Demushkin group, that is, H¹(G_K(p), 𝔽_p) is finite, H²(G_K(p), 𝔽_p) is one-dimensional and the cup product H¹ × H¹ → H² is nondegenerate, and for a finite extension K of ℚ_p its [rank](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/ProP/Demushkin.html#TauCeti.demushkinRank_absoluteGaloisGroupProP) is [K:ℚ_p] + 2; the invariant q and the Demushkin character of G_K(p) are not yet identified, so Labute's classification does not yet give a presentation (Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, II §5.6, Thm 4).
name: Demushkin's theorem for local fields

about: for a bounded open subset Ω of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and bounded boundary values g, with no regularity of ∂Ω and no continuity of g, the supremum of the subharmonic functions that are continuous on the closure of Ω and ≤ g on ∂Ω is harmonic in Ω; with [Harnack's convergence theorem](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Harnack/Convergence.html#TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_iSup_of_monotone), that an increasing family of harmonic functions on a connected open set which is bounded at one point converges locally uniformly to a harmonic function; attainment of the boundary values through barriers is not yet proved (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thms 2.9 and 2.12).
name: Perron's method: the Perron solution is harmonic

about: every locally flat embedding f : Sⁿ → Sⁿ⁺¹ extends to an open embedding Sⁿ × ℝ → Sⁿ⁺¹ equal to f on Sⁿ × {0}, for every n ≥ 0; by the Jordan–Brouwer theorem above and the theorem that a locally bicollared compact connected hypersurface with disconnected complement is bicollared; the annulus theorem is not proved (Brown 1962).
name: Brown's bicollaring theorem for spheres

about: for a compact manifold M without boundary and an injective C² immersion f : M → V into a finite-dimensional real inner product space, there is ε > 0 such that (x, v) ↦ f(x) + v is an open embedding of the normal vectors of length < ε, and the whole normal bundle embeds as an open subset of any prescribed neighbourhood of f(M); with it, every C² knot in ℝ³ or S³ has a solid torus neighbourhood D² × S¹; the conclusions are topological, with no smooth structure on the normal bundle yet (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 6.24).
name: The tubular neighbourhood theorem for compact submanifolds of Euclidean space

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K, n invertible in K and a finite G_K-module A killed by n, with A′ = Hom(A, μₙ), the cup-product maps Hⁱ(G_K, A) → Hom(H²⁻ⁱ(G_K, A′), H²(G_K, μₙ)) are bijective for i = 0, 1, 2, starting from modules with trivial action over a field containing μₙ; the groups are the explicit cocycle models of H⁰, H¹ and H², and the transfer to the library's general continuous cohomology is still to come (Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, II §5.2, Thm 2; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (7.2.6)).
name: Local Tate duality, on explicit low-degree cochains

about: for a strongly noetherian Tate ring A and any ring of integral elements A⁺, the structure presheaf of Spa(A, A⁺) is a sheaf of complete topological rings, so a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring is sheafy; this is the case that the adic spaces entry of TauCeti#10656 left open; acyclicity in higher degrees and stable sheafiness are not yet proved (Huber; Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Thm 8.28(b)).
name: Strongly noetherian Tate rings are sheafy

about: for a geometrically reduced affine group G of finite type over a field and a normal closed subgroup scheme N, possibly nonreduced, the Hopf subalgebra of functions on G invariant under N represents the fppf sheaf quotient G/N, the kernel of G → G/N is exactly N, and 1 → N → G → G/N → 1 is exact; a nonreduced G is not covered (Waterhouse, *Introduction to Affine Group Schemes*, §16.3).
name: Quotients of affine algebraic groups by normal subgroups

about: the multiplicity of the Specht module S^λ in the permutation module M^μ of Sₙ on μ-tabloids, taken as dim Hom(S^λ, M^μ) over ℚ, is the Kostka number K_{λμ} counting semistandard tableaux of shape λ and content μ; equivalently the permutation character is ψ^μ = Σ_λ K_{λμ} χ^λ; no explicit decomposition isomorphism is constructed (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, Ch. 14).
name: Young's rule

about: for an idempotent e of a ring A with AeA = A, the functor M ↦ eM is an equivalence from A-modules to eAe-modules, with inverse N ↦ Hom_{eAe}(eA, N); the existence of such an e with basic corner ring for a finite-dimensional algebra is not proved (Lam, *Lectures on Modules and Rings*, §18).
name: Morita equivalence with the corner ring of a full idempotent

about: for a function field F/k of characteristic p and F′ = F(y) with yᵖ − y = u, where u is not of the form wᵖ − w, with constant fields k and k′: [k′:k]·(2g′ − 2) = p·(2g − 2) + (p − 1) Σ_P (m_P + 1) deg P, summed over the places P at which u has reduced pole order m_P prime to p; the reduced local representatives of u are hypotheses of the theorem, their existence in general not being formalized (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Prop. 3.7.8).
name: The Artin–Schreier genus formula

about: for a profinite group G, an open subgroup U, a closed subgroup V and a discrete G-module M, in every degree n the composite res ∘ cor : Hⁿ(U, M) → Hⁿ(G, M) → Hⁿ(V, M) is the sum over the double cosets VsU of the maps cor ∘ s_∗ ∘ res passing through Hⁿ(V ∩ sUs⁻¹, M) (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.5.6)).
name: The Mackey double coset formula for corestriction

about: for a unit q of a commutative ring R and a linearly ordered set of colours, the action of Bₙ on the free R-module on words of length n in which σᵢ applies Jimbo's R-matrix to the letters i, i + 1; it satisfies the Hecke relation T² = (q − q⁻¹)T + 1 and the [braid relation](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/KnotTheory/Jimbo/Basic.html#TauCeti.KnotTheory.jimboGenerator_braid) and is the permutation action at q = 1; Turaev's [weighted trace](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/KnotTheory/Jimbo/Trace.html#TauCeti.KnotTheory.jimboWeightedTrace) of it is invariant under conjugation and satisfies the unnormalized HOMFLY skein relation, but invariance under Markov stabilization, and hence a link invariant, is not yet proved (Jimbo 1986; Turaev 1988).
name: Jimbo's R-matrix representation of the braid group

about: for a Weierstrass curve W over a commutative ring R, the scheme Proj R[X, Y, Z]/(W) over Spec R, proper and with a zero section; it is [smooth of relative dimension one](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Smooth.html#WeierstrassCurve.smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_projModelOver) when the discriminant is a unit and integral when R is a domain; for an elliptic curve over a field K its K-points are identified with [the points](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Points.html#WeierstrassCurve.projModelPointsEquiv) of Mathlib's affine point type, and over a domain its function field is the fraction field of the affine coordinate ring; no group scheme structure yet (Katz–Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, §2.2).
name: The projective Weierstrass model of an elliptic curve

about: the power sums expand in the Schur polynomials with the character table of Sₙ as coefficients, p_ρ = Σ_λ χ^λ(ρ) s_λ, with inverse Σ_π χ^μ(π) p_{ρ(π)} = n!·s_μ; so over a field of characteristic zero the character of the Weyl module 𝕊^μ(kⁿ) at diag(t) is [s_μ(t)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/WeylModule/Character.html#TauCeti.char_weylRepOfShape_diagramOf_diagonal) for every partition μ, and the rational Weyl module of a dominant weight λ has [dimension ∏_{i<j}(λᵢ−λⱼ+j−i)/(j−i)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/WeylModule/Dimension.html#TauCeti.finrank_rationalWeylFDRep), with the hook-content form ∏_{(i,j)∈μ}(n+j−i)/hook(i,j); that this module is the irreducible of highest weight λ is not claimed (Macdonald I.7; Fulton–Harris Lecture 4, §15.3).
name: Frobenius's formula, and the characters of the Weyl modules of GLₙ are Schur polynomials

about: for a C² function with globally Lipschitz gradient on a finite-dimensional inner product space, the global stable and unstable sets of a nondegenerate critical point under the negative gradient flow are embedded C¹ submanifolds of dimensions n − ind and ind, with [manifold structures](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Calculus/Morse/Manifold.html#TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_stableSet_isManifold); where W^u(p) and W^s(q) meet transversally their [intersection](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Calculus/Morse/Transversality.html#TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_unstableSet_inter_stableSet_chart) is an embedded C¹ submanifold of dimension ind p − ind q and the index drops strictly along a connecting trajectory; and the earlier normed-space Morse lemma now holds [on a smooth manifold](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Morse/Lemma.html#TauCeti.IsManifoldNondegenerateCriticalPoint.nonempty_morseChart); the Morse complex is not yet built (Audin–Damian, Ch. 1–3).
name: The stable manifold theorem for gradient flows

about: for a chain complex X in a k-linear abelian category and an object Y, the sequence 0 → Ext¹(H_{i−1}(X), Y) → Hⁱ(Hom(X, Y)) → Hom(Hᵢ(X), Y) → 0 is exact and split whenever the cycle inclusions in degrees i and i−1 are split monomorphisms and the (i−1)-cycles are projective, as holds for degreewise projective complexes over a hereditary ring; the sequence is natural in X and Y, the splitting is not; the specialization to singular cochains over a PID is still to come (Hatcher Thm 3.2; Weibel 3.6.5).
name: The universal coefficient theorem for cohomology

about: for a bounded open Ω in a finite-dimensional inner product space and continuous g on ∂Ω, if every boundary point admits a barrier then the Perron solution is continuous on the closure and equals g on ∂Ω, so Δu = 0 in Ω, u = g on ∂Ω has a solution; in ℝⁿ, for every n, the [exterior sphere condition](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Perron/Barrier.html#TauCeti.exists_harmonicOnNhd_continuousOn_closure_eqOn_frontier_of_exterior_sphere) supplies barriers (the logarithmic one for n = 2, TauCeti#12607); this supplies the boundary attainment that the harmonicity of the Perron solution left open (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Lemma 2.13 and Thm 2.14).
name: Perron's method: the Dirichlet problem is solvable under the barrier condition

about: for a space of finite CW type, the alternating cell count of any finite CW complex homotopy equivalent to it is [independent of the model](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cellular/EulerCharacteristic/FiniteCWType.html#TauCeti.eulerChar_eq_cwEulerChar), equals the [alternating sum of the singular Betti numbers](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cellular/EulerCharacteristic/FiniteCWType.html#TauCeti.eulerChar_eq_finsum_finrank_singularHomology) over any division ring, and is invariant under homotopy equivalence; a finite discrete space has χ equal to its cardinality and a contractible space has χ = 1 (Hatcher Thm 2.44).
name: The Euler characteristic is a homotopy invariant

about: the weighted trace of Jimbo's R-matrix representation of the braid group, normalized by (qᴺ)^(−e) with e the exponent sum, is invariant under conjugation and both Markov stabilizations, hence constant on unframed Markov equivalence classes of braids, over any commutative ring with a unit q and with the quantum dimension as the value of the unknot; this closes the Markov invariance that Jimbo's representation and weighted trace left open, while the two-variable HOMFLY polynomial is not yet reconstructed (Turaev 1988; Jones 1987).
name: The slₙ specialization of HOMFLY is a Markov invariant

about: Reidemeister equivalent oriented link diagrams, as PD-codes, have ℤ[T, T⁻¹]-linearly equivalent Alexander modules and hence the same elementary ideals, so for a knot diagram the Alexander polynomial, the generator of E₁, is a Reidemeister invariant; Reidemeister's theorem linking diagrams to isotopy is not proved (Crowell–Fox Ch. VI–VII; Lickorish Ch. 6).
name: The Alexander module is an invariant of Reidemeister equivalence

about: [Hilbert's projective metric](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/BirkhoffContraction.html#TauCeti.hilbertProjectiveDist) d(x, y) = sup_{i,j} log(xᵢyⱼ/(yᵢxⱼ)) on positive vectors in ℝ^ι is a pseudometric vanishing exactly on proportional vectors, and a matrix K with strictly positive entries satisfies d(Kx, Ky) ≤ tanh(Δ(K)/4)·d(x, y), where Δ(K) = sup log(K_{ij}K_{i'j'}/(K_{ij'}K_{i'j})) is the projective diameter; the input to Sinkhorn convergence, which is not yet proved (Birkhoff 1957; Bushell 1973; Seneta Ch. 3).
name: Birkhoff's contraction theorem for Hilbert's projective metric

about: over a field of characteristic zero Der(𝕆) of the split octonions is a simple Lie algebra, so its Killing form is nondegenerate, and the Chevalley generators found earlier form a [Lie algebra basis](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Octonion/Simple.html#TauCeti.Octonion.lieBasis) with Cartan matrix of type G₂, so the root system of Der(𝕆) is of type G₂; the identification with Mathlib's Serre-presented 𝔤₂ remains (Fulton–Harris Lecture 22; Schafer Ch. III).
name: The derivation algebra of the octonions is the simple Lie algebra G₂

about: for K a finite extension of ℚ_p of degree N containing μ_p, the q-invariant of the Demushkin group G_K(p) is the number q(K) of p-power roots of unity in K and its canonical character is the cyclotomic character, so Labute's classification gives explicit presentations: for q(K) ≠ 2, G_K(p) ≅ ⟨x₁,…,x_{N+2} | x₁^{q(K)}(x₁,x₂)(x₃,x₄)⋯⟩; for p = 2 and [N odd](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/ProP/Marked.html#TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_odd), ⟨x | x₁²x₂⁴(x₂,x₃)(x₄,x₅)⋯⟩; for p = 2 and [N even](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/ProP/Marked.html#TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_of_degree_even), an even relator with parameters pinned by the image of the cyclotomic character; Demushkin's theorem gave the rank N + 2 but no presentation (Labute 1967, Thms 7–9; NSW 7.5.11–12).
name: Labute's presentations of the local Galois groups G_K(p)

about: over a field of characteristic zero, a geometrically connected affine group scheme of finite type whose Lie algebra has nondegenerate Killing form is linearly reductive: every finite-dimensional representation is [completely reducible](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/CompleteReducibility.html#TauCeti.Comodule.isCompletelyReducible_of_isKilling); this transports the library's Lie-algebra Weyl theorem through the identification of subrepresentations with Lie(G)-stable subspaces, and is the semisimple half of reductive ⇔ linearly reductive in characteristic zero (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 22.42).
name: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem for algebraic groups

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p containing no primitive p-th root of unity, the maximal pro-p quotient of the absolute Galois group is isomorphic as a topological group to the free pro-p group on [K:ℚ_p] + 1 generators; with Demushkin's theorem this is the Shafarevich–Demushkin dichotomy (Shafarevich 1947; Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, II §5.6 Thm 3; NSW 7.5.11).
name: Shafarevich's theorem: G_K(p) is free when K lacks μ_p

about: over a complete nonarchimedean field K the Tate algebra K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ of restricted power series in finitely many variables is a noetherian ring; hence every complete nonarchimedean normed field is a [strongly noetherian Tate ring](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Restricted/Noetherian.html#TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian.of_normedField), the hypothesis under which the structure presheaf of Spa was shown to be a sheaf (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert §5.2.6, Thm 1).
name: Tate algebras are noetherian

about: on a cylinder [0, T] × K with K compact in a finite-dimensional inner product space, a subsolution of ∂ₜu ≤ Δu + b·∇u, for any time-dependent drift b, that is continuous on the closed cylinder and C² in space and differentiable in time on the open cylinder is bounded by any bound it satisfies on the parabolic boundary ({0} × K) ∪ ([0, T] × ∂K); with the minimum and comparison principles and [uniqueness](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/MaximumPrinciple/Parabolic.html#TauCeti.eqOn_of_deriv_sub_laplacian_sub_fderiv_eq_of_eqOn_parabolicBoundary) for the initial-boundary value problem (Evans §2.3.3, Thms 4(i) and 5).
name: The weak maximum principle for the heat equation

about: for a number field and a finite set S of finite places, the S-unit group has ℤ-rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 + |S|, from a Dedekind-domain rank formula that needs only a finite class group and finitely generated units, so it extends Mathlib's Dirichlet unit theorem, the case S = ∅ (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII §4).
name: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K of characteristic zero and every prime ℓ, cd_ℓ G_K = 2, and for any nonarchimedean local field whenever ℓ is invertible in K (Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, II §5.3, Prop. 12).
name: The absolute Galois group of a p-adic field has cohomological dimension 2

about: in weight k ≥ 3 Mathlib's primitive residue-class Eisenstein series E_a, a ∈ (ℤ/N)², span a complement of the cusp forms, M_k(Γ(N)) = E_k(Γ(N)) ⊕ S_k(Γ(N)), because the constant term of E_a at a cusp detects whether a is ± the bottom row of the cusp's matrix; the passage to M_k(N, χ) and to the series E_k^{ψ,φ} is still to come (Diamond–Shurman Thm 4.2.3).
name: The cusp–Eisenstein decomposition of M_k(Γ(N))

about: for a commutative cocommutative Hopf algebra H over a commutative ring R, finite projective of constant rank n, every A-valued point of Spec H satisfies xⁿ = 1 in the convolution group, for every commutative R-algebra A, by Deligne's norm argument on the Cartier dual; the restatement for group schemes over a non-affine base is not yet made (Tate–Oort 1970, §1).
name: Deligne's theorem: a finite locally free commutative group scheme is killed by its rank

about: over an ordered field with 2 invertible the signature is a ring homomorphism from the Witt ring of regular quadratic forms to ℤ, and over an ordered real closed field, in particular ℝ, it is a ring isomorphism W(K) ≅ ℤ with inverse the integer cast, so two regular forms are Witt equivalent exactly when their signatures agree (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, II §3).
name: The Witt ring of a real closed field is ℤ

about: every nondegenerate finite quadratic module is isometric to an orthogonal sum of Nikulin's generators: the odd cyclic forms q_θ^{(p)}(p^k), the dyadic cyclic forms q_θ^{(2)}(2^k), and the rank-two forms u^{(2)}(2^k) and v^{(2)}(2^k); the relations among the generators, which turn this into a classification, are not treated (Nikulin, Prop. 1.8.1; Wall 1963).
name: Nikulin's decomposition of nondegenerate finite quadratic forms

about: the analytic realization of a nonempty regular fan is compact exactly when the cones cover the real vector space, and the analytic map of a morphism of regular fans with nonempty source is [proper](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Toric/Analytic/Fan/Map/Proper.html#TauCeti.Toric.FanHom.isProperMap_analyticMap_iff) exactly when for every target cone τ the inverse image f_ℝ⁻¹(τ) is the union of the source cones mapped into τ; smooth fans and the analytic topology only (Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §2.4).
name: A toric variety is compact exactly when its fan is complete

about: for a finite extension L/K of number fields the canonical maps 𝔸_K ⊗_K L → 𝔸_L and 𝔸_K^f ⊗_K L → 𝔸_L^f are isomorphisms of topological 𝔸_K-algebras; and for Galois L/K the adeles and ideles of K are exactly the [Gal(L/K)-fixed](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/Adeles/GaloisDescent.html#TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.mem_range_adeleExtension_iff) adeles and ideles of L (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II (8.3); Cassels–Fröhlich II §14).
name: Base change and Galois descent for adeles

about: for an exact divisor Q of N the Atkin–Lehner matrix normalizes Γ₁(N), giving operators W_Q on M_k(Γ₁(N)) and S_k(Γ₁(N)) with W_Q∘⟨d⟩ = ⟨ι_Q d⟩∘W_Q, where ι_Q inverts the residue of d modulo Q; so W_Q [carries M_k(N, χ) to M_k(N, χ∘ι_Q)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/AtkinLehner/Gamma1.html#TauCeti.atkinLehnerOperatorGamma1_mem_modFormCharSpace), that is χ_Q·χ_{N/Q} ↦ χ̄_Q·χ_{N/Q}, which is why newforms of general nebentypus have pseudo-eigenvalues rather than eigenvalues; those are not yet defined (Atkin–Li, Invent. Math. 48 (1978), §1).
name: The Atkin–Lehner operators on Γ₁(N) and the Atkin–Li character shift

about: for A a commutative ring, B a finite projective A-algebra and C a finitely presented B-algebra, the functor T ↦ Hom_B(C, B ⊗_A T) on A-algebras is represented by an A-algebra of finite presentation, and its formation [commutes with arbitrary base change](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/WeilRestriction.html#TauCeti.Algebra.WeilRestriction.baseChangeAlgEquiv) A → A'; the affine case of restriction of scalars, the non-affine base being separate (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, *Néron Models*, §7.6; Stacks 05Y8).
name: Weil restriction along a finite locally free algebra is representable

about: for a C³ map u : ℂ → V solving ∂ₜu = J(u)∂ₛu, with J a C² matrix-valued almost complex structure bounded with its first two derivatives along u by a, b, c, the energy density satisfies Δ‖∂ₛu‖² ≥ −A‖∂ₛu‖⁴ with A = 4ac + 2b² + 8a²b², and if 8A∫_{B_r(z₀)}‖∂ₛu‖² < π then πr²‖∂ₛu(z₀)‖² ≤ 8∫_{B_r(z₀)}‖∂ₛu‖², the ε-regularity estimate behind bubbling; Gromov compactness is not proved (McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, §4.3).
name: The mean-value inequality for J-holomorphic curves

about: over a perfect exact constant field, a function field of genus one has, at every place of degree one, Weierstrass coordinates whose Weierstrass curve is nonsingular, because a rational singular point would make the slope generate the field and force genus zero; over an imperfect field the singular point need not be rational and nothing is claimed (Stichtenoth Prop. 6.1.2; Silverman III.1.4).
name: A genus-one function field with a rational place is elliptic

about: K_t(x) = (4πt)^{−n/2} exp(−‖x‖²/4t) on a finite-dimensional real inner product space is smooth, positive and of mass one, solves ∂ₜK = ΔK, satisfies the [semigroup identity](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HeatKernel/Basic.html#TauCeti.heatKernel_convolution_heatKernel) K_t ⋆ K_s = K_{t+s} and has [Fourier transform](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HeatKernel/Basic.html#TauCeti.fourier_heatKernel) exp(−4π²t‖ξ‖²); it is an [approximate identity](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HeatKernel/ApproximateIdentity.html#TauCeti.tendsto_heatKernel_convolution): for a.e.-bounded measurable g continuous at x₀, (K_t ⋆ g)(x) → g(x₀) as (t, x) → (0⁺, x₀), uniformly for bounded uniformly continuous g; the interior equation for K_t ⋆ g is still to come (Evans §2.3.1; Stein–Weiss I.1.13).
name: The heat kernel

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K, the subgroup W_K ⊂ G_K of elements acting on K^ur as an integral power of Frobenius, dense and proper in G_K, with the exact sequence 1 → I_K → W_K → ℤ → 1 given by the [degree](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/WeilGroup/Basic.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.weilDegree); the Weil topology, the unique group topology making profinite inertia an open subgroup, makes W_K a [locally compact](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/WeilGroup/Topology.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.instLocallyCompactSpaceWeilGroup) totally disconnected [non-compact](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/WeilGroup/Topology.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.not_compactSpace_weilGroup) group, its inclusion into G_K continuous but not an embedding; the reciprocity isomorphism Kˣ ≅ W_K^ab is not yet proved (Tate, *Number theoretic background*, §1.4).
name: The local Weil group and its Weil topology

about: the conductor exponent of a finite separable extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, the least n with U(K, n) ⊆ N(Lˣ), the conductor ideal 𝔪_K^n, and the conductor exponent of a continuous character Kˣ → ℂˣ, the least n with U(K, n) in its kernel, attained because ℂˣ has no small subgroups; an unramified extension has conductor exponent 0, and a finite abelian extension has [conductor exponent 0 exactly when it is unramified](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Local/Conductor.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.conductorExponent_eq_zero_iff), by local reciprocity (Serre, *Local Fields*, XV §2).
name: Local conductors

about: geodesic spaces satisfying the Bruhat–Tits CN inequality d(z, m)² ≤ (d(z, x)² + d(z, y)²)/2 − d(x, y)²/4 at every midpoint m of x and y, with real inner product spaces as instances; the squared distance is 2d(x, y)²-strongly convex along every geodesic segment, so a nonzero measure on a CAT(0) metric space has [at most one quadratic Fréchet barycenter](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/FrechetMean/CATZero.html#TauCeti.subsingleton_frechetBarycenters_two), a barycenter being a minimizer of finite Fréchet functional; the midpoint-to-segment step is [Jensen's theorem](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/Midpoint.html#TauCeti.convexOn_of_midpoint) that a continuous midpoint-convex function on a convex set is convex (Bridson–Haefliger II.1; Sturm 2003, §4).
name: CAT(0) spaces

about: a Weierstrass curve over a field of characteristic p is supersingular when it has no nonzero p-torsion over the algebraic closure, and ordinary otherwise; the property is invariant under arbitrary field extension and change of variables, the algebraic rather than separable closure being essential over imperfect fields, and in characteristic [2 and 3](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Supersingular.html#WeierstrassCurve.isSupersingular_iff_j_eq_zero_of_char_three) an elliptic curve is supersingular exactly when j = 0; the Frobenius-trace criterion over finite fields is not yet proved (Silverman V.3.1, V.4.1).
name: Supersingular and ordinary elliptic curves

about: uncurved nonunital A∞-categories on graded linear quivers over a commutative ring, stored as an A∞-algebra on the total Hom module whose operations are path-compatible, with the operations mₙ on composable strings of degree 2 − n satisfying the Stasheff identities, the Hom differential m₁ with d² = 0, the composition m₂ with the Leibniz rule, and the one-object A∞-category of an A∞-algebra; A∞-functors are not yet defined (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §§3.1, 7.1).
name: A∞-categories

about: the homology cross product Hₚ(X; R) ⊗ H_q(Y; S) → H_{p+q}(X × Y; R ⊗ S) via the shuffle map, agreeing under the Eilenberg–Zilber isomorphism with the cross product of the singular chain complexes, and the cohomology cross product via Alexander–Whitney, natural in both spaces and coefficients, with the cup product as the diagonal pullback of the cross product; the Künneth isomorphism over a field is not yet proved (Hatcher §3.2, §3.B).
name: Cross products in singular homology and cohomology

about: every finite set of real polynomials in n variables admits a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of ℝⁿ on each of whose cells all of them are sign-invariant (Collins's induction, with Thom's lemma supplying the semialgebraicity of the stacks); as a corollary, [the projection ℝⁿ⁺¹ → ℝⁿ carries semialgebraic sets to semialgebraic sets](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/RealAlgebraic/CAD/Existence.html#TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic.image_tail), the geometric form of the Tarski–Seidenberg theorem, with quantifier elimination for ordered-ring formulas as the next step (Basu–Pollack–Roy, *Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry*, §5.1).
name: Existence of cylindrical algebraic decompositions, and projection closure of semialgebraic sets

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p, every subgroup of finite index in Kˣ is the norm group N_{L/K}(Lˣ) of a finite abelian extension L/K, and [in any characteristic](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/LocalExistence/Existence.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.localAbelianExistence_primeToResidueCharacteristic) the same holds for subgroups of index prime to the residue characteristic; the proof goes through norm limitation, the reciprocity map and Kummer theory with the Hilbert symbol, with no Lubin–Tate input (Serre, *Local Fields*, XIV §6).
name: The existence theorem of local class field theory

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a finite discrete Galois module A killed by any n ≥ 1, the cup-product pairing H^i(G_K, A^∨(1)) × H^{2−i}(G_K, A) → H²(G_K, μ_n) ≅ ℤ/n is perfect, and [over any nonarchimedean local field](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Local/Duality/Perfect.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.tateDualityPairing_perfect) the same holds for n invertible in K; this upgrades the duality on explicit low-degree cochains of TauCeti#12075 to full perfectness for every finite coefficient module (Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, II §5.2, Theorem 2).
name: Local Tate duality, for every finite Galois module

about: a positive definite integral lattice L of rank n satisfies min L ≤ (4/3)^{(n−1)/2} (det L)^{1/n}, with [equality attained by the root lattice A₂](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeA/Hermite.html#TauCeti.IntegralLattice.minimum_typeARootLattice_two_eq_rpow_mul_determinant_rpow); the proof is Hermite's induction on the rank, carried out entirely in ℤ by way of [Chiò's condensation](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Condensation.html#Matrix.mul_det_condensation_eq_pow_mul_det) A₀₀·det A′ = A₀₀ⁿ·det A, proved over any commutative ring (Cassels, *Geometry of Numbers*; Conway–Sloane, Ch. 2).
name: Hermite's inequality for the minimum of a positive definite lattice

about: every submodule of a free module over a PID is free, with no finite-generation or finite-rank hypothesis; Mathlib has the finite-rank case, and this is the general statement, proved by well-ordering a basis and choosing pivots for the principal ideals of leading coordinates (Lang, *Algebra*, III, Theorem 7.1).
name: Submodules of free modules over a principal ideal domain are free

about: for a polarized four-dimensional quadratic space over a field of characteristic not 2, the Spin group is isomorphic to SL₂(K) × SL₂(K), and under such an isomorphism the even and odd half-spin representations are the standard representations of the first and second factors; [over a field in which every element is a square](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Spin/Exceptional/Four/Group.html#TauCeti.nonempty_spinGroup_mulEquiv_specialLinearGroup_prod_of_finrank_eq_four_of_forall_isSquare) every nondegenerate quaternary form qualifies, following the Spin₃ ≅ SL₂ identification of TauCeti#6167 (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Lecture 20).
name: Spin₄ ≅ SL₂ × SL₂, with the half-spin representations

about: over an A∞-algebra A with a strict unit e, evaluation at e is a homotopy equivalence from the morphism complex Hom(A, M) out of the free rank-one right A∞-module to the underlying complex (M, m₁) of any right A∞-module M with m₂(x, e) = x, with homotopy inverse the Yoneda cochains x ↦ (m_{n+1}(x, −))ₙ, over any commutative ring (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §4).
name: The Yoneda lemma for A∞-modules

about: for an odd prime p, G_{ℚ_p(μ_p)}(p) is the pro-p group on generators x₁, …, x_{p+1} with the single relation x₁^p [x₁,x₂] ⋯ [x_p,x_{p+1}] = 1, and the cyclotomic character takes the value (1−p)⁻¹ on x₂ and 1 on every other generator; this is the arithmetic instance of the Labute classification of Demushkin groups of TauCeti#10321 (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, 7.5.12).
name: The maximal pro-p quotient of the absolute Galois group of ℚ_p(μ_p) is a Demushkin group on p+1 generators

about: the automorphism group scheme Aut(Mₙ) represents the fppf sheaf quotient of GLₙ by the kernel of the conjugation action over every commutative ring, and over a field the fppf quotient GLₙ/Z(GLₙ), with the quotient map the conjugation homomorphism; the input is a [local Skolem–Noether theorem](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/ProjectiveGeneralLinear/Quotient.html#TauCeti.ProjectiveGeneralLinear.kernelFppfQuotientIso): every algebra automorphism of Mₙ(A), for any commutative ring A, is inner Zariski-locally on Spec A, hence inner over every local ring (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*; Knus–Ojanguren, LNM 389, Ch. IV).
name: PGLₙ represents the fppf quotient of GLₙ by its centre

about: on an arbitrary scheme X, a quasi-coherent sheaf has a left dual, equivalently a right dual, in the symmetric monoidal category QCoh(X) if and only if it is locally free of finite rank, the dual being the internal Hom into 𝒪_X (Brandenburg, *Tensor categorical foundations of algebraic geometry*, Prop. 4.7.5).
name: A quasi-coherent sheaf is dualizable exactly when it is finite locally free

about: every Riemannian isometry of the unit sphere Sⁿ in a finite-dimensional real inner product space is the restriction of a unique orthogonal linear map, so Isom(Sⁿ) ≅ O(n+1), including the two-point sphere S⁰ (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Prop. 5.22).
name: The isometry group of the round sphere is the orthogonal group

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K and a prime ℓ invertible in K, scd_ℓ(G_K) = 2, so for K/ℚ_p finite this holds for every ℓ; the ordinary cohomological dimension cd_ℓ(G_K) = 2 is TauCeti#12282, and the strict version is proved from it through local Tate duality and the integral Bockstein sequences (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, 7.2.5).
name: The strict cohomological dimension of a p-adic Galois group is 2

about: for a newform f of level N and arbitrary nebentypus χ, the normalized Fricke operator sends f to λ_N(f)·f_ρ, where f_ρ is the conjugate newform (nebentypus χ⁻¹, conjugate Fourier coefficients) and the Atkin–Li pseudo-eigenvalue λ_N(f) has [modulus one](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/Fricke.html#HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.norm_frickePseudoEigenvalue), reducing to the Fricke sign when χ is trivial (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Theorem 4.6.15; Atkin–Li, Invent. Math. 48, 1978).
name: The Fricke pseudo-eigenvalue of a newform with general nebentypus

about: a nonsingular matrix over a free algebra K over an infinite field F that intertwines two families of matrices over F can be replaced by a nonsingular intertwining matrix over F; the application is [Tate's lemma](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Lattice.html#TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_eq_of_isBaseChange) that two ℤ-free representations of a finite cyclic group which are lattices in the same real representation have equal Herbrand quotients, the step that compares the S-unit lattice with a permutation lattice in the fundamental inequalities (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII; Curtis–Reiner §29).
name: The Noether–Deuring theorem in matrix form, and Tate's lattice lemma for Herbrand quotients

about: every complex Dirichlet character modulo n gives a finite-order Hecke character of ℚ, injectively and compatibly with change of level, its finite conductor is generated by the Dirichlet conductor and its infinite conductor is empty exactly when the character is even; conversely every finite-order Hecke character of ℚ has a unique primitive Dirichlet representative at its finite conductor (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VII §6).
name: Dirichlet characters are the finite-order Hecke characters of ℚ

about: for a finite quiver without sinks, left multiplication by any arrow is injective on e_vΠ over every commutative ring, so the complex 0 → e_vΠ → ⊕ e_iΠ → e_vΠ → S_v → 0 is a projective resolution of each vertex simple; since a connected graph has a sink-free orientation exactly when it contains a cycle, this covers every connected non-tree graph, including the affine Ãₙ, and is proved with Bergman's diamond lemma (Etingof–Eu, *Koszulity and the Hilbert series of preprojective algebras*, 2007).
name: The Koszul resolution of the simple modules of a preprojective algebra, for graphs with a cycle
