about: a map into a finite-dimensional complex vector space that is continuous on the closed upper part of a conjugation-symmetric domain, holomorphic on its open upper part, and takes values on the real axis in an affine translate of a maximal totally real subspace extends analytically across the real axis, hence is smooth up to the boundary; this is the linear-boundary case of the boundary regularity used for J-holomorphic discs (McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, App. B).
name: Schwarz reflection for maps with a totally real boundary condition

about: an order O in a number field is Gorenstein when its codifferent, the trace dual of O packaged as a fractional ideal, is invertible; for such an order [a fractional ideal is proper (its multiplier ring is O) if and only if it is invertible](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/Orders/Gorenstein.html#TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder.isProperFractionalIdeal_iff_isUnit_of_isGorenstein), and conversely O is Gorenstein exactly when every proper fractional ideal is invertible; maximal orders and monogenic orders ℤ[x] are Gorenstein (Buchmann–Lenstra, §2; Kopp–Lagarias, *Class field theory for orders of number fields*, §2).
name: Gorenstein orders in number fields

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the open subgroups of finite index in Kˣ and the finite abelian extensions of K are in the usual order-reversing bijection, the subgroup attached to L being N_{L/K}(Lˣ), so [two abelian extensions with the same norm group coincide](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/LocalExistence/Correspondence.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.localClassField_unique), and in every characteristic the same holds for index prime to the residue characteristic; the absolute local Artin map is [injective](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/LocalExistence/ArtinMap.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.injective_artinMap) and extends to an [isomorphism of topological groups](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/LocalExistence/ArtinMap.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.profiniteCompletionArtinEquiv) from the profinite completion of Kˣ onto G_K^ab, all deduced from the existence theorem of TauCeti#12809 (Serre, *Local Fields*, XIV §6; Milne, *Class Field Theory*, I §1).
name: The local class field correspondence, and (Kˣ)^ ≅ G_K^ab

about: every first-order formula of ordered rings with parameters from ℝ is equivalent, under every assignment of its free variables, to a quantifier-free formula, so the [semialgebraic subsets of ℝⁿ are exactly the definable ones](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/RealAlgebraic/Semialgebraic/QuantifierElimination.html#TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_iff_definable) and images and compositions of semialgebraic maps are semialgebraic; the projection-closure hypothesis these results carried is now [discharged over ℝ](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/RealAlgebraic/CAD/Existence.html#TauCeti.instHasSemialgebraicProjectionsReal) by the cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition proof of Tarski–Seidenberg of TauCeti#11891 (Bochnak–Coste–Roy, *Real Algebraic Geometry*, §2.2).
name: Quantifier elimination for the real field

about: every upper ramification break of a finite abelian Galois extension of nonarchimedean local fields is an integer: a break is detected in a cyclic subextension, survives passage to the residue-characteristic-primary part of its Galois group, and the cyclic prime-power case is the norm-conductor induction along the prime-order series (Serre, *Local Fields*, V §7).
name: The Hasse–Arf theorem

about: an integrable f : ℝⁿ → E, at any height t > 0, is g + Σ_Q b_Q over a family of pairwise disjoint [dyadic cubes](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/CalderonZygmund/Decomposition.html#TauCeti.calderonZygmundCubes) Q on which the average of ‖f‖ lies in (t, 2ⁿt], with t·|⋃Q| ≤ ∫_{⋃Q}‖f‖, [‖g‖ ≤ 2ⁿt a.e.](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/CalderonZygmund/Decomposition.html#TauCeti.ae_enorm_calderonZygmundGood_le) and ‖g‖₁ ≤ ‖f‖₁, and each b_Q supported on Q with mean zero and ‖b_Q‖₁ ≤ 2∫_Q‖f‖; the singular-integral theorem it serves is still to come (Stein, *Singular Integrals*, I §3).
name: The Calderón–Zygmund decomposition

about: the Künneth map ⊕_{p+q=n} Hₚ(K) ⊗ H_q(L) → Hₙ(K ⊗ L), assembled from the homology cross products and natural in both complexes, is an isomorphism whenever K and L are homotopy equivalent to complexes with zero differential, which [every complex of semisimple modules is](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Semisimple.html#HomologicalComplex.exists_homotopyEquiv_d_eq_zero), complexes of vector spaces over a division ring included; the topological Künneth theorem for singular homology is not yet proved (Weibel, §§1.4, 3.6).
name: The Künneth theorem for chain complexes over a field

about: for every natural number N, Σ_{r<N} e^{2πi r²/N} = ((1+i)/2)(1+(−i)^N)√N, the phase and not only the square that Mathlib has; it is the input to [Nikulin's Gauss-sum invariant](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/OddCyclic/GaussSum.html#TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.gaussSign_oddCyclic) of the odd cyclic generators, sign q_θ^{(p)}(p^k) ≡ k²(1−p) + 4kη (mod 8) with (θ/p) = (−1)^η (Berndt–Evans–Williams, *Gauss and Jacobi Sums*, Ch. 1; Nikulin, Prop. 1.11.2).
name: Gauss's evaluation of the quadratic Gauss sum

about: an analytic relation R ⊆ X × Y, with X a T₁ space and Y a Borel space, has a uniformizing function f : X → Y, measurable for the σ-algebra generated by the analytic subsets of X, with (x, f(x)) ∈ R for every x in the projection of R; relative to an s-finite measure on a metrizable X there is a [measurable choice](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Uniformization.html#MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet.exists_measurable_ae_uniformization) valid at almost every point of the projection (Kechris, *Classical Descriptive Set Theory*, 18.1).
name: The Jankov–von Neumann uniformization theorem

about: for probability measures μ, ν on any measurable space, the relative entropy is D(μ‖ν) = sup_f (∫f dμ − log ∫e^f dν) over bounded measurable f, with the finite-measure form sup_f (∫f dμ − ∫(e^f − 1) dν) carrying Mathlib's mass correction, and bounded continuous f suffice on a pseudometrizable Borel space; hence (μ, ν) ↦ D(μ‖ν) is [jointly lower semicontinuous](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler/Variational.html#TauCeti.lowerSemicontinuous_klDiv_probabilityMeasure) for the weak topology (Dembo–Zeitouni, Lemma 6.2.13).
name: The Donsker–Varadhan variational formula

about: the successive minima λ₀, …, λ_{n−1} of a positive definite integral lattice L of rank n, measured as norms β(x, x), satisfy ∏ᵢλᵢ ≤ cₙⁿ·det L with cₙ = (4/π)Γ(n/2+1)^{2/n}, and in particular [min L ≤ cₙ(det L)^{1/n}](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/PosDef/Minkowski.html#TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.minimum_le_mul_determinant_rpow), by the convex body theorem applied to a realization of L in ℝⁿ; the lower bound of the second theorem is not proved. Every positive semidefinite lattice has a [Minkowski-reduced basis](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/PosDef/Reduction.html#TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosSemidef.exists_isMinkowskiReduced) (Cassels, *Geometry of Numbers*, VIII).
name: Minkowski's second theorem for positive definite lattices

about: for a stably uniform Tate ring A and A⁺ a ring of power-bounded elements containing a ring of definition, the structure presheaf of Spa(A, A⁺) is a sheaf of complete topological rings, with no noetherian hypothesis, so a [complete Hausdorff stably uniform Tate ring is sheafy](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/StructurePresheaf/Rational/StableUniform.html#TauCeti.Huber.isSheafyRing_of_isStablyUniform); alongside it, a [strongly noetherian Tate ring is stably sheafy](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/StructurePresheaf/StronglyNoetherian.html#TauCeti.Huber.isStablySheafyRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian), every complete Hausdorff Huber ring topologically of finite type over it being sheafy (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, *Stably uniform affinoids are sheafy*, Thm 7; Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Cor. 8.35).
name: The Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem

about: for a lower semicontinuous cost c on a product of Polish spaces with an integrable split upper bound c(x, y) ≤ c_X(x) + c_Y(y), the dual problem is attained by integrable potentials (φ, ψ), feasible on a product of sets of full measure, and every optimal plan is [concentrated on their contact set](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Duality/BoundedAbove.html#TauCeti.IsOptimalCoupling.exists_ae_mem_dualContactSet_of_le_add); more generally an [optimal plan of finite cost for any lower semicontinuous cost is concentrated on a Borel c-cyclically monotone set](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Duality/CyclicalMonotonicity.html#TauCeti.IsOptimalCoupling.exists_isCyclicallyMonotone_of_lowerSemicontinuous), beyond the equality of primal and dual values announced earlier (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 5.10 (ii), (iii)).
name: Kantorovich dual attainment, and the cyclical monotonicity of optimal plans

about: in singular cohomology with coefficients in a symmetric monoidal linear category, b ⌣ a = (−1)^{pq} a ⌣ b for a of degree p and b of degree q, the two products formed along coefficient data that agree up to the braiding, in particular for a [commutative pairing on the coefficients](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/GradedCommutativity.html#TopCat.singularCup_gradedComm_tensorUnit); the substance is an acyclic-models chain homotopy between the Alexander–Whitney map followed by the Koszul braiding and the swap of factors (Hatcher, Thm 3.11).
name: Graded commutativity of the cup product

about: a one-dimensional formal group law F over a ℚ-algebra has a normalized [invariant differential](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Logarithm.html#FormalGroup.invariantDifferential) ω = P(T)dT, and its logarithm log_F = ∫ω satisfies [log_F(F(X, Y)) = log_F(X) + log_F(Y)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Logarithm.html#FormalGroup.subst_toPowerSeries_log), the additive power series along F being exactly its multiples; with the exponential as compositional inverse, F(X, Y) = exp_F(log_F X + log_F Y), so F is strictly isomorphic to the additive formal group; stated for Mathlib's `FormalGroup`, hence for the formal group of an elliptic curve (Silverman, *AEC*, IV.4.2, IV.5.2).
name: The formal logarithm of a formal group law

about: the compact real Spin group of a definite form is simply connected in every dimension at least three: Spin(3) is the unit quaternion sphere S³, and the sphere bundle Spin(n) → Spin(n+1) → Sⁿ, trivialized over two antipodal punctured spheres whose overlap retracts to the equator, carries the induction by a two-set van Kampen argument; this upgrades the path-connectedness announced earlier (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).
name: Compact Spin(n) is simply connected for n ≥ 3

about: for a nondegenerate quadratic form Q on a five-dimensional space, an isomorphism C₀(Q) ≅ M₄(K) carrying Clifford reversal to the symplectic adjoint X ↦ −JXᵀJ identifies Spin(Q) with Sp₄(K), and [such a splitting exists over every separably closed extension](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/LowRank/Symplectic.html#CliffordAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_reverseEven_baseChange_eq_neg_J_mul_transpose_mul_J), so reversal is a symplectic involution and Spin(Q) is the group of K-points of a twisted form of Sp₄; in signature (2,1), [Spin(2,1) ≅ SL₂(ℝ)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/Real/TwoOne.html#TauCeti.realSpinTwoOneEquivSpecialLinear) with the vector action becoming X ↦ AXAᵀ on symmetric matrices, following the Spin₃ ≅ SL₂ and Spin₄ ≅ SL₂ × SL₂ identifications of TauCeti#6167 and TauCeti#12783 (Knus–Merkurjev–Rost–Tignol, *The Book of Involutions*, §15.C).
name: Spin₅ ≅ Sp₄, and Spin(2,1) ≅ SL₂(ℝ)

about: for a finite group G and a field k of characteristic p, every class x in the Grothendieck group G₀(k[G]) of finitely generated modules has a positive multiple, |G|·x in fact, in the subgroup generated by the classes induced from cyclic subgroups of order prime to p; it rests on [Artin's identity |G|·1 = Σ_C a_C|C|·Ind_C 1 in G₀(k[G])](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/GroupAlgebra/Artin.html#TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_one_eq_sum_artinCoeff_indK0), the characteristic-zero Artin induction announced earlier now holding over every field (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, 7.3.4; Milne, *Arithmetic Duality Theorems*, I 2.10).
name: The modular Artin induction theorem

about: for an elliptic curve W over a field of exponential characteristic p, possibly imperfect, the [Verschiebung](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/RelativeFrobenius/Verschiebung.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.verschiebungIsogeny) V : W⁽ᵖ⁾ → W is the unique isogeny with V∘F_{W/F} = [p], of degree p and with F_{W/F}∘V = [p] on the twist; W is supersingular exactly when V is purely inseparable, equivalently when [p] has separable degree 1, and for p prime [ordinary exactly when V is separable](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/RelativeFrobenius/Supersingular.html#WeierstrassCurve.isOrdinary_iff_isSeparable_verschiebungIsogeny), the criterion left open when the dichotomy was announced with TauCeti#12532; the finite-field trace criterion is still to come (Silverman, III.6.1, V.3.1).
name: The Verschiebung, and supersingularity as its pure inseparability

about: for g measurable and essentially bounded on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, with values in a Banach space, u(t, x) = (K_t ⋆ g)(x) is [smooth in x](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HeatKernel/HeatEquation.html#TauCeti.contDiff_heatKernel_convolution) for t > 0 and satisfies ∂ₜu = Δu = ΔK_t ⋆ g, so with the approximate-identity limit of TauCeti#12494 it is a classical solution of the Cauchy problem ∂ₜu = Δu, u(0, ·) = g, the interior equation left open when the heat kernel was announced (Evans, §2.3.1, Thm 1).
name: The heat kernel solves the heat equation

about: on E × (0, ∞), E a finite-dimensional real inner product space, the metric (‖dx‖² + dt²)/t² is complete, its Levi-Civita connection on constant fields is ∇ᵤv = (⟨u, v⟩eₜ − uₜv − vₜu)/t, its [curvature tensor is R(u, v)w = −(⟨v, w⟩u − ⟨u, w⟩v)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Hyperbolic/UpperHalfSpace/Curvature.html#TauCeti.UpperHalfSpace.curvatureTensor_eq), so every tangent 2-plane has [sectional curvature −1](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Hyperbolic/UpperHalfSpace/Curvature.html#TauCeti.UpperHalfSpace.hasConstantSectionalCurvature), and it is packaged as a complete hyperbolic metric on ℍⁿ; Mostow rigidity is the open target it serves (Lee, *Riemannian Manifolds*, Thm 8.34).
name: The upper half-space model of hyperbolic space

about: for a finite group G and a field k of characteristic p, every class x in the Grothendieck group G₀(k[G]) of finitely generated modules has a positive multiple, |G|·x in fact, in the subgroup generated by the classes induced from cyclic subgroups of order prime to p; it rests on [Artin's identity |G|·1 = Σ_C a_C|C|·Ind_C 1 in G₀(k[G])](https://cbirkbeck.github.io/tauceti-reviewed-by-test/#/d/TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_one_eq_sum_artinCoeff_indK0), the characteristic-zero Artin induction announced earlier now holding over every field (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, 7.3.4; Milne, *Arithmetic Duality Theorems*, I 2.10).
name: The modular Artin induction theorem

about: over a principal ideal domain k of characteristic zero in which every prime number is a unit or generates a maximal ideal (ℤ, ℤ_p, ℤ_(p), a field), a representation A of a finite group G whose Tate cohomology Ĥⁿ(S, A) vanishes for every subgroup S and every n ∈ ℤ has projective dimension at most one over k[G]: the kernel of any surjection from a projective module onto A is projective, and [A itself is projective when its underlying k-module is](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Projective.html#Rep.projective_of_isZero_res); conversely [projective dimension at most one implies cohomological triviality](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Projective.html#Rep.isZero_res_of_exact) over any commutative ring (Serre, *Local Fields*, IX §§3–5; Rim, Ann. of Math. 69, 1959).
name: The Nakayama–Rim theorem

about: an algebraic function field F = k(x, y) with exact constant field has g(F) ≤ ([F : k(x)] − 1)([F : k(y)] − 1), the case F₀ = k(x) of the [bound g(F) ≤ 1 + [F : F₀](g(F₀) − 1) + deg C](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/RiemannInequality.html#TauCeti.genus_le_one_add_finrank_mul_genus_sub_one_add_degree) valid whenever a basis of F/F₀ lies in L(C); no separability or perfectness is needed, and Castelnuovo's inequality is the next item (Stichtenoth, Cor. 3.11.4).
name: Riemann's inequality for the genus of k(x, y)

about: for f : [a, b] → V with f(a) = f(b), V a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and f' ∈ L², ∫‖f − ⨍f‖² ≤ ((b − a)/2π)²∫‖f'‖², the sharp periodic form proved by Parseval, distinct from the Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality on convex domains announced earlier; hence for a symplectic form compatible with the inner product the [symplectic area of a loop](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Isoperimetric.html#TauCeti.SymplecticForm.abs_integral_apply_le) is at most (b − a)/(2π) times its energy ∫‖γ'‖², the input to removal of singularities for J-holomorphic curves (Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya, *Inequalities*, §7.7; McDuff–Salamon, §4.4).
name: Wirtinger's inequality, and the symplectic isoperimetric inequality

about: for a regular quadratic form class q of rank n over a field with 2 invertible, the comparison ι : Br(K)[2] ≅ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂) sends the Clifford invariant to w₂(q) + C(n−1, 2)·(−1)∪w₁(q) + C(n+1, 4)·(−1)∪(−1), with w₁(q) the Kummer class of the discriminant; the Clifford invariant is [additive on the square of the fundamental ideal](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/RegularFormClass/Clifford.html#TauCeti.RegularFormClass.cliffordInvariant_add_of_signedDiscr_eq_zero) of the Witt ring and [descends to a homomorphism I²/I³ → Br(K)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Witt/Clifford.html#TauCeti.cliffordHomI2Bar), the invariant e₂ whose injectivity is Merkurjev's theorem, not proved here (Lam, V.3.20; Serre, *L'invariant de Witt de la forme Tr(x²)*).
name: The Clifford invariant in Galois cohomology, and the homomorphism I²/I³ → Br(K)

about: for F' = F(y) with yⁿ = u, n invertible in the constants and no root of unity assumed, every place has [e(P'|P) = d(P'|P) + 1 = n/gcd(n, ord_P u)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Different/Radical.html#TauCeti.Place.differentExponent_add_one_eq_of_pow_eq), and the [genus formula](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Radical/Genus.html#TauCeti.genus_formula_of_pow_eq) [k' : k](2g' − 2) = n(2g − 2) + Σ_P (n − gcd(n, ord_P u)) deg P follows; before this only the unramified and totally ramified cases, hence prime n, were covered (Stichtenoth, Prop. 3.7.3, Cor. 3.7.4).
name: Ramification and genus of Kummer-type extensions of function fields

about: for a strictly positive finite kernel K and positive target marginals a, b, each half-step of alternating row and column scaling contracts Hilbert's projective metric by tanh(Δ(K)/4) and a [full step by its square](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Sinkhorn.html#Matrix.hilbertProjectiveDist_sinkhornStep_le), the factors of the Sinkhorn–Knopp scaling are a fixed point, and the scaled plans converge to that scaling at this geometric rate; existence of the scaling, Sinkhorn's theorem, was announced earlier (Franklin–Lorenz, *Linear Algebra Appl.* 114/115, 1989).
name: Linear convergence of the Sinkhorn iteration

about: for a Morse function f on a compact boundaryless manifold M and a pseudo-gradient X adapted to it, the flow of X is a smooth global flow, built from the new [global flow of a complete C¹ vector field on a manifold](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/IntegralCurve/GlobalFlow.html#TauCeti.globalFlow), every orbit converges to a critical point forward and backward in time, and M is the disjoint union of the [stable sets](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Morse/PseudoGradient/Flow.html#TauCeti.IsAdaptedPseudoGradient.iUnion_stableSet) W^s(x) of the critical points, and likewise of their unstable sets (Audin–Damian, *Morse Theory and Floer Homology*, Prop. 2.1.6).
name: Pseudo-gradient flows on a compact manifold converge to critical points

about: a newform f of level N, weight k and trivial nebentypus has a_p(f) = −ε_p(f)·p^{(k−2)/2} at every prime p exactly dividing N, with ε_p(f) = ±1 its Atkin–Lehner sign, so a_p ≠ 0 and [a_p² = p^{k−2}](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/BadPrime/AtkinLehner.html#HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.qExpansion_coeff_prime_sq_of_isExactDivisor); the cases p² ∣ N and nontrivial nebentypus at p remain (Atkin–Lehner, *Hecke operators on Γ₀(m)*, Thm 3; Miyake, Thm 4.6.17).
name: The Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue at p ∥ N

about: for probability laws μᵢ on ℝ and weights wᵢ summing to one, the law ν̄ whose quantile function is Σwᵢ·Q_{μᵢ} satisfies [Σwᵢ W₂(ν, μᵢ)² = W₂(ν, ν̄)² + Σwᵢ W₂(ν̄, μᵢ)²](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Barycenter.html#TauCeti.sum_mul_wassersteinEDist_sq_eq_add) for every law ν, with no moment hypothesis, so it is the unique quadratic Fréchet barycenter of Σwᵢδ_{μᵢ} in P₂(ℝ) (Agueh–Carlier, *SIAM J. Math. Anal.* 43, 2011, §6.1).
name: Wasserstein barycenters on the real line

about: for measured kernels (X, μ, ω_X) and (Y, ν, ω_Y), with ω_X : X × X → Z into an extended metric space, the infimum over couplings π of μ and ν of the L^p(π ⊗ π) norm of d(ω_X(x, x'), ω_Y(y, y')), so that metric measure spaces are compared without a common ambient space; it is [symmetric](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Basic.html#TauCeti.gromovWassersteinEDist_comm), vanishes between a kernel and its pullback along a measure-preserving map, and for p ≥ 1 satisfies the [triangle inequality](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/GromovWasserstein/Basic.html#TauCeti.gromovWassersteinEDist_triangle), an extended pseudodistance (Mémoli, *Found. Comput. Math.* 11, 2011).
name: The Gromov–Wasserstein distance

about: an orientation of a real vector bundle is an orientation of every fibre, locally constant in the local trivializations, with the opposite orientation, the constant orientations of a trivial bundle, and the theorem that [over a preconnected base two orientations agree or are opposite](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/VectorBundle/Orientation.html#TauCeti.VectorBundleOrientation.eq_or_eq_neg); on a Riemannian manifold the [gradient](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Gradient.html#TauCeti.Manifold.riemannianGradient) of f : M → ℝ is the tangent vector dual to df_x under the metric, ⟨grad f, v⟩ = df(v), a [C^n vector field](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Gradient.html#TauCeti.Manifold.contMDiff_riemannianGradient) for a C^n metric and C^{n+1} function (Milnor–Stasheff, §9; Lee, *Riemannian Manifolds*, §2).
name: Orientations of real vector bundles, and the Riemannian gradient

about: for a cohomologically unital A∞-category 𝒞 over a commutative ring, the preadditive linear category whose morphisms are closed degree-zero morphisms modulo differentials of degree −1 morphisms, with composition descending from m₂ and associativity from the boundary of m₃; the [opposite A∞-category](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/AInfinity/Opposite.html#TauCeti.AInfinityCategory.op) and [full subcategories](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/AInfinity/FullSubcategory/Basic.html#TauCeti.AInfinityCategory.fullSubcategory) are also defined, A∞-functors and quasi-equivalences not yet (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §7.1).
name: The homotopy category H⁰ of an A∞-category

about: for a based pair (X, A, a₀), π_{n+1}(X, A, a₀) is the set of homotopy classes of maps of cubes I × Iⁿ → X sending the face {0} × Iⁿ into A and the rest of the boundary to a₀, functorial in based pairs, with the natural [boundary map](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Homotopy/Relative/Basic.html#TauCeti.RelHomotopyGroup.boundary) π_{n+1}(X, A, a₀) → πₙ(A, a₀) by restriction to that face; a cube lying in A represents the trivial class, so π_{n+1}(X, X, x₀) is trivial; the group structure and the long exact sequence are not yet constructed (Hatcher, §4.1).
name: Relative homotopy sets and their boundary map

about: for a ℂ-linear T from simple functions to a.e. classes with ‖Tf‖_{q₀} ≤ M₀‖f‖_{p₀} and ‖Tf‖_{q₁} ≤ M₁‖f‖_{p₁} on simple f, with q₀, q₁ ≥ 1 and endpoints at ∞ allowed on both sides, the interpolated bound ‖Tf‖_q ≤ M₀^{1−θ} M₁^θ ‖f‖_p holds for 1/p = (1−θ)/p₀ + θ/p₁ and 1/q likewise, 0 < θ < 1, by Thorin's complex method through Mathlib's Hadamard three-lines theorem; the extension by density to a bounded operator Lᵖ → L^q, and the Hausdorff–Young and Young inequalities, are the next items (Grafakos, *Classical Fourier Analysis*, Thm 1.3.4).
name: The Riesz–Thorin interpolation theorem

about: for an elliptic curve W over 𝔽_q, Z(W/𝔽_q, T) = exp(Σ_{n≥1} #W(𝔽_{qⁿ}) Tⁿ/n) ∈ ℚ⟦T⟧ equals (1 − a_q T + q T²)/((1 − T)(1 − qT)), and [every complex root of 1 − a_q T + q T² has absolute value q^{−1/2}](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius/Zeta.html#WeierstrassCurve.norm_eq_inv_sqrt_card_of_one_sub_frobeniusTrace_mul_add_card_mul_sq_eq_zero), from the Hasse bound; the inputs are the [Frobenius identities π² = [a_q]π − [q] and π + π̂ = [a_q]](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius/Charpoly.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.ofIsogeny_frobeniusIsogeny_comp_ofIsogeny_frobeniusIsogeny) in End(W) and the [trace recurrence t_{n+2} = a_q t_{n+1} − q t_n](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius/PowTrace.html#WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusPowTrace_add_two), proved on the ℓ-torsion without choosing eigenvalues; the functional equation Z(1/(qT)) = Z(T) is still to come (Silverman, *AEC*, V.2.3–2.4).
name: The zeta function of an elliptic curve over a finite field is rational, and the Riemann hypothesis for E/𝔽_q

about: for a based pair (X, A, a₀) the sequence π_{n+1}(A) → π_{n+1}(X) → π_{n+1}(X, A) → πₙ(A) → πₙ(X) is exact at its three middle terms in every degree, down to π₁(X, A) → π₀(A) → π₀(X), as pointed sets; and [π_{n+1}(X, A, a₀) is a group for n ≥ 1 and abelian for n ≥ 2](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Homotopy/Relative/Group.html#TauCeti.RelHomotopyGroup.group), transported from Mathlib's πₙ of the space of paths from A to a₀, with the boundary map and j : π_{n+1}(X) → π_{n+1}(X, A) [homomorphisms](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Homotopy/Relative/Group.html#TauCeti.RelHomotopyGroup.boundaryHom); both were left open when the relative homotopy sets were announced with TauCeti#13273 (Hatcher, Thm 4.3).
name: The long exact homotopy sequence of a based pair, with its group structure

about: the homology cross products assemble into a natural map ⊕_{p+q=n} Hₚ(X; R) ⊗ H_q(Y; S) → Hₙ(X × Y; R ⊗ S), which is an isomorphism over a field and, [more generally, whenever the singular chain complexes have split cycles and projective homology](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Kunneth.html#TopCat.isIso_singularHomologyKunneth_of_projective), since [such complexes are homotopy equivalent to their homology with zero differential](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Split.html#HomologicalComplex.exists_homotopyEquiv_d_eq_zero), the algebraic Künneth theorem announced earlier doing the rest through the shuffle map; the Tor short exact sequence over a principal ideal domain remains (Hatcher, §3.B; Weibel, §3.6).
name: The Künneth theorem for singular homology

about: for a linear map A between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces, A⁺y = Σᵢ σᵢ⁻² ⟨A vᵢ, y⟩ vᵢ over the eigenbasis (vᵢ) of A†A, and [a map B equals A⁺ exactly when it satisfies the four Penrose equations](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/MoorePenrose.html#LinearMap.isMoorePenroseInverse_iff_eq_moorePenroseInverse) ABA = A, BAB = B, AB and BA self-adjoint, uniqueness holding in any inner product space; with (A†)⁺ = (A⁺)†, (A⁺)⁺ = A, and the injective, surjective and invertible cases (Penrose, 1955; Ben-Israel–Greville, *Generalized Inverses*, Ch. 1).
name: The Moore–Penrose inverse

about: for a bounded linear operator T on L²(ℝⁿ) represented off the support of its argument by a kernel satisfying Hörmander's condition ∫_{|x − y'| > 2|y − y'|} ‖K(x, y) − K(x, y')‖ dx ≤ B, one has t·|{‖Tf‖ > t}| ≤ (2ⁿ(4‖T‖² + 1) + 4B)‖f‖₁ for every f ∈ L² and t > 0, by the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition announced earlier; the strong Lᵖ bounds for 1 < p < ∞ and the Mihlin–Hörmander multiplier theorem remain (Stein, *Singular Integrals*, II §2; Grafakos, §5.3).
name: The Calderón–Zygmund theorem: singular integrals are of weak type (1, 1)

about: for f integrable on a cube Q ⊆ ℝⁿ whose mean oscillation ⨍_B ‖f − f_B‖ is at most M on every subcube B, |{x ∈ Q : ‖f(x) − f_Q‖ > s}| ≤ 2 exp(−(log 2) s/(2ⁿ⁺¹M)) |Q| for every s, hence [exp(σ‖f − f_Q‖) is integrable on Q](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/JohnNirenberg.html#TauCeti.setLIntegral_exp_mul_norm_sub_setAverage_closedBall_le) with an explicit bound once exp(2ⁿ⁺¹σM) < 2, first on dyadic cubes by iterating the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition and then on arbitrary cubes by affine rescaling; the space BMO itself and the L^∞ → BMO endpoint are not yet built (John–Nirenberg, 1961; Grafakos, *Modern Fourier Analysis*, Thm 3.1.6).
name: The John–Nirenberg inequality

about: iterating Schensted row insertion over the letters of a word w gives a bijection w ↦ (P(w), r(w)) from words in an ordered alphabet onto the pairs of a tableau and a lattice word (every prefix has at least as many i's as (i+1)'s) with row i of P as long as r has letters i, the recording word storing the recording tableau row by row; injectivity and the image are proved one letter at a time from the single-step row-insertion bijection, and the restriction to permutations and standard tableaux, with Σ_λ (f^λ)² = n!, is still to come (Fulton, *Young Tableaux*, §4.1; Sagan, *The Symmetric Group*, §3.1).
name: The Robinson–Schensted correspondence for words

about: for S faithfully flat over R, a descent datum on an S-algebra B, a coaction B → S ⊗_R B that is a section of multiplication and coassociative, shown [equivalent to the classical gluing isomorphism B ⊗_R S ≅ S ⊗_R B with the cocycle condition](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Flat/EffectiveDescent.html#TauCeti.Algebra.DescentDatum.equivIsoDescentDatum), is effective, S ⊗_R B^θ ≅ B for the descended algebra B^θ, the descended object is unique, [morphisms of descent data descend, so base change to algebras with descent data is fully faithful](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Flat/EffectiveDescent.html#TauCeti.Algebra.DescentDatum.baseChangeHomEquiv), and [descent commutes with base change of R](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Flat/EffectiveDescent.html#TauCeti.Algebra.DescentDatum.tensorDescendedEquiv); under Spec this is Grothendieck's descent for affine schemes over an affine base, and separately [sections and morphisms descend along any morphism whose base changes are effective epimorphisms](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/EffectiveEpi/Descent.html#TauCeti.homDescentEquiv), hence along fpqc and fppf morphisms of schemes (SGA 1, VIII, Thm 2.1; Stacks, *Descent*; Vistoli, Thm 2.55).
name: Effective faithfully flat descent for affine schemes

about: for a convex f on a finite-dimensional inner product space, [MA_f(s) = μ(∂f(s ∩ D))](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere.html#TauCeti.mongeAmpereMeasure), the Haar measure of the subgradient image, is a locally finite Borel measure on the interior D of the domain, almost-disjointness of subgradient images coming from Rademacher's theorem for the conjugate; for twice differentiable convex u it is [det(D²u) dx](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere.html#TauCeti.mongeAmpereMeasure_eq_withDensity_det); and for u convex on a bounded open convex Ω, continuous up to the boundary and nonnegative there, (−u(x₀))₊ⁿ μ(B(0, 1)) ≤ 2ⁿ⁺¹ diam(Ω)ⁿ⁻¹ dist(x₀, Ωᶜ) MA_u(Ω), the first step toward the Dirichlet problem and Caffarelli's regularity theory (Gutiérrez, *The Monge–Ampère Equation*, Thms 1.1.13 and 1.4.2; Figalli, Ch. 2).
name: The Aleksandrov Monge–Ampère measure, and the Aleksandrov maximum principle

about: for a compactly supported C¹ map u : ℂ → F into a complex Banach space, u(w) = (2π)⁻¹ ∫ (w − z)⁻¹ (∂ₓu + i ∂ᵧu)(z) dz, so the Cauchy kernel is a fundamental solution of ∂̄, and conversely, for compactly supported C¹ f, [∂̄ of the Cauchy transform of f is f](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Pompeiu.html#HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply_one_add_I_smul_apply_I_two_pi_inv_smul_integral_sub_inv_smul); Mathlib has the contour Cauchy integral formula for holomorphic maps only, and the Lᵖ bound for the Beurling transform that this representation starts is the next item on the way to the Calderón–Zygmund inequality for ∂̄ (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, Thms 1.2.1–1.2.2).
name: The Cauchy–Pompeiu formula

about: the integer character of the Specht module S^λ at a permutation of cycle type μ is computed by deleting one part r of μ and summing (−1)^{ht} over the rim hooks of r cells removed from λ, compatibly with the choice of permutation representative; this is the character-theoretic rule, derived by comparing coefficients in the Schur basis from the symmetric-function form p_r s_ν = Σ ± s_μ announced earlier with TauCeti#8814 (Sagan, *The Symmetric Group*, Ch. 4; Macdonald, I §7).
name: The Murnaghan–Nakayama rule for the characters of the symmetric group

about: for an even nondegenerate integral lattice L of signature (t₊, t₋), the Gauss-sum invariant of its discriminant form equals t₊ − t₋ in ℤ/8, by induction on the rank through a vector of norm 2m and the half Gauss sum Σ_{k<2M} e^{2πik²/4M} = (1 + i)√M; hence [an even unimodular lattice has 8 ∣ t₊ − t₋](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Milgram.html#TauCeti.IntegralLattice.eight_dvd_sigPos_sub_sigNeg_of_isUnimodular), the input to van der Blij's formula and the rank-8 results (Milnor–Husemoller, *Symmetric Bilinear Forms*, App. 4; Nikulin, Thm 1.3.3).
name: Milgram's theorem for even nondegenerate lattices

about: for a finite group G, a G-module C and u ∈ H²(G, C) such that on every subgroup S of prime-power order H¹(S, C) = 0 and res u generates H²(S, C), of order |S|, cup product with u is a bijection Ĥʳ(G, M) → Ĥʳ⁺²(G, M ⊗ C) in every degree r ∈ ℤ, for every G-module M with Tor₁^ℤ(M, C) = 0, the Tor condition stated as injectivity of M ⊗ X → M ⊗ Y for every short exact 0 → X → Y → C → 0; Tate's theorem announced earlier is the case M = ℤ, and the new input is that [M ⊗ A stays cohomologically trivial when A is and Tor₁(M, A) = 0](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/NakayamaRim.html#Rep.isZero_res_tensor_of_isZero_res) (Nakayama, Ann. of Math. 65, 1957; Serre, *Local Fields*, IX §8).
name: The Tate–Nakayama theorem

about: for a function field F = F₁F₂ over an algebraically closed field with F/F₁ separable, nᵢ = [F : Fᵢ] and gᵢ the genus of Fᵢ, g(F) ≤ n₁g₁ + n₂g₂ + (n₁ − 1)(n₂ − 1), through a [split-place version over any constant field](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/Castelnuovo.html#TauCeti.genus_le_finrank_mul_genus_add_finrank_mul_genus_add_of_isSplitCompletely) and a nonspecial divisor of degree g₂; alongside it, [the genus of a plane model of degree n is at most (n − 1)(n − 2)/2](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/PlaneModel.html#TauCeti.genus_le_totalDegree_sub_one_mul_totalDegree_sub_two_div_two), for any relation φ(x, y) = 0 over any constant field, which completes the III.11 genus estimates after Riemann's inequality announced earlier (Stichtenoth, Thm 3.11.3, Prop. 3.11.5).
name: Castelnuovo's inequality (the Castelnuovo–Severi inequality) for function fields

about: there are only finitely many isometry classes of positive definite integral lattices of a given rank and bounded determinant, by Hermite's reduction: a primitive vector of least norm, Hermite's inequality and Chiò's condensation put a Gram matrix of every such lattice in an explicit finite set of integer matrices; and [every entry of a Minkowski-reduced Gram matrix is bounded by (∏ᵢ i!)²·4ⁿ·Γ(n/2 + 1)²·det L/πⁿ](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/PosDef/ReducedGram.html#TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsMinkowskiReduced.abs_gramMatrix_mul_pi_pow_le), through β(bᵢ, bᵢ) ≤ (i!)² λᵢ and Minkowski's second theorem announced earlier (Hermite, 1850; Cassels, *Rational Quadratic Forms*, Ch. 9 §1 and Ch. 12).
name: Finiteness of classes of positive definite integral lattices

about: every isogeny φ : E₁ → E₂ of elliptic curves over any field has a [dual φ̂](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Dual/Basic.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.dual) with φ̂ ∘ φ = [deg φ], the separable case by Galois descent from the separable closure and the inseparable case through φ = φ_s ∘ Fʳ and the Verschiebung, extending the dual for separable isogenies over a separably closed field announced earlier; the dual is additive, and deg extends to a positive-definite quadratic form on Hom(E₁, E₂) with no separability hypothesis, via the [Weil-pairing adjointness e_N(φS, T) = e_N(S, φ̂T) for every isogeny](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Dual/WeilPairing.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.weilPairing_eq_weilPairing_dual) (Silverman, III.6.1–6.3, III.8.2).
name: The dual of an arbitrary isogeny, and the degree as a positive-definite quadratic form

about: for a function field F = F₁F₂ over an algebraically closed field with F/F₁ separable, nᵢ = [F : Fᵢ] and gᵢ the genus of Fᵢ, g(F) ≤ n₁g₁ + n₂g₂ + (n₁ − 1)(n₂ − 1), through a [split-place version over any constant field](https://cbirkbeck.github.io/tauceti-reviewed-by-test/#/d/TauCeti.genus_le_finrank_mul_genus_add_finrank_mul_genus_add_of_isSplitCompletely) and a nonspecial divisor of degree g₂; alongside it, [the genus of a plane model of degree n is at most (n − 1)(n − 2)/2](https://cbirkbeck.github.io/tauceti-reviewed-by-test/#/d/TauCeti.genus_le_totalDegree_sub_one_mul_totalDegree_sub_two_div_two), for any relation φ(x, y) = 0 over any constant field, which completes the III.11 genus estimates after Riemann's inequality announced earlier (Stichtenoth, Thm 3.11.3, Prop. 3.11.5).
name: Castelnuovo's inequality (the Castelnuovo–Severi inequality) for function fields

about: for a nonarchimedean local field K of characteristic zero, the local Artin map is an isomorphism of topological groups from Kˣ onto the topological abelianization W_K/closure[W_K, W_K] of the local Weil group with its Weil topology, [compatible with the absolute Artin map Kˣ → G_K^ab](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/WeilGroup/Reciprocity.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.localWeilArtinEquiv_compat); the inputs, valid in every characteristic, are that [W_K^ab → G_K^ab is injective](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/WeilGroup/Abelianization.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.injective_weilToAbsoluteAbelianization) and that [the image of the Artin map in G_K^ab is exactly the image of the Weil group](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/WeilGroup/ArtinMap.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.mem_range_artinMap_iff), the classes with integral unramified coordinate, so the Artin map is not surjective onto G_K^ab; with this every item of the local Weil group layer is proved (Tate, *Number theoretic background*, §1.4; Weil, 1951).
name: Local reciprocity for the Weil group, Kˣ ≃ W_K^ab

about: on a finite-dimensional real normed space with a Haar measure, a locally integrable f agrees almost everywhere with an α-Hölder function, α > 0, exactly when its mean oscillation on every ball of radius r is at most M rᵅ, the Hölder representative being the precise representative with constant 2·2ᵅ·2ⁿ/(1 − 2^{−α})·M, by telescoping the averages over dyadic radii; Morrey's Dirichlet growth theorem and the Campanato route to the Schauder estimates are the next steps (Campanato, 1963; Giaquinta–Martinazzi, Thm 5.5).
name: Campanato's characterization of Hölder continuity

about: for a covering p : E → B with finite fibres, the transfer C(B; R) → C(E; R) sums the lifts of a simplex, with p_* ∘ τ = d·id when every fibre has d points, on chains and on homology in every degree, and τ ∘ p_* = Σ_{g∈G} g_* for the quotient covering of a free action of a finite group G; for such a quotient [C(B; R) is the complex of coinvariants C(E; R)_G](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Coinvariants.html#IsQuotientCoveringMap.isColimitMapCoconeSingularChainComplex) for any group, and [Hₙ(B; R) = Hₙ(E; R)_G when |G| is invertible in R](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Coinvariants.html#IsQuotientCoveringMap.isColimitMapCoconeSingularHomology); the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence is the next item (Hatcher, §3.G; Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, VII).
name: The transfer of a finite covering on singular chains, and the chains of a quotient as coinvariants

about: over a field F with a valuation, [reduction W(F) → W̃(k) is a group homomorphism](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/GoodReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.reductionHom) whenever the integral model has unit discriminant, proved through the Bosma–Lenstra complete addition laws over a local ring, with kernel O together with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole; over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain at a good prime it is injective on W(F)[n] for n prime to the residue characteristic, so #W(F)[n] divides #W̃(k), the standard bound on torsion; that E₁ has no p-torsion when v(p) < p − 1 is still to come (Silverman, VII.2.1, VII.3.1).
name: Reduction of points at good reduction is a homomorphism, injective on prime-to-p torsion

about: over every field, characteristic two included, the preprojective algebra Π(Q) of every orientation of every finite simply-laced Dynkin diagram (Aₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈) is left and right self-injective, by Baer's criterion one vertex at a time using exactness of the Koszul complex at its middle term and no explicit basis, where before only A₁, A₂, D₄ and the Aₙ family were known; and, on the non-Dynkin side, for [any orientation without sinks of a finite graph the matrix Hilbert series of Π equals C_G(−X)⁻¹](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Preprojective/HilbertSeries/ZigzagCartan.html#TauCeti.preprojectiveHilbertSeries_eq_inv_zigzagGradedCartanMatrix_map_aeval_neg_X) with C_G(q) = (1 + q²)I + qA_G the quantum Cartan matrix (Brenner–Butler–King, §4; Etingof–Eu, §§2–3).
name: Preprojective algebras of Dynkin type are self-injective

about: on a set Ω of finite measure in an n-dimensional space, every u ∈ W^{1,n}₀(Ω) lies in L^q(Ω) for all finite q ≥ n with ‖u‖_q ≤ n⁻¹ ω^{−1/n} (q(1 − 1/n) + 1)^{1−1/n+1/q} μ(Ω)^{1/q} ‖∇u‖_n, through the potential bound ‖u(x)‖ ≤ (nω)⁻¹ ∫ ‖Du(y)‖‖x − y‖^{1−n} dy and Young's inequality for integral kernels; the constant grows like q^{1−1/n}, which is what summing the exponential series for Trudinger's inequality needs (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Lemmas 7.12, 7.14 and Thm 7.15).
name: The borderline Sobolev embedding W^{1,n}₀ ⊆ L^q for every finite q

about: for a quadratic extension L/K with 2 invertible and a ∈ Lˣ, the trace forms satisfy w₂(Tr_*⟨a⟩) = w₂(Tr_*⟨1⟩) + N^{Ev}((a)) + w₁(Tr_*⟨1⟩) ∪ cor(a), with the Evens norm and corestriction along any embedding of L into a separable closure, completing the degree-one formula already on main; the key input is [the value of the Evens norm on a Kummer class](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Evens/Kummer/Value.html#TauCeti.galoisEvens2_kummerClass), N^{Ev}((a)) = (Tr a) ∪ (−d·N a) + (2) ∪ (d) for L = K(√d) and Tr a ≠ 0, and (2) ∪ (d) at trace zero, following the second proof of Serre's theorem on the Witt invariant of Tr(x²) (Kahn, Invent. Math. 78, 1984, Thm 2 and Lemme II.2.1; Serre, Comment. Math. Helv. 59, 1984).
name: Kahn's relative Stiefel–Whitney formula for a quadratic extension

about: for a separated smooth relative curve f : X → S with a section x₀, the natural transformation x ↦ 𝒪(Γₓ) ⊗ 𝒪(x₀_T)⁻¹ from the functor of points Hom_S(−, X) to the relative Picard presheaf T ↦ Pic(X_T)/Pic(T), [sending x₀ to the identity](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PicardFunctor/AbelJacobi.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.abelJacobiMap_app_basePoint), built from the graph of a T-point as a relative effective Cartier divisor commuting with base change; representability of Pic⁰ by the Jacobian and the Albanese property are what remain for the morphism X → Jac(X) (Kleiman, *The Picard scheme*, §9.3; Milne, *Jacobian varieties*, §2).
name: The Abel–Jacobi map on functors of points

about: e^{tΔ} on Lᵖ(E; F), 1 ≤ p < ∞, as a strongly continuous contraction semigroup, convolution with the heat kernel for t > 0 and the identity at t = 0, the semigroup law from the Chapman–Kolmogorov identity, contractivity from Young's inequality and strong continuity from the approximate-identity theorem, built on a new [L¹ ⋆ Lᵖ → Lᵖ convolution operator](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Function/Lp/Convolution.html#TauCeti.convolutionLp) with Young's inequality, which Mathlib lacks; after the heat kernel and its solution of the heat equation announced earlier, identifying the generator with the Laplacian and the Lᵖ smoothing estimates remain (Engel–Nagel, II.2.12; Folland, *Real Analysis*, §8.2).
name: The heat semigroup on Lᵖ

about: for an extended-real energy φ on a metric space, the [descending slope |∂φ|(x) = limsup_{y→x} (φ(x) − φ(y))⁺/d(x, y)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/Slope.html#TauCeti.descendingSlope) and [strong upper gradients](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/UpperGradient.html#TauCeti.IsStrongUpperGradient) g, with φ(γ_a) ≤ φ(γ_b) + ∫ g(γ)|γ'| along absolutely continuous curves and the chain rule |(φ ∘ γ)'| ≤ |∂φ|(γ)|γ'|; a p-curve of maximal slope satisfies the energy-dissipation inequality φ(u_t) + (1/p)∫|u'|ᵖ + (1/q)∫g(u)^q ≤ φ(u_s), and for a strong upper gradient [this is an equality](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/MaximalSlope.html#TauCeti.IsCurveOfMaximalSlope.apply_eq_add_dissipation) with |u'|ᵖ = g(u)^q almost everywhere; u' = −∇f on a Hilbert space is the model case, and existence by minimizing movements is the next item (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, *Gradient Flows*, §§1.2–1.3).
name: Curves of maximal slope, descending slopes and strong upper gradients

about: for a form on a manifold with boundary or corners, dω is defined by conjugating Mathlib's flat exterior derivative through the chart at each point, within the range of the model, as mfderiv is, so it is total and needs no smoothness instance; it is local in the set and in the form, linear, [agrees with extDeriv over the model space](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/DifferentialForm/ExtDeriv.html#TauCeti.mextDeriv_eq_extDeriv), and sends the 0-form of a function to its differential; chart independence as a theorem, naturality, d² = 0 and the Leibniz rule are the next layers (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Ch. 14).
name: The exterior derivative of differential forms on manifolds

about: for a linear map A between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces with Mathlib's singular values σ₀ ≥ σ₁ ≥ ⋯, the [right singular basis](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.html#LinearMap.rightSingularBasis) (vᵢ), an orthonormal eigenbasis of A†A, and the [left singular vectors](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.html#LinearMap.leftSingularVector) uᵢ = σᵢ⁻¹ A vᵢ satisfy A vᵢ = σᵢ uᵢ, A† uᵢ = σᵢ vᵢ and A = Σᵢ σᵢ uᵢ ⊗ vᵢ, with the nonzero uᵢ extending to an orthonormal basis of the target (Horn–Johnson 2.6.3); the singular-system definitions are adapted from Kitware's DKPS formalization (Apache-2.0).
name: The singular value decomposition

about: for a symmetric operator T on a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space with eigenvalues λ₀ ≥ λ₁ ≥ ⋯, λₖ = sup over (k+1)-dimensional subspaces V of inf over unit x ∈ V of Re⟪Tx, x⟫; hence the sorted eigenvalues are [monotone under quadratic-form domination](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/CourantFischer.html#LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_mono) and [|λₖ(T) − λₖ(S)| ≤ ‖T − S‖](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/CourantFischer.html#LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm) for symmetric S, T (Horn–Johnson 4.2.6 and 4.3.1); ported from Kitware's DKPS formalization (Apache-2.0).
name: The Courant–Fischer min–max theorem, and Weyl's inequality

about: if V ↪ H ↪ V* is a [Gelfand triple](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/GelfandTriple.html#ContinuousLinearMap.gelfandDual) and u ∈ L²(a, b; V) has weak time derivative u' ∈ L²(a, b; V*), then u agrees a.e. with a function in C([a, b]; H), every such representative satisfies the [energy identity](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/WeakDeriv/GelfandTriple.html#TauCeti.HasWeakLineDerivOn.norm_sq_sub_norm_sq_eq_of_gelfandDual) ‖u(t)‖² − ‖u(s)‖² = 2 ∫ₛᵗ ⟨u'(r), u(r)⟩ dr, and [its supremum norm is bounded by the L² norms of u and u'](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/WeakDeriv/GelfandTriple.html#TauCeti.HasWeakLineDerivOn.norm_sq_le_of_gelfandDual) (Evans §5.9.2, Theorem 3); the setting in which weak solutions of linear parabolic equations take their initial values.
name: The Lions–Magenes lemma for a Gelfand triple V ↪ H ↪ V*

about: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve over any commutative ring R, its projective model is a [commutative](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/GroupLaw.html#WeierstrassCurve.isCommMonObj_projModel) group object of Over(Spec R), with unit the zero section (0 : 1 : 0), multiplication the Bosma–Lenstra addition morphism and inverse (X : Y : Z) ↦ (X : −Y − a₁X − a₃Z : Z), the last axiom being the [scheme-theoretic inverse law](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Addition/Inverse.html#WeierstrassCurve.additionMorphism_right_inv) proved here (Katz–Mazur §2.1); base change and gluing over a non-affine base are still to come.
name: The projective Weierstrass model is a commutative group scheme

about: every horn Λ[n+1, i] → Sing(X) has a filler, obtained by gluing the given singular n-simplices along the facets of the topological horn and composing with a retraction of Δⁿ⁺¹ onto that horn (May, Chapter I), a result Mathlib lists as a TODO.
name: The singular simplicial set of a space is a Kan complex

about: the function field y^q + y = x^(q+1), with q a power of the characteristic p, [has genus q(q − 1)/2](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Hermitian/Genus.html#TauCeti.IsHermitianCoordinates.two_mul_genus_eq) (Stichtenoth §6.4), so over 𝔽_{q²} its q³ translations [exceed 84(g − 1) once q ≥ 41](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Hermitian/HurwitzCounterexample.html#TauCeti.IsHermitianCoordinates.eighty_four_mul_genus_sub_one_lt_natCard_hermitianTranslations); for q = 64 that is a group of order 262,144 acting on a curve of genus 2016, and the extension over its fixed field [is wildly ramified](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Hermitian/HurwitzCounterexample.html#TauCeti.IsHermitianCoordinates.exists_not_isTame_hermitianTranslations), so the tameness hypothesis in the Hurwitz bound cannot be dropped.
name: The Hermitian function field breaks the Hurwitz bound in characteristic p

about: a finite-dimensional central division algebra D over any field K, perfect or not, contains a separable subfield L of degree deg D over K, [which is therefore a splitting field of D](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/CentralSimple/MaximalSubfield/Separable.html#TauCeti.Algebra.exists_isSplittingField_isSeparable_finrank_eq_deg); the proof applies Jacobson–Noether to the centralizer of a separable commutative subalgebra of maximal dimension (Pierce, Chapter 13; Gille–Szamuely §2.2).
name: Every central division algebra has a separable maximal subfield

about: over any field F, the translation pullbacks form a [normal subgroup](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/FunctionField/Translation/Automorphism.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.normal_range_translationHom) T of Aut(F(E)/F), the automorphisms [fixing the place at infinity are exactly the changes of variables preserving E](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/FunctionField/Translation/Automorphism.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.stabilizer_infinity_eq_range_autGroupToAlgEquiv) and form a complement, so Aut(F(E)/F)/T ≃ Aut(E, O); and [Aut(E, O) is finite in every characteristic](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Aut.html#WeierstrassCurve.finite_autGroup), over any integral domain (Stichtenoth Exercise 6.14; Silverman III.10); this adds normality, finite index and the quotient to the Galois theory of translations announced earlier.
name: The automorphism group of an elliptic function field is the translations extended by Aut(E, O)

about: the diagonal dₖ = Re⟪T eₖ, eₖ⟫ of a symmetric operator in any orthonormal basis is majorized by its spectrum: Σₖ φ(dₖ) ≤ Σᵢ φ(λᵢ) for every convex φ, because the [matrix of squared overlaps ‖⟪vᵢ, eₖ⟫‖² of two orthonormal bases is doubly stochastic](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SchurHorn.html#OrthonormalBasis.schurWeight_mem_doublyStochastic) and [convex sums decrease under doubly stochastic averaging](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/DoublyStochasticMatrix.html#ConvexOn.sum_map_mulVec_le_of_mem_doublyStochastic) (Marshall–Olkin–Arnold 9.B.1); Horn's converse is not yet formalised.
name: Schur's majorization inequality, the forward half of Schur–Horn

about: the [weight](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/WeierstrassGaps.html#TauCeti.Place.weierstrassWeight) w(P) = Σⱼ (lⱼ − j) of the gap sequence l₁ < ⋯ < l_g at a rational place satisfies 0 ≤ w(P) ≤ g(g − 1)/2, [with equality exactly when 2 is a pole number at P](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Consequences/WeierstrassGaps.html#TauCeti.Place.weierstrassWeight_eq_genus_choose_two_iff), in which case the gaps are 1, 3, …, 2g − 1 and, away from characteristic 2, [the function field is hyperelliptic](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Hyperelliptic/WeierstrassGaps.html#TauCeti.isHyperellipticFunctionField_of_isPoleNumber_two) (Farkas–Kra III.5); the total weight g³ − g is still to come.
name: The Weierstrass weight of a point is at most g(g − 1)/2

about: for a subset J of the simple reflections, P_J is the subgroup generated by B and the cells BsB for s ∈ J, and [P_J is exactly the union of the cells BwB over w in the subgroup W_J generated by J](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Parabolic.html#TauCeti.TitsSystem.coe_standardParabolic), with P_∅ = B and P_S = G (Bourbaki, Lie IV §2.5; Humphreys §29); the classification of all subgroups containing B is still to come.
name: Standard parabolic subgroups of a Tits system, and their Bruhat decomposition

about: the rational function (1 − a_q T + qT²)/((1 − T)(1 − qT)) in ℚ(T), [whose Laurent expansion is Z(E/𝔽_q, T)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius/Zeta.html#WeierstrassCurve.coe_zetaRatFunc), is invariant under T ↦ 1/(qT), so Z(E/𝔽_q, 1/(qT)) = Z(E/𝔽_q, T) as an identity in ℚ(T) (Silverman V.2.4); together with yesterday's rationality and Riemann hypothesis this completes the Weil conjectures for elliptic curves.
name: The functional equation of the zeta function of an elliptic curve over 𝔽_q

about: at a rational place with a separating uniformizer t, [Laurent expansion turns d/dt into formal differentiation](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Expansion/Laurent/Derivative.html#TauCeti.Place.laurentSeriesExpansion_derivativeOfSeparating), which gives the [transformation formula res_{P,s}(z) = res_{P,t}(z · ds/dt)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Expansion/Laurent/Derivative.html#TauCeti.Place.residue_eq_residue_mul_derivativeOfSeparating) for any two uniformizers in every characteristic, so the [residue](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Expansion/Laurent/Derivative.html#TauCeti.Place.kaehlerResidue) of a Kähler differential ω = z dt does not depend on t, and exact differentials have residue zero (Stichtenoth 4.2.9 and 4.2.10).
name: The residue of a differential at a point is well defined

about: the class of maps in `TopCat` with the right lifting property against the cylinder inclusions Dⁿ ↪ Dⁿ × I, [equivalently the homotopy lifting property for every disk or every cube](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/SerreFibration/Basic.html#TauCeti.TopCat.mem_serreFibrations_iff_cube); Mathlib's lifting-property calculus makes them closed under composition, retracts, products and [base change](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/SerreFibration/Basic.html#TauCeti.TopCat.mem_serreFibrations_pullbackFst), covering maps and projections are examples, and maps of fibrations induce maps of fibres (Hatcher §4.2); the long exact sequence and the Serre spectral sequence are still to come.
name: Serre fibrations

about: for probability measures μ, ν on any measurable space, ‖μ − ν‖² ≤ 2·KL(μ‖ν), where ‖·‖ is the total variation of the signed measure μ − ν (twice the usual d_TV, so d_TV² ≤ KL/2), and [2(μ(s) − ν(s))² ≤ KL(μ‖ν) for every measurable s](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler/Pinsker.html#TauCeti.two_mul_sq_measureReal_sub_le_klDiv); no absolute continuity is assumed and infinite entropy is allowed; proved from the Donsker–Varadhan bound and Hoeffding's lemma (Csiszár–Körner, *Information Theory*).
name: Pinsker's inequality

about: on an open set Ω of a finite-dimensional inner product space with a Haar measure, a locally integrable u with ∫ Δφ·u = 0 for every test function φ on Ω agrees a.e. on Ω with a harmonic function, and [a continuous u is harmonic iff it is weakly harmonic](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Harmonic/Weyl.html#TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_iff_weaklyHarmonicOn); by mollification, the mean-value property and Lebesgue differentiation (Weyl 1940; Hörmander, *Linear PDO I*, Thm 4.4.1).
name: Weyl's lemma

about: for a PID k, a projective coefficient module R (for instance k = R = ℤ), any k-module M and any space X, the sequence 0 → Ext¹(Hₙ(X; R), M) → Hⁿ⁺¹(X; R, M) → Hom(Hₙ₊₁(X; R), M) → 0 is [exact](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/UniversalCoefficient.html#TopCat.exact_singularExtToCohomology_singularKronecker), its second map the Kronecker pairing, [natural in X](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/UniversalCoefficient.html#TopCat.singularExtToCohomology_naturality) and split, the splitting not naturally; this is the specialisation to spaces of the chain-level sequence announced earlier, reached independently by two PRs (Hatcher, Thm 3.2).
name: The universal coefficient theorem for singular cohomology

about: the isomorphism Hₙ(cellular chains) ≅ Hₙ(C, D), announced earlier for finite-dimensional complexes, now holds for arbitrary relative CW complexes with coefficients in any abelian category with exact sequential colimits, since [the inclusion of the (n + 1)-skeleton is an isomorphism on Hₙ](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cellular/Comparison.html#TauCeti.isIso_singularHomologyMap_skeletonBasePairToComplex_succ_of_hasExactColimitsOfShape) (Hatcher, Lemma 2.34, Thm 2.35).
name: Cellular homology computes singular homology, for every relative CW complex

about: for T bounded on L²(ℝⁿ) (Hilbert-space valued) whose kernel satisfies Hörmander's condition, [‖Tf‖ₚ ≤ C(p, n, ‖T‖, B)·‖f‖ₚ for 1 < p < 2](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/CalderonZygmund/StrongType.html#ContinuousLinearMap.eLpNorm_le_of_hormander) by Marcinkiewicz interpolation from the weak (1, 1) bound announced earlier, and [for 2 < p < ∞](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/CalderonZygmund/StrongType.html#ContinuousLinearMap.eLpNorm_le_of_hormander_adjoint) by duality when the adjoint satisfies the same cancellation condition; the estimates are proved for f ∈ L² ∩ Lᵖ, and the extension of T to all of Lᵖ by density is still to come (Stein, *Singular Integrals*, II §2; Grafakos §5.3).
name: The Calderón–Zygmund theorem: singular integrals are bounded on Lᵖ, 1 < p < ∞

about: y² = x(x − A)(x + B) over any ring; over a Dedekind domain O with fraction field F, when A ≡ −1 (mod 4), 16 ∣ B, gcd(A, B) = 1 and the curve is elliptic over F, it is [semistable](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FreyCurve.html#TauCeti.isSemistable_freyCurve) with [minimal discriminant ideal generated by A²B²(A + B)²/2⁸](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FreyCurve.html#TauCeti.minimalDiscriminantIdeal_freyCurve); for coprime integers with aᵖ + bᵖ + cᵖ = 0 and p ≥ 4, reordered so that b is even and aᵖ ≡ −1 (mod 4), which is always possible, the curve y² = x(x − aᵖ)(x + bᵖ) over ℚ is semistable with [minimal discriminant (abc)^{2p}/2⁸](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FreyCurve.html#TauCeti.minimalDiscriminantIdeal_freyCurve_pow); the conductor is still to come (Frey 1986; Hellegouarch 1975; Silverman VIII.11).
name: The Frey–Hellegouarch curve

about: for E over a field K and m invertible in K, [the Kummer sequence 0 → E[m] → E(Kˢ) → E(Kˢ) → 0](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.html#WeierstrassCurve.kummerShortExact) of discrete G_K-modules (multiplication by m being [surjective on separably closed points](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/MulByInt/Surjective.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.zsmul_surjective)), the Kummer map E(K) → H¹(G_K, E[m]), σ ↦ σQ − Q, and the exact sequence [0 → E(K)/mE(K) → H¹(G_K, E[m]) → H¹(G_K, E)[m] → 0](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/GaloisCohomology/Descent.html#WeierstrassCurve.exact_kummerClassMap_torsionCoeffInclH1), in continuous cohomology (Silverman X.4).
name: The Kummer map of an elliptic curve and the m-descent sequence

about: for y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆ over a number field F, the explicit 2-Selmer group cut out of the square classes of F[X]/(f) by norm and local conditions is finite, so the bound [2^rank · #E(F)[2] ≤ #Sel₂](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/RankBound.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.pow_rank_le_card_selmerGroup%E2%82%82), announced earlier for any finite group containing the image of the descent map, now applies to the Selmer group itself; computing a rank remains (Silverman X.4; statement after Stoll's EllipticCurves project).
name: The 2-Selmer group of an elliptic curve over a number field is finite

about: for probability measures μ, ν on any measurable space, ‖μ − ν‖² ≤ 2·KL(μ‖ν), where ‖·‖ is the total variation of the signed measure μ − ν (twice the usual d_TV, so d_TV² ≤ KL/2), and [2(μ(s) − ν(s))² ≤ KL(μ‖ν) for every measurable s](https://cbirkbeck.github.io/tauceti-reviewed-by-test/#/d/TauCeti.two_mul_sq_measureReal_sub_le_klDiv); no absolute continuity is assumed and infinite entropy is allowed; proved from the Donsker–Varadhan bound and Hoeffding's lemma (Csiszár–Körner, *Information Theory*).
name: Pinsker's inequality

about: for T bounded on L²(ℝⁿ) (Hilbert-space valued) whose kernel satisfies Hörmander's condition, [‖Tf‖ₚ ≤ C(p, n, ‖T‖, B)·‖f‖ₚ for 1 < p < 2](https://cbirkbeck.github.io/tauceti-reviewed-by-test/#/d/ContinuousLinearMap.eLpNorm_le_of_hormander) by Marcinkiewicz interpolation from the weak (1, 1) bound announced earlier, and [for 2 < p < ∞](https://cbirkbeck.github.io/tauceti-reviewed-by-test/#/d/ContinuousLinearMap.eLpNorm_le_of_hormander_adjoint) by duality when the adjoint satisfies the same cancellation condition; the estimates are proved for f ∈ L² ∩ Lᵖ, and the extension of T to all of Lᵖ by density is still to come (Stein, *Singular Integrals*, II §2; Grafakos §5.3).
name: The Calderón–Zygmund theorem: singular integrals are bounded on Lᵖ, 1 < p < ∞

about: for a function field F/k with k algebraically closed and any Kähler differential ω of F/k, the residues res_P(ω) vanish at all but finitely many places and Σ_P res_P(ω) = 0, with a uniformiser-free residue; the inputs are the chain rule dy = (dy/dx)·dx for Weil differentials and the identification of local components with residues (Stichtenoth, Thm 4.3.2, Cor 4.3.3).
name: The residue theorem for function fields

about: for a function field of genus g over an algebraically closed field in which the gap numbers at every place remain distinct in k (automatic in characteristic 0 and in characteristic p ≥ 2g − 1), [only finitely many places are Weierstrass points](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/Weierstrass/TotalWeight.html#TauCeti.Place.finite_setOf_weierstrassWeight_ne_zero) and their weights add up to g³ − g, completing yesterday's bound w(P) ≤ g(g − 1)/2; via [the order of the Wronskian of a canonical basis at a rational place, w(P) − g·W(P)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/Weierstrass/Weight.html#TauCeti.Place.ord_wronskian_derivativeOfSeparating_basis_eq_weierstrassWeight_sub) and [the Wronskian criterion for linear independence over the constants of a derivation](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Derivation/Wronskian/Basic.html#Derivation.wronskian_ne_zero_iff) (Farkas–Kra III.5; Goldschmidt, GTM 215).
name: The Weierstrass weights of a curve sum to g³ − g

about: [an L² function in the Bessel-potential space H^s with 2s > n agrees a.e. with a continuous function vanishing at infinity](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/BesselPotential/Embedding.html#TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev.exists_zeroAtInftyContinuousMap_ae_eq), building on Mathlib's lemma that its Fourier transform is integrable, and for integer k the representative gives a bounded linear map W^{k,2}(ℝⁿ) → C₀(ℝⁿ) (Folland, *Real Analysis*, §9.3).
name: The Sobolev embedding H^k(ℝⁿ) ⊆ C₀(ℝⁿ) for 2k > n

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, every k and an arbitrary open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, with no boundary regularity, the functions smooth on Ω are dense in W^{k,p}(Ω); the first-order case was announced earlier (Meyers–Serrin 1964; Evans §5.3.2).
name: The Meyers–Serrin theorem at every order

about: for an adapted pseudo-gradient of a function on a closed manifold and a critical point x of index k, the stable set W^s(x) is [a smooth submanifold of dimension n − k with the subspace topology](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Morse/StableManifold.html#TauCeti.IsAdaptedPseudoGradient.exists_stableSet_isManifold) and the image of a smooth embedding of a vector space sending 0 to x, and for a Morse function likewise [W^u(x), of dimension k](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Morse/StableEmbedding.html#TauCeti.IsAdaptedPseudoGradient.exists_isSmoothEmbedding_unstableSet); this is the manifold version of the Euclidean gradient-flow statement announced earlier (Audin–Damian, §2.1).
name: The stable manifold theorem for Morse flows on a closed manifold

about: [a map with a trivialisation around every point of its base has the homotopy lifting property for every finite-dimensional cube](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/SerreFibration/FiberBundle.html#TauCeti.hasHomotopyLiftingProperty_cube_of_exists_trivialization), with no paracompactness or other hypothesis on the base, so the projection of any fibre bundle in Mathlib's sense is a Serre fibration in the sense announced yesterday (Hatcher, Prop 4.48).
name: Fibre bundles are Serre fibrations

about: for a linear map A between finite-dimensional inner product spaces with singular values σ₀ ≥ σ₁ ≥ ⋯ and orthonormal families u₁, …, u_k and v₁, …, v_k, |Σᵢ ⟨uᵢ, A vᵢ⟩| ≤ σ₀ + ⋯ + σ_{k−1}, [with equality for the leading singular pairs](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/KyFan.html#LinearMap.exists_orthonormal_sum_inner_eq_kyFanSum); hence the Ky Fan sums are [subadditive](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/KyFan.html#LinearMap.kyFanSum_add_le), [σ(A + B) is weakly majorised by σ(A) + σ(B)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/KyFan.html#LinearMap.isWeaklyMajorizedBy_singularValues_add) and [σᵢ(CA) ≤ ‖C‖·σᵢ(A)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.html#LinearMap.singularValues_comp_le), and [symmetric gauges are monotone for weak majorisation](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/Majorization.html#TauCeti.IsWeaklyMajorizedBy.apply_le) (Fan 1951; Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, II.1, IV.1).
name: Ky Fan's maximum principle

about: for E a finite-dimensional inner product space, every isometry of E × (0, ∞) with the metric (‖dx‖² + dt²)/t², announced earlier, is a similarity (x, t) ↦ (cAx + b, ct) with c > 0 and A orthogonal, or such a similarity followed by the inversion in a sphere centred on the boundary hyperplane; for E = ℝ² this is the isometry group of ℍ³ (Ratcliffe, *Foundations of Hyperbolic Manifolds*, §4.6).
name: The isometries of the upper half-space model, classified

about: for convex u, v on a bounded open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, continuous up to the boundary, with Aleksandrov measures MA_u ≤ MA_v and v ≤ u on ∂Ω, one has v ≤ u on Ω, so [the Dirichlet problem has at most one solution](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Comparison.html#TauCeti.eqOn_of_mongeAmpereMeasure_eq_of_eqOn_frontier); and [the Monge–Ampère measure is weakly continuous](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Convergence.html#TauCeti.tendsto_mongeAmpereMeasure): if convex F_k → u locally uniformly on Ω then MA_{F_k} → MA_u weakly, with limsup on compacts, liminf on opens and convergence on continuity sets; both continue the Aleksandrov measure announced earlier (Gutiérrez, *The Monge–Ampère Equation*, §§1.2, 1.4).
name: The comparison principle for the Monge–Ampère equation

about: on a Polish geodesic space, [for any μ, ν at finite distance there is a measure on C([0, 1], X) concentrated on geodesics whose endpoint law is an optimal coupling, and its time marginals form a constant-speed W_p geodesic for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Geodesic.html#TauCeti.exists_ae_mem_geodesicPaths_wassersteinEDist_timeMarginal_eq), every two-time projection being optimal, so the Wasserstein space is geodesic; [λ-geodesic convexity of energies](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/GeodesicConvex.html#TauCeti.GeodesicallyConvex), displacement convexity on Wasserstein space, with [the global slope formula |∂φ|(x) = sup_y ((φ(x) − φ(y))/d(x, y) + (λ/2)·d(x, y))⁺](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/GeodesicConvex.html#TauCeti.GeodesicallyConvex.descendingSlope_eq_iSup) and lower semicontinuity of the slope; and [the continuity equation ∂ₜμₜ + div(vₜμₜ) = 0 in distributional form](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/ContinuityEquation.html#TauCeti.IsContinuityEquation), [solved by the laws of a family of absolutely continuous curves following v](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/ContinuityEquation.html#TauCeti.isContinuityEquation_map) (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, §§2.4, 7.2, 8.1; Villani, Ch. 7).
name: Wasserstein geodesics, and P_p(X) is a geodesic space

about: for f ∈ C²_c(ℝⁿ), n ≥ 3, the potential u = Γ ⋆ f of the Newtonian kernel Γ, announced earlier as a fundamental solution, is as smooth as f, satisfies −Δu = f, is harmonic off supp f, and is [the unique C² solution tending to 0 at infinity](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/FundamentalSolution/Euclidean/Potential.html#TauCeti.eq_newtonianKernel_convolution_of_laplacian_eq_neg); [in the plane, with Γ = −(2π)⁻¹ log|z|](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/FundamentalSolution/Planar/Potential.html#TauCeti.laplacian_planarNewtonianKernel_convolution), the same holds for the unique solution v with v − Γ·∫f → 0 at infinity (Evans §2.2.1, Thm 1).
name: The Newtonian potential solves Poisson's equation

about: over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, including 2, the Borel subgroups of Sp₂ₘ are exactly the conjugates of the stabiliser of the standard isotropic flag, so [any two are conjugate](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Symplectic/IsotropicFlag/Borel.html#TauCeti.Symplectic.IsotropicFlag.exists_conjugate_eq_of_isBorelOverAlgClosed); via an invariant Lagrangian and the Lie–Kolchin theorem (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, Thm 11.1, §23).
name: Borel subgroups of the symplectic group

about: two nondegenerate finite quadratic modules (ℚ/ℤ-valued quadratic forms on finite abelian groups) are isometric iff their polar bilinear forms are isometric and their Gauss-sum invariants in ℤ/8 agree (Nikulin, *Integral symmetric bilinear forms*, Thm 1.11.3; proof after Deloup–Massuyeau, Cor 4.2).
name: Nikulin's comparison theorem for finite quadratic forms

about: for subsets Uᵢ containing x whose interiors cover X, with every triple intersection path connected, homomorphisms π₁(Uᵢ, x) → K agreeing on pairwise intersections extend uniquely to π₁(X, x) → K; the two-set and common-overlap forms were announced earlier (Hatcher, Thm 1.20).
name: Seifert–van Kampen for a cover by neighbourhoods with varying overlaps

about: for F' = F·k' with k'/k finite and no separability assumed, [[k' : k]·(g' − 1) ≤ [F' : F]·(g − 1)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantExtension/Genus.html#TauCeti.finrank_mul_genus_sub_one_le_of_constantCompositum_eq_top), hence g' ≤ g (Stichtenoth III.6; Tate 1952).
name: The genus does not increase under a finite constant field extension

about: over a perfect constant field, in every characteristic including 2, a genus-two function field is a separable extension of degree two of a rational subfield, the separability being automatic (Stichtenoth, Lemma 6.2.2).
name: Every function field of genus two is hyperelliptic

about: as ε → 0⁺ the entropic cost inf_π (∫c dπ + ε·KL(π‖μ⊗ν)), announced earlier, [converges to the infimum of ∫c dπ over finite-entropy couplings](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Entropic/ZeroTemperature.html#TauCeti.tendsto_entropicTransportCost_nhdsGT_zero), which equals the transport cost for continuous costs on compact spaces and more generally for discretisable costs, and [weak limits of entropic optimisers are optimal plans](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Entropic/ZeroTemperature.html#TauCeti.isOptimalCoupling_of_tendsto_of_entropicTransportCost) (Carlier–Duval–Peyré–Schmitzer 2017).
name: The zero-temperature limit of entropic optimal transport

about: at a place of good reduction the inertia group acts trivially on torsion of order prime to the residue characteristic, the easy direction of the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion; [reduction is injective on the whole torsion subgroup](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/TorsionReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.injOn_reductionHom_torsion) when the ramification index of the residue characteristic p is less than p − 1, so over ℚ at every odd prime, hence [#E(F)_tors divides #Ẽ(k) for a finite residue field](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/TorsionReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.card_torsion_dvd_card_reduction); [good ordinary and good supersingular reduction](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MinimalModel/OrdinaryReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodOrdinaryReduction) are defined, with their dichotomy and independence of the minimal model; and as worked examples, [the rational torsion of 11.a3, y² + y = x³ − x², is ℤ/5](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/DivisionPolynomial/Torsion/WorkedExamples.html#TauCeti.WorkedExamples.curve11a3TorsionAddEquiv) and [(0, 0) on 37.a1, y² + y = x³ − x, has infinite order, so its rank is at least 1](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/WorkedExamples.html#TauCeti.WorkedExamples.finrank_point_curve37a1_pos) (Silverman VII.3.1, VII.4.1, VIII.7).
name: Good reduction and torsion
