about: for a smooth proper curve E → S with a section that is locally on S the projective model of a Weierstrass curve, the addition morphism E ×_S E → E and the negation glued from the Weierstrass charts make E [a commutative group object of Over S](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Geom/GroupLaw.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurveGeom.isCommMonObj), compatibly with base change; yesterday's announcement covered the Weierstrass model over an affine base (Katz–Mazur, §§2.1–2.2).
name: An elliptic curve over any base scheme is a commutative group scheme

about: a continuous φ with φ(t) ≤ c + K·∫ₐᵗ φ satisfies φ(t) ≤ c·e^{K(t − a)} (Mathlib has the differential form); hence in a Gelfand triple V ↪ H ↪ V* with A(t) satisfying Gårding's inequality, a weak solution of u' + A(t)u = f obeys [‖u(t)‖²_H + α·∫‖u‖²_V ≤ e^{2βt}·(‖u(0)‖²_H + α⁻¹·∫‖f‖²)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Parabolic/EnergyEstimate.html#TauCeti.HasWeakLineDerivOn.norm_sq_add_mul_integral_le_of_gelfandDual) and [is unique](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Parabolic/EnergyEstimate.html#TauCeti.HasWeakLineDerivOn.eqOn_of_gelfandDual) (Evans §7.1.2, Thms 2 and 4).
name: Grönwall's inequality in integral form, and the energy estimate for linear parabolic equations

about: paths of variable duration L stopped at time L, whose concatenation adds durations, so that [Moore loops at a point form a strictly associative and unital topological monoid](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore.html#TauCeti.MooreLoopSpace), where the usual loop space is associative only up to homotopy; [Moore paths are homotopy equivalent over X × X to paths on the unit interval](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore/Comparison/Basic.html#TauCeti.MoorePath.homotopyEquivUnitPath) and [the Moore loop space to the loop space](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore/Comparison/Basic.html#TauCeti.MooreLoopSpace.homotopyEquivPath), compatibly with concatenation; and [the free Moore loop space](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore/FreeLoop.html#TauCeti.MooreFreeLoopSpace) with its component of contractible loops (Whitehead, *Elements of Homotopy Theory*, Ch. III).
name: Moore paths and the Moore loop space

about: π_{n+1}(X, x) → H_{n+1}(X; R), [p] ↦ p_*[Iⁿ⁺¹], defined through the generator of H_{n+1}(Iⁿ⁺¹, ∂Iⁿ⁺¹; R), natural in based maps and sending the identity to 0; that it is a homomorphism, and the Hurewicz theorem, are still to come (Hatcher §4.2).
name: The Hurewicz map

about: a CM action of a ring R on an elliptic curve is an injective ring homomorphism R → End(E), and E [has geometric CM](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Hom/ComplexMultiplication.html#WeierstrassCurve.HasGeometricCM) when its endomorphism ring over the separable closure is larger than ℤ, which in positive characteristic includes the supersingular case; ℤ[i] acts on y² = x³ + a₄x by (x, y) ↦ (−x, iy), and ordinary curves over finite fields have geometric CM through Frobenius; the structure of End(E) is still to come (Silverman III.9, V.3).
name: Complex multiplication

about: for a sequence of extended-real functionals Fₙ on a first-countable space that Γ-converges to f in the sequential sense ([liminf inequality and recovery sequences](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Semicontinuity/GammaConvergence.html#TauCeti.TendstoGamma)) and is [equicoercive](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Semicontinuity/GammaConvergence.html#TauCeti.Equicoercive), the infima of the Fₙ converge to the infimum of f, which [is attained](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Semicontinuity/GammaConvergence.html#TauCeti.TendstoGamma.exists_isMinOn), and cluster points of minimisers minimise f; sequential Γ-convergence is [equivalent to the Γ-liminf and Γ-limsup both being f](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Semicontinuity/GammaConvergence.html#TauCeti.tendstoGamma_iff_gammaLiminf_eq_and_gammaLimsup_eq) (Braides, *Γ-convergence for Beginners*, Ch. 1; Dal Maso, Chs. 7–8).
name: The fundamental theorem of Γ-convergence

about: for a word over a linear order, the first row of its Robinson–Schensted insertion tableau has the length of a longest weakly increasing subsequence, and [for words with distinct letters](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Combinatorics/Young/LongestSubsequence.html#TauCeti.exists_sortedLT_sublist_length_iff_le_length_headD_robinsonSchensted_fst) of a longest strictly increasing one; the decreasing-subsequence half is still to come, and the input is Fulton's row bumping lemma, that inserting x then y places the second new cell [weakly above and strictly right of the first when x ≤ y](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Combinatorics/Young/Schensted/Bumping.html#TauCeti.rowInsert_column_lt_of_le) and [strictly below and weakly left when y < x](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Combinatorics/Young/Schensted/Bumping.html#TauCeti.rowInsert_column_le_of_lt) (Schensted, *Canad. J. Math.* 13, 1961; Fulton, *Young Tableaux*, §1.1).
name: Schensted's theorem on longest increasing subsequences

about: over an algebraically closed field, a function field of genus g ≥ 2 has finitely many automorphisms, provided the Weierstrass gaps at every place are pairwise distinct in the field, which is automatic in characteristic 0; on the way, the number of Weierstrass points lies [between 2g + 2](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/Weierstrass/Count.html#TauCeti.two_mul_genus_add_two_le_ncard_setOf_weierstrassWeight_ne_zero) and [g³ − g](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/Weierstrass/Count.html#TauCeti.ncard_setOf_weierstrassWeight_ne_zero_le_genus_pow_three_sub_genus), [with equality at 2g + 2 exactly for hyperelliptic fields](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Differential/Weierstrass/Count.html#TauCeti.isHyperellipticFunctionField_iff_ncard_setOf_weierstrassWeight_ne_zero_eq); the Hurwitz bound 84(g − 1) is not claimed (Farkas–Kra, *Riemann Surfaces*, III.5, III.7, V.1).
name: The automorphism group of a curve of genus at least two is finite

about: for linear maps A, C between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, if every Ky Fan sum σ₀(A) + ⋯ + σₖ₋₁(A) is at most the corresponding sum for C then N(A) ≤ N(C) for every unitarily invariant seminorm N, because [A then lies in the convex hull of the two-sided unitary orbit {UCV}](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/FanDominance.html#LinearMap.mem_twoSidedUnitaryOrbitHull_iff_kyFanSum_le), and conversely; with it the [nuclear](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm/KyFan.html#TauCeti.UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm.nuclear), [Ky Fan](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm/KyFan.html#TauCeti.UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm.kyFan) and [Frobenius](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm/Frobenius.html#TauCeti.UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm.frobenius) norms as unitarily invariant seminorms and a [rectangular singular value decomposition](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SingularValues.html#LinearMap.exists_linearIsometryEquiv_eq_comp_toLin_comp); Ky Fan's maximum principle was announced earlier (Fan, *Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci.* 37, 1951; Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, Thm IV.2.2).
name: Fan's dominance theorem

about: for functors F, G from a category to chain complexes of modules, if F is free on a family of model objects and G is [acyclic on the models](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AcyclicModels.html#TauCeti.AcyclicModels.IsAcyclicOn), a natural transformation in degree 0 compatible with the augmentations extends to a natural chain map F → G, and [two such natural chain maps are naturally chain homotopic](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AcyclicModels.html#TauCeti.AcyclicModels.ModelPresentation.homotopy); stated in the model-presentation form in which coefficients need not be unique, for the comparison of cubical and simplicial chains (Eilenberg–Mac Lane, *Amer. J. Math.* 75, 1953; Massey, *Singular Homology Theory*, Ch. VII).
name: The method of acyclic models

about: every finite group G has a finite central stem extension 1 → M → Ĝ → G → 1, with M inside the centre and the commutator subgroup of Ĝ, whose transgression Hom(M, kˣ) → H²(G, kˣ) is a bijection, for k algebraically closed of characteristic 0; the underlying lifting criterion says a projective representation with factor set α [lifts to a linear representation of the extension defined by γ, with the kernel acting through a character χ, exactly when the class of γ pushed along χ is the class of α](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ProjectiveRepresentation/Linearization.html#TauCeti.IsProjectiveRep.characterTransgression_eq_iff_exists_linearization); the universal lifting property and the identification of M with the Schur multiplier H₂(G, ℤ) are still to come (Karpilovsky, *Projective Representations of Finite Groups*, Chs. 2–3).
name: Schur's representation groups exist

about: in a nondegenerate unimodular integral lattice of any signature, even or odd, every characteristic vector w (one with w·x ≡ x·x mod 2 for all x) satisfies w·w ≡ signature (mod 8), proved through Milgram's formula on the discriminant form of the even sublattice; for w = 0 in an even lattice this is the classical 8 ∣ signature (van der Blij, *Indag. Math.* 21, 1959; Milnor–Husemoller, *Symmetric Bilinear Forms*, App. 4).
name: Van der Blij's lemma

about: an elliptic curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring in which 2 is a unit acquires good reduction over some finite extension if and only if its j-invariant is integral; the sufficiency direction is new and goes through the Legendre form, [which every elliptic curve attains over a finite separable extension when 2 ≠ 0](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Legendre.html#WeierstrassCurve.exists_variableChange_smul_baseChange_eq_freyCurve_one); residue characteristic 2 is excluded (Silverman, *AEC*, VII.5.5, III.1.7).
name: Potential good reduction and the integrality of j

about: for a self-adjoint densely defined partial operator A on a real or complex Hilbert space, every non-real z is a resolvent point with [‖(z − A)⁻¹‖ ≤ 1/|Im z|](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/LinearPMap/Resolvent.html#IsSelfAdjoint.norm_resolvent_le) and [(z − A)⁻¹* = (z̄ − A)⁻¹](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/LinearPMap/Resolvent.html#IsSelfAdjoint.adjoint_resolvent), so the spectrum is real and closed; separately, [spectral mapping for resolvents](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Module/LinearPMap/Resolvent/SpectralMapping.html#TauCeti.LinearPMap.notMem_spectrum_resolvent_iff) of an unbounded operator on any topological module over a field: for μ ≠ 0, μ lies outside the spectrum of (z − A)⁻¹ exactly when z − 1/μ is a resolvent point of A; Mathlib has the real spectrum only for bounded operators (Reed–Simon I, Ch. VIII; Engel–Nagel, IV.1).
name: The spectrum of a self-adjoint unbounded operator is real

about: for T bounded on L²(ℝⁿ) and represented off the support by a kernel satisfying Hörmander's condition with constant B, the mean oscillation of Tf over every ball is at most 2(5^{n/2}‖T‖ + B)‖f‖_∞ for f ∈ L² ∩ L^∞, the endpoint of the weak (1, 1) and Lᵖ bounds announced earlier, with no packaged BMO space yet; also [a kernel satisfying the standard Calderón–Zygmund estimate ‖K(x, y) − K(x, y′)‖ ≤ C|y − y′|^δ / |x − y′|^(n+δ) satisfies the Hörmander condition](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/CalderonZygmund/StandardKernel.html#TauCeti.setLIntegral_enorm_sub_le_of_norm_sub_le_mul_rpow), so [such operators are of weak type (1, 1)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/CalderonZygmund/StandardKernel.html#ContinuousLinearMap.mul_volume_lt_enorm_le_of_norm_sub_le_mul_rpow) (Stein, *Harmonic Analysis*, Ch. IV; Grafakos, *Modern Fourier Analysis*, Ch. 3).
name: Singular integrals map bounded functions to BMO

about: for an abstract Tits system (B, N) with simple reflections S, every subgroup containing B is P_J = B W_J B for a unique J ⊆ S, and [J ↦ P_J is an order isomorphism from subsets of S to the subgroups above B](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Parabolic/Classification.html#TauCeti.TitsSystem.standardParabolicOrderIso); the standard parabolics and their Bruhat decomposition were announced earlier (Bourbaki, *Lie*, IV §2.5, Thm 3; Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §29).
name: The subgroups containing B in a Tits system are the standard parabolics

about: over a field of characteristic 0, the weight-d space of the Weyl module S_μ(kⁿ) of GLₙ has dimension the Kostka number K_{μ,d}, the number of semistandard tableaux of shape μ and content d; in particular [the highest weight has multiplicity one](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/WeylModule/Weight/Multiplicity.html#TauCeti.finrank_weightSpace_weylRepOfShape_weightOfShape), [also for the rational Weyl modules of every dominant weight](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/WeylModule/Weight/Multiplicity.html#TauCeti.finrank_weightSpace_rationalWeylRep_self) (Fulton–Harris, Lectures 6 and 15; Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I §5).
name: Weight multiplicities of Weyl modules are Kostka numbers

about: for an elliptic curve E over a field K with m invertible and a family of extensions L_i of K, the [Shafarevich–Tate group](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/GaloisCohomology/Selmer.html#WeierstrassCurve.shafarevichTateGroup) Ш is the kernel of H¹(G_K, E) → ∏ H¹(G_{L_i}, E) and the [m-Selmer group](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/GaloisCohomology/Selmer.html#WeierstrassCurve.selmerGroup) is the preimage of Ш in H¹(G_K, E[m]), in the language of Selmer structures, and 0 → E(K)/mE(K) → Sel_m → Ш[m] → 0 is exact, with [the last map surjective](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/GaloisCohomology/Selmer.html#WeierstrassCurve.selmerShaMap_surjective); the family of extensions is a parameter, so the classical case of all completions of a number field, and finiteness of Sel_m, are not yet instantiated; the Kummer sequence into H¹(G_K, E)[m] was announced earlier (Silverman, *AEC*, X.4.2; Rubin, *Euler Systems*, I.1).
name: The Selmer group, the Shafarevich–Tate group and the m-descent sequence

about: [Hurewicz fibrations](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/HurewiczFibration.html#TauCeti.IsHurewiczFibration) (homotopy lifting against every space) are [Serre fibrations](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/HurewiczFibration.html#TauCeti.IsHurewiczFibration.mem_serreFibrations), closed under composition and base change, and [the loop map Ωp of a Hurewicz fibration is a Hurewicz fibration](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/LoopSpaceFibration.html#TauCeti.IsHurewiczFibration.loopMap); every map p : E → B factors through E′ = {(e, γ) : γ a Moore path from p(e)}, whose endpoint map is a Hurewicz fibration with a strictly transitive lifting function, so that the fibre carries a strict action of the Moore loop space, and [the inclusion e ↦ (e, constant path), a map over B, is a homotopy equivalence](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore/Replacement/Basic.html#TauCeti.MooreReplacement.homotopyEquiv); when p is already a Hurewicz fibration [the inclusion is a fibre homotopy equivalence](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore/Replacement/Equiv.html#TauCeti.MooreReplacement.fiberHomotopyEquiv), and [the path-space fibration, endpoint evaluation on Moore paths starting in a subset, is a Hurewicz fibration](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/PathSpace/Moore/Replacement/Equiv.html#TauCeti.MoorePath.isHurewiczFibration_target); Moore paths were announced earlier (Whitehead, *Elements of Homotopy Theory*, I.7; Hurewicz, 1955).
name: Hurewicz fibrations, and the Moore-path replacement of a map by a fibration

about: [if a prime P of A/(f) lies over a prime Q with A_Q regular and some derivation D has D(f) ∉ Q, then the local ring of A/(f) at P is regular](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Hypersurface.html#Ideal.isRegularLocalRing_localization_of_derivation_notMem); hence for an irreducible f ∈ k[X, Y] over any field with f, ∂f/∂X, ∂f/∂Y generating the unit ideal, the coordinate ring k[X, Y]/(f) is a Dedekind domain (Fulton, *Algebraic Curves*, §3.2, Thm 1; Stacks, Tag 00NQ).
name: The Jacobian criterion for hypersurfaces, and smooth plane curves have Dedekind coordinate rings

about: an H¹ weak solution of −∂ⱼ(Aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = f on an open set Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, with A a constant uniformly elliptic matrix and f locally in every W^(k,2), agrees almost everywhere with a C^∞ function on Ω, so in particular the weak Dirichlet solution of −Δu = f on a ball is smooth for smooth f; the input is the interior Sobolev embedding [W^(k+j,2)(Ω) ⊆ Cʲ(Ω) for 2k > n](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/Wkp/ContDiffRepresentative.html#TauCeti.Wkp.exists_contDiffOn_ae_eq); constant coefficients and p = 2 only, with no boundary regularity (Evans, *PDE*, §6.3.1, Thm 3; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Cor. 8.11).
name: Interior regularity for constant-coefficient elliptic equations

about: for an energy φ : X → [−∞, ∞] on a metric space, φ_τ(x) = inf_y (φ(y) + d(x, y)²/2τ) with its [resolvent J_τ x, the set of minimisers](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/MoreauYosida/Basic.html#TauCeti.moreauYosidaResolvent), [the slope bound |∂φ|(y) ≤ d(x, y)/τ for y ∈ J_τ x](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/MoreauYosida/Basic.html#TauCeti.descendingSlope_le_of_mem_moreauYosidaResolvent), [the energy–dissipation sum along a minimising-movement sequence](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/MoreauYosida/Basic.html#TauCeti.apply_add_sum_le_of_forall_mem_moreauYosidaResolvent); then [τ ↦ φ_τ(x) has derivative −d(x, y_τ)²/(2τ²) at all but countably many τ](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/MoreauYosida/Derivative.html#TauCeti.hasDerivAt_toReal_moreauYosida) for any selection y_τ ∈ J_τ x where the values are finite, and for φ lower semicontinuous at x with φ(x) < ∞, [φ_σ(x) + ∫₀^σ d(x, y_r)²/(2r²) dr = φ(x)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/MoreauYosida/Derivative.html#TauCeti.moreauYosida_add_integral_eq), De Giorgi's identity behind the convergence of the minimising movement scheme; existence of minimisers is not proved (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, *Gradient Flows*, §§2.4, 3.1, Thm 3.1.4).
name: The Moreau–Yosida approximation, and De Giorgi's variational interpolation

about: a curve u is an [EVI_λ solution](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/EVI.html#TauCeti.IsEVISolution) of an energy φ on a pseudometric space when ½ d⁺/dt d(u_t, y)² + (λ/2) d(u_t, y)² ≤ φ(y) − φ(u_t) for every y of finite energy; for lower semicontinuous φ the energy is non-increasing along u, the integrated form and regularisation estimate hold, and two solutions satisfy d(u_t, v_t) ≤ e^(−λt) d(u₀, v₀), so [on a metric space a solution is determined by its initial point](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/GradientFlow/EVI.html#TauCeti.IsEVISolution.eqOn); existence is not proved (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Ch. 4).
name: Evolution variational inequalities and their λ-contraction

about: on an n-dimensional real inner product space, ‖K_t ⋆ f‖_∞ ≤ (4πt)^(−n/2p) ‖f‖_p for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and t > 0, for Banach-space-valued f, [likewise for the Lᵖ heat semigroup](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HeatKernel/Smoothing.html#TauCeti.eLpNorm_heatSemigroup_top_le), and [every Lᵖ datum with p < ∞ has a C^∞ representative at each positive time](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HeatKernel/Smoothing.html#TauCeti.exists_contDiff_ae_eq_heatSemigroup) (Davies, *Heat Kernels and Spectral Theory*, Ch. 2; Evans, §2.3.1).
name: Ultracontractivity of the heat semigroup

about: for a cyclic Galois extension E/K with generator g and character χ with χ(g) = 1/[E : K], every Brauer class of K split by E is the cup product a ∪ δχ for some a ∈ Kˣ, [this class is the inflation of the cyclic class of a](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Brauer/Cyclic.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.relBrInfl_cyclicClass), and [it vanishes exactly when a is a norm from E](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Brauer/Cyclic.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.unitsRepH2Equiv_characterCarryCocycle_eq_zero_iff), so Br(E/K) ≅ Kˣ/N(Eˣ) (Serre, *Local Fields*, XIV §1; Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII, Lemma 8.5).
name: Brauer classes split by a cyclic extension are cyclic algebras

about: if B is a finite CW complex and p : E → B a d-sheeted covering map, then [E has finite CW type, with cells lifted from B](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/Covering.html#IsCoveringMap.finiteCWType), and χ(E) = d·χ(B) (Hatcher, §§1.3, 2.2).
name: The Euler characteristic is multiplicative in finite covers

about: a Cⁿ map between real or complex Banach spaces, 1 ≤ n ≤ ω, has Mathlib's chart-level immersion normal form at a point as soon as its derivative there has a continuous left inverse, and [for finite-dimensional target exactly when the derivative is injective](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Immersion/Differential.html#ContDiffOn.isImmersionAt_iff_injective_fderiv); model spaces only, not general manifolds (Hirsch, *Differential Topology*, Ch. 1 §3).
name: The local immersion theorem

about: for a finite group G acting on a commutative ring A, every G-invariant morphism Spec A → X to an arbitrary scheme factors uniquely through Spec A → Spec Aᴳ, which was known in the library only for affine X; on the way, [the projection is an epimorphism of schemes](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Quotient/FiniteGroup/UniversalProperty.html#TauCeti.AffineInvariantQuotient.instEpiProjection) (SGA 3, Exp. V §1; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, §7, Thm 1).
name: Spec Aᴳ is the quotient of Spec A by a finite group among all schemes

about: for an elliptic curve over an arbitrary base scheme and n ≠ 0, [n] : E → E is a finite morphism, by Mathlib's Zariski main theorem; over a field, [[n] on the projective Weierstrass model is flat](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/MulBy.html#WeierstrassCurve.flat_projModelMulBy) and [K(E) has degree n² over [n]*K(E)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/MulBy.html#WeierstrassCurve.finrank_fieldRange_mulByFunctionFieldPullback), and in general [the rank of a finite flat dominant morphism of integral schemes at every point is the degree of the function fields](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/FiniteFlatDegree.html#AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank_eq_finrank_fieldRange_functionFieldMap); that E[n] is finite locally free of rank n² over the base is not yet assembled (Katz–Mazur, 2.3.1; Stacks, Tag 02KA).
name: Multiplication by n on an elliptic curve is finite, of degree n²

about: over any commutative ring, a Weierstrass curve with a point (x, y) at which the 2- and 3-division polynomials are units admits exactly one change of variables taking it to [y² + axy + by = x³ + bx²](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/TateNormalForm.html#WeierstrassCurve.tateNormalForm) with (x, y) ↦ (0, 0); for an elliptic curve the unit conditions are also necessary, [the discriminant is computed](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/TateNormalForm.html#WeierstrassCurve.tateNormalForm_Δ), and [the universal Tate normal form over ℤ[A, B][Δ⁻¹]](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/TateNormalForm.html#WeierstrassCurve.UniversalTate.curve) classifies all of them (Silverman, *AEC*, Ex. 8.13; Kubert, 1976).
name: Tate normal form

about: for a Weierstrass curve over a field with a valuation and any integral model, whose reduction may be singular, [the points reducing to nonsingular points form a subgroup E₀](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/NonsingularReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.nonsingularReduction), [reduction is a homomorphism E₀ → Ẽ_ns(k)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/NonsingularReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.nonsingularReductionHom) with [kernel E₁, the points whose x-coordinate has a pole](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point/NonsingularReduction.html#WeierstrassCurve.Affine.nonsingularReductionHom_eq_zero_iff), and it is surjective when the valuation ring is Henselian, by Hensel's lemma for the Weierstrass equation; the good-reduction homomorphism was announced earlier (Silverman, *AEC*, VII.2.1).
name: The reduction exact sequence 0 → E₁ → E₀ → Ẽ_ns(k) → 0

about: for a T₁ space M and a point x with a chart to an n-dimensional real normed space, H_k(M, M ∖ {x}; R) is [zero for k ≠ n](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/LocalHomology.html#TauCeti.isZero_singularHomology_complSingleton_of_ne) and isomorphic to the coefficients R for k = n, the groups whose generators are local orientations (Hatcher, §3.3).
name: Local homology of a manifold point

about: for a quadratic form with trivial radical on a finite-dimensional space over a nontrivially normed locally compact field, the special orthogonal group is compact if and only if the form is anisotropic, and [over ℝ if and only if the form is definite](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/QuadraticForm/OrthogonalGroup/Real.html#TauCeti.QuadraticMap.isCompact_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff_posDef_or_negDef) (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, §43).
name: SO(Q) is compact exactly when Q is anisotropic

about: every Riemannian isometry of the Thurston geometry Nil, the Heisenberg group with its left-invariant metric, is a left translation followed by an orthogonal automorphism, and [the stabiliser of the identity is exactly O(2)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Nil/Stabilizer.html#TauCeti.Nil.range_orthogonalToIsom_eq_stabilizer) (Scott, *The geometries of 3-manifolds*, §4).
name: The isometry group of Nil is Nil ⋊ O(2)

about: for u ∈ W^(1,p)(Ω), p ≥ 1, Ω open in an n-dimensional real inner product space, and K ⊆ Ω of diameter at most R whose 2R-neighbourhood lies in Ω, if ∫_{B(x,r)} ‖∇u‖ ≤ M r^(n−1+α) for all x ∈ K and r ≤ 2R, then the precise representative of u is α-Hölder on K with a constant depending only on n, α and M; distinct from the Morrey embedding announced earlier (Morrey, *Multiple Integrals*, Thm 3.5.2; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 7.19).
name: Morrey's Dirichlet growth theorem

about: for an irreducible g ∈ k[X, Y], monic in Y, with g, ∂g/∂X, ∂g/∂Y generating the unit ideal, and F = k(x, y) with g(x, y) = 0 separable over k(x), the different exponent of F/k(x) at every place where x is regular equals ord_P(∂g/∂Y(x, y)); places over infinity are not covered (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.5.10).
name: The different of a smooth plane curve

about: on a real inner product space, if γ is a [three-plan whose (x, y₀) and (x, y₁) marginals are W₂-optimal couplings of μ with ν₀ and ν₁](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/GeneralizedGeodesic.html#TauCeti.exists_isGeneralizedGeodesicPlan), then along the [generalised geodesic ν_t = law of (1 − t)y₀ + t y₁](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/GeneralizedGeodesic.html#TauCeti.generalizedGeodesic) one has W₂(μ, ν_t)² + t(1 − t)∫‖y₀ − y₁‖² dγ ≤ (1 − t)W₂(μ, ν₀)² + t W₂(μ, ν₁)², so ν ↦ W₂(μ, ν)²/2 is 1-convex along generalised geodesics based at μ; and on a separable Banach space, for V m-strongly convex and measurable with negative part of at most quadratic growth, [the potential energy μ ↦ ∫V dμ is m-geodesically convex on P₂](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/PotentialEnergy.html#StrongConvexOn.geodesicallyConvex_potentialEnergy) along the displacement interpolation of an optimal plan; Wasserstein geodesics and the definition of geodesic convexity were announced earlier (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Lemma 9.2.1, Prop. 9.3.2).
name: Generalised geodesics in Wasserstein space, and displacement convexity of the potential energy

about: the [approximation numbers aₙ(T) = inf {{‖T − R‖ : rank R ≤ n}}](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/OperatorIdeal/ApproximationNumber/Basic.html#ContinuousLinearMap.singularValue) of a bounded operator between seminormed spaces satisfy the s-number axioms, [a_(m+n)(S + T) ≤ a_m(S) + a_n(T)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/OperatorIdeal/ApproximationNumber/Basic.html#ContinuousLinearMap.singularValue_add_index_le) and [a_(m+n)(ST) ≤ a_m(S)·a_n(T)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/OperatorIdeal/ApproximationNumber/Basic.html#ContinuousLinearMap.singularValue_comp_add_le_mul); a bounded operator into a Hilbert space is compact if and only if aₙ(T) → 0, [aₙ(T) = 0 exactly when rank T ≤ n over a complete field](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/OperatorIdeal/ApproximationNumber/Compact.html#ContinuousLinearMap.singularValue_eq_zero_iff_rank_le), and [bounded finite-rank operators are compact](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Compact/FiniteRank.html#LinearMap.HasFiniteRange.isCompactOperator) (Pietsch, *Eigenvalues and s-Numbers*, §§2.2–2.3; Gohberg–Kreĭn, Ch. II).
name: Approximation numbers, and compactness of operators into Hilbert space

about: [mutation of a smooth knot in a 3-manifold along a Conway sphere](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/KnotTheory/Mutation.html#TauCeti.conwayMutation), cutting along a four-punctured sphere in standard position and regluing after a half-turn, is symmetric, invariant under diffeomorphisms, and [realised on the unknot in S³](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/KnotTheory/Mutation.html#TauCeti.exists_isConwaySphere_unknot); the Kirk–Livingston theorem that mutation does not preserve smooth concordance is recorded as a statement and not proved (Conway, 1970; Lickorish, *An Introduction to Knot Theory*, Ch. 3).
name: Conway mutation

about: for an elliptic curve over any base scheme S, E[n] is the scheme-theoretic kernel of [n], [the fibre of [n] over the zero section](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Geom/Torsion.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurveGeom.isPullback_torsion), a closed proper commutative subgroup scheme compatible with base change, with [E[N](K) ≅ (ℤ/N)² over a separably closed field with N invertible](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/FieldPoints.html#WeierstrassCurve.nonempty_toEllipticCurveGeom_torsion_mulEquiv_prod); since [commutative group objects in a braided cartesian monoidal category form a preadditive category](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/CommGrp.html#CategoryTheory.CommGrp.instPreadditive), the converse of what Mathlib has, [elliptic curves over S have an abelian group Hom_S(E, E′) and a ring End_S(E)](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Geom/Hom.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurveGeom.toCommGrp) in which [the integer n is multiplication by n](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Scheme/Geom/Hom.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurveGeom.homMk_mulBy); finiteness and flatness of E[n] over S are not claimed (Katz–Mazur, §§2.3–2.5).
name: The torsion group scheme E[n] and the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve over a scheme

about: Ω(E) = 2∫ dx/√(4x³ + b₂x² + 2b₄x + b₆) over the set where the radicand is positive, as a Lebesgue integral, [finite and positive for an elliptic curve](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/RealPeriod.html#WeierstrassCurve.realPeriod_pos) and [scaling by |u| under a change of variables](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/RealPeriod.html#WeierstrassCurve.realPeriod_variableChange); its equality with ∫_E(ℝ) |ω| is not yet proved; with the regulator and Ш now in the library, of the four ingredients of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer quotient only the Tamagawa numbers remain to be defined (Silverman, *AEC*, III.1 and App. C §16).
name: The real period of an elliptic curve over ℝ

about: [the normalised cubical chains of a topological monoid form a differential graded algebra under the Pontryagin product](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Cubical/MonoidAlgebra/DGAlgebra.html#TauCeti.cubicalChain_isDGAlgebra), so [C_*(Ω_b B; R) of the Moore loop space is an augmented DG algebra](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/DGLocalSystem/LoopAlgebra.html#TauCeti.loopChain_isDGAlgebra), functorial in based maps; a DG local system on a pointed space is a right DG module over it, with [pullback along based maps as restriction of scalars](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/DGLocalSystem/Basic.html#TauCeti.DGLocalSystem.pullback), the coefficient notion of Floer and Morse homology with DG coefficients (Barraud–Damian–Humilière–Oancea, *Floer homology with DG coefficients*, §1.4, Def. 1.8).
name: DG local systems and the Pontryagin chain algebra of the loop space

about: [the category whose objects are elliptic curves over B-schemes and whose arrows are cartesian squares](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ModularCurve/Ell.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllObj), [fibred in groupoids over Sch/B](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ModularCurve/Ell.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllObj.isFibered_forget); moduli problems as presheaves on it, [relative representability](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ModularCurve/ModuliProblem.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuliProblem.RelRepData) with the affine, finite, flat and étale properties, [rigidity](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ModularCurve/ModuliProblem.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuliProblem.IsRigid), and [a representable moduli problem is rigid](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ModularCurve/ModuliProblem.html#TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuliProblem.isRigid_of_representableBy); no modular curve is constructed yet (Katz–Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, Ch. 4, A.4.1.2).
name: The Katz–Mazur category Ell/B and moduli problems for elliptic curves

about: every map of CW complexes is homotopic to a cellular map, and a map of relative CW complexes is homotopic, relative to the base, to a cellular map (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 4.8).
name: The cellular approximation theorem

about: for u ∈ W^{1,n}₀(Ω) in dimension n ≥ 2, ∫_Ω exp((|u|/(c‖∇u‖_{Lⁿ}))^{n/(n−1)}) ≤ e(nⁿ + 5)|Ω|, with an explicit c depending only on n (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 7.15).
name: Trudinger's inequality

about: for a finite discrete Galois module A over a finite extension F of ℚ_p, #H¹(F, A) = #H⁰(F, A) · #H²(F, A) · p^{[F:ℚ_p]·v_p(#A)} (Milne, *Arithmetic Duality Theorems*, I.2.8).
name: Tate's local Euler characteristic formula

about: for a strongly noetherian Tate ring A, every rational cover of a rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺) has an exact augmented Čech complex for the structure presheaf in every degree, extending the degree-zero sheaf property of TauCeti#11930 (Huber 1994, Thm 2.5; Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Lemma 8.34).
name: Tate's acyclicity theorem for strongly noetherian Tate rings

about: between finite-dimensional inner product spaces over ℝ or ℂ, the operator-norm distance from T to the maps of rank at most n is the n-th singular value σₙ(T) (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §7.4).
name: The Eckart–Young theorem in operator norm

about: unitarily invariant seminorms on linear maps between finite-dimensional inner product spaces correspond bijectively to symmetric gauge functions evaluated on the singular values (von Neumann 1937; Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, Thm IV.2.1).
name: Von Neumann's theorem on unitarily invariant norms

about: an elliptic curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring has potential good reduction if and only if its j-invariant is integral; TauCeti#14633 needed 2 to be a unit, and residue characteristic 2 is now included (Silverman, *AEC*, VII.5.5).
name: Potential good reduction and the integrality of j, in every residue characteristic

about: if a finite group G acts on a commutative ring A with g·a − a generating the unit ideal for each g ≠ 1, then A ⊗_{Aᴳ} A ≅ ∏_G A and Spec A → Spec Aᴳ is finite étale (Chase–Harrison–Rosenberg 1965, Thm 1.3).
name: Free actions of finite groups have finite étale quotients

about: for a convex w on a separable Banach space E, the interaction energy μ ↦ ∫∫ w(x − y) dμ(x) dμ(y) is geodesically convex on the 2-Wasserstein space P₂(E) (McCann 1997).
name: Displacement convexity of the interaction energy

about: for an odd prime p and integral lattices L, M with p ∤ det, L ⊗ ℤ_p ≅ M ⊗ ℤ_p iff the ranks agree and det L · det M is a square in ℤ_p (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 92:1).
name: Unimodular lattices at odd primes are classified by rank and determinant

about: every Riemannian isometry of the Thurston geometry Sol, ℝ³ with the metric e^{2z}dx² + e^{−2z}dy² + dz², is uniquely a left translation followed by one of eight dihedral automorphisms (Scott, *The geometries of 3-manifolds*, §4).
name: The isometry group of Sol is Sol ⋊ D₄

about: πₙ(X, x) as homotopy classes of n-simplices with boundary at x, a group for n ≥ 1 when X is a Kan complex, with induced homomorphisms; follows Joël Riou's open mathlib4#42435 (May, *Simplicial Objects in Algebraic Topology*, Ch. I).
name: Homotopy groups of Kan complexes

about: for a cochain complex K in an abelian category with an increasing ℤ-filtration F, the spectral sequence with E₁^{p,q} ≅ H^{p+q}(F_{q+1}/F_q), converging strongly to H*(K) when F is globally finite (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, §§5.4–5.5).
name: The spectral sequence of a filtered complex

about: for a topological group G acting continuously on a topological group A, the pointed set of continuous 1-cocycles G → A up to cohomology, with the exact inflation–restriction sequence 1 → H¹(G/N, Aᴺ) → H¹(G, A) → H¹(N, A) (Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, I.5).
name: Continuous nonabelian first cohomology H¹(G, A)

about: for the valuation ring O of a perfect valued field of characteristic p and a radius 0 < ρ < 1, the completion of W(O)[1/[ϖ]] for the Gauss norm λ_ρ, a complete Tate ring with a multiplicative norm and Kedlaya's degree, additive on products (Kedlaya, *Noetherian properties of Fargues–Fontaine curves*, §2).
name: The integral extended Robba rings A^r

about: a continuous map between CW complexes that is bijective on path components and induces bijections on all homotopy groups at every basepoint is a homotopy equivalence (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 4.5).
name: Whitehead's theorem

about: the discriminant Δ = Σ τ(n)qⁿ is an eigenform of every Hecke operator, so τ(mn) = τ(m)τ(n) for coprime m, n and τ(p^{r+2}) = τ(p)τ(p^{r+1}) − p¹¹τ(pʳ) for every prime p (Mordell 1917; Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII.4).
name: Ramanujan's τ is multiplicative (Mordell's theorem)

about: for a principal ideal domain k, 0 → ⊕_{p+q=n} Hₚ(X;k)⊗H_q(Y;k) → Hₙ(X×Y;k) → ⊕_{p+q=n−1} Tor₁(Hₚ(X;k), H_q(Y;k)) → 0 is exact, adding the Tor term to the field case of TauCeti#13648; the splitting is not included (Hatcher, Thm 3B.6).
name: The Künneth short exact sequence for singular homology

about: for −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) ≤ 0 with measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients on a connected open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, an H¹ subsolution whose essential supremum is attained on a compact subset of Ω is constant a.e., extending the C² case of TauCeti#1724 (Moser 1961; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 8.19).
name: The strong maximum principle for weak subsolutions of divergence-form equations

about: for self-adjoint operators T, S on a finite-dimensional inner product space with eigenvalues in decreasing order, Σᵢ (λᵢ(T) − λᵢ(S))² is at most the squared Frobenius distance Σₖ ‖Teₖ − Seₖ‖² (Hoffman–Wielandt 1953; Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, §VI.4).
name: The Hoffman–Wielandt inequality

about: for finite measures μ, ν of equal mass and a bounded measurable g, there are bounded potentials φ, ψ with exp(φ(x)+ψ(y)+g(x,y)) the density against μ ⊗ ν of a coupling of μ and ν (Fortet 1940; Nutz, *Introduction to Entropic Optimal Transport*).
name: Schrödinger potentials for a bounded kernel

about: for a Weierstrass cubic over a field F singular at a point whose tangent slopes lie in F, the group of nonsingular points is F at a cusp and Fˣ at a node, with explicit coordinates (Silverman, *AEC*, III.2.5).
name: The nonsingular points of a singular cubic form 𝔾ₐ or 𝔾ₘ

about: for F′ = F(y) with ∏_{c∈V}(y−c) = u, V a finite group of constants, 2g′−2 = |V|(2g−2) + (|V|−1)Σ_P (m_P+1) deg P over the places of reduced pole order m_P; the prime-field case yᵖ−y = u is TauCeti#11816 (Stichtenoth, Prop 3.7.10).
name: The Artin–Schreier genus formula for elementary abelian extensions

about: De Giorgi's limits of implicit Euler (minimizing movement) schemes for an energy on an extended metric space; one starts from every finite-energy point under coercivity, lower semicontinuity and compactness of bounded sublevels, and is ½-Hölder in time (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Ch. 2–3).
name: Generalized minimizing movements

about: now in full: a nonnegative weak solution of −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = 0 with measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients satisfies ess sup_{B(x₀,r)} u ≤ C ess inf_{B(x₀,r)} u on interior balls, in every dimension n ≥ 1 (Moser 1961; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 8.20).
name: Moser's Harnack inequality

about: for a base of a finite reduced crystallographic root system, the braid relations are the only relations among the simple reflections, and the Coxeter length of w is its number of inversions (Bourbaki, *Lie*, Ch. VI §1.5, Thm 2).
name: Tits' theorem: the Weyl group is a Coxeter system

about: if K contains the n-th roots of unity and Δ ≤ Kˣ, the field K(Δ^{1/n}) generated by the n-th roots of the elements of Δ is abelian Galois over K of degree [Δ : Δ ∩ (Kˣ)ⁿ] (Lang, *Algebra*, VI §8, Thm 8.1).
name: The degree of a Kummer extension

about: if Lu = aⁱʲ∂ᵢ∂ⱼu + bⁱ∂ᵢu is uniformly elliptic with bounded b on a compact K ⊆ ℝⁿ, c ≥ 0, and u ∈ C(K) ∩ C²(int K) satisfies Lu ≥ cu, then sup_K u ≤ sup_{∂K} u⁺ (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 3.1).
name: The weak maximum principle for elliptic operators in non-divergence form

about: now for every perfect constant field, not only algebraically closed ones as in TauCeti#13697: for F = F₁F₂ with F/F₁ separable, nᵢ = [F : Fᵢ], gᵢ = g(Fᵢ), g(F) ≤ n₁g₁ + n₂g₂ + (n₁ − 1)(n₂ − 1) (Stichtenoth, Thm 3.11.3).
name: Castelnuovo's inequality

about: for a self-adjoint, possibly unbounded, operator A on a complex Hilbert space, U = (A − i)(A + i)⁻¹ is unitary, 1 is not an eigenvalue of U, and A is recovered as i(1 + U)(1 − U)⁻¹ (Reed–Simon I, §VIII.3).
name: The Cayley transform of a self-adjoint operator is unitary

about: if generators of a group satisfy the exchange condition for their word length and their pairwise products have the orders of a Coxeter matrix M, then the group with these generators is the Coxeter system of M (Bourbaki, *Lie*, Ch. IV §1.6, Thm 1).
name: The exchange condition characterizes Coxeter systems

about: if G acts on a simply connected space covered by translates of a path-connected open set U, then G is presented by the g with gU meeting U, subject to s·t = st whenever U, sU, stU share a point (Macbeath 1964; Bridson–Haefliger, I.8.10).
name: Macbeath's theorem

about: on Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ of finite measure, a weak subsolution of −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) + cu ≤ f with c ≥ 0, f ∈ Lʳ, r > max(1, n/2), and (u − k)⁺ ∈ H¹₀(Ω) satisfies u ≤ k + C‖f‖_{Lʳ}|Ω|^{2/n−1/r}/λ (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 8.16).
name: Stampacchia's global bound for weak subsolutions

about: for a tableau t of shape λ ⊢ n, c_t² = (n!/f^λ) c_t with f^λ the number of standard tableaux, equivalently c_t² = (∏ hook lengths) c_t, and dim ℚ[Sₙ]c_t = f^λ (Fulton–Harris, Lemma 4.26).
name: Young symmetrizers are essentially idempotent

about: bounded operators u between Hilbert spaces with u u* u = u, equivalently isometric on (ker u)^⊥, equivalently with u*u an orthogonal projection; adjoints, isometries, unitaries and projections are examples (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*).
name: Partial isometries

about: a convex function on a subset of a finite-dimensional inner product space is differentiable at almost every point and has there a second-order Taylor expansion with a unique positive semidefinite symmetric Hessian (Rockafellar–Wets, *Variational Analysis*, Thm 13.51).
name: Alexandrov's theorem

about: a projective plane curve of degree d that is nonsingular over an algebraic closure has genus (d − 1)(d − 2)/2, over every constant field (Fulton, *Algebraic Curves*, §8.3).
name: The genus–degree formula for smooth plane curves

about: now for every smoothly embedded submanifold of Euclidean space, not only compact ones as in TauCeti#12027: inside any open neighbourhood of the image, an open set is diffeomorphic to the normal bundle, the zero section going to the embedding (Lee, *Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 6.24).
name: The tubular neighbourhood theorem

about: over a principal ideal domain the Künneth short exact sequence of TauCeti#15357 splits, so Hₙ(X × Y) ≅ ⊕_{p+q=n} Hₚ(X) ⊗ H_q(Y) ⊕ ⊕_{p+q=n−1} Tor₁(Hₚ(X), H_q(Y)), non-naturally (Hatcher, Thm 3B.6).
name: The Künneth formula for singular homology, with its splitting

about: a map from a measurable space to nonempty closed subsets of a Polish space that is weakly measurable ({z : M(z) meets U} measurable for every open U) has a measurable selection (Kechris, *Classical Descriptive Set Theory*, Thm 12.13).
name: The Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski selection theorem

about: for a place P' of the compositum E₁E₂ of intermediate fields of a finite separable extension of function fields, with P = P'|F of perfect residue field: if e(P'∩E₁|P) is prime to the characteristic, e(P'|P) = lcm(e(P'∩E₁|P), e(P'∩E₂|P)) (Stichtenoth, Thm 3.9.1).
name: Abhyankar's lemma

about: for every closed interval I ⊂ (0, ∞) the ring B^I is strongly noetherian: B^I⟨T₁/c₁, …, Tₙ/cₙ⟩ is noetherian for all positive radii (Kedlaya, *Noetherian properties of Fargues–Fontaine curves*, Thm 4.10).
name: Kedlaya's theorem on the interval rings of the Fargues–Fontaine curve

about: for absolutely continuous laws μ, ν on ℝⁿ with densities f, g and finite quadratic cost, the Brenier potential u satisfies f(x) = g(∇u(x)) det D²u(x) for a.e. x, D²u its Alexandrov Hessian (McCann 1997, Thm 4.4).
name: The Monge–Ampère equation for the Brenier map, almost everywhere

about: if U is A-invariant, W is invariant under a symmetric B on an inner product space, and the quadratic forms of A on U and B on W are separated by a gap g, then g‖P_W P_U‖ ≤ ‖B − A‖ (Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, §VII.3).
name: The Davis–Kahan sin Θ theorem

about: for a cyclic extension L/K of number fields, h(C_L) = [L : K] (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII Thm 4.3).
name: The Herbrand quotient of the idele class group

about: for Lu = −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ∂ᵢu + cu with uniformly elliptic a, bounded drift of any size and c ≥ 0, a weak subsolution with (u − k)⁺ ∈ H¹₀(Ω) is at most k, with no smallness condition on the drift as in TauCeti#8757 (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 8.1).
name: The weak maximum principle for divergence-form equations with bounded drift

about: a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form on a finite free module over a discrete valuation ring is an orthogonal sum of πⁱ-modular pieces, p = 2 included; so a nondegenerate ℤ_p-lattice is ⊕ pⁱLᵢ with Lᵢ unimodular (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 91:9).
name: Jordan splittings over a discrete valuation ring

about: for a smooth plane curve of degree n, (n − 3)(x)_∞ is a canonical divisor, L((n − 3)(x)_∞) is spanned by xⁱyʲ with i + j ≤ n − 3, and the regular differentials are the xⁱyʲ dx/g_Y (Fulton, *Algebraic Curves*, §8.5).
name: The canonical divisor of a smooth plane curve

about: over any field, in every characteristic, a curve with the same j-invariant as E is isomorphic to E or to the quadratic twist of E by a quadratic subextension of the separable closure, distinct subextensions giving non-isomorphic twists (Silverman, *AEC*, X.5.4).
name: The twists of an elliptic curve with j ∉ {0, 1728} are its quadratic twists

about: for a finite-valued lower semicontinuous cost on Polish spaces, a coupling of finite cost is optimal if and only if it is concentrated on a c-cyclically monotone set; the converse direction completes the forward one of TauCeti#13178 (Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Thm 5.10).
name: The Schachermayer–Teichmann theorem

about: for a Galois extension L/K, finite or infinite, the continuous cohomology H¹(Gal(L/K), L) of the additive group of L vanishes; in particular H¹(G_K, Kˢ) = 0 (Serre, *Local Fields*, X §1, Prop. 1).
name: The additive Hilbert 90

about: for a Hilbert space H and a vector space Φ with E : Φ × H → ℝ bilinear and coercive, E(φ, jφ) ≥ c p(φ)² where ‖jφ‖ ≤ p(φ), every linear ℓ with |ℓ| ≤ M p is E(·, u) for some u, ‖u‖ ≤ M/c (Showalter, *Monotone Operators in Banach Space*, III §2).
name: Lions' representation theorem

about: for p ≥ 1, μ σ-finite, ν s-finite and f ≥ 0 jointly measurable, (∫(∫ f(x, y) dν(y))^p dμ(x))^{1/p} ≤ ∫(∫ f(x, y)^p dμ(x))^{1/p} dν(y) (Folland, *Real Analysis*, Thm 6.19).
name: Minkowski's integral inequality

about: on a proper metric space and 1 ≤ p < ∞, every finite weighted family of laws with finite p-th moment has a p-Wasserstein barycenter, extending the real-line case of TauCeti#13576 (Le Gouic–Loubes 2017, Thm 8).
name: Existence of Wasserstein barycenters

about: a metric-measure space has Ricci curvature ≥ K in the sense of Sturm and Lott–Villani when the Boltzmann entropy relative to the reference measure is K-convex along W₂-geodesics; monotone in K, with approximate midpoints and a two-point non-example (Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Ch. 29).
name: The curvature-dimension condition CD(K, ∞)

about: φ : (ℤ/N)² → E(S) is a Drinfeld basis when the divisor ∑ₐ[φ(a)] is the closed subscheme E[N], meaningful where N is not invertible; stable under base change and GL₂(ℤ/N), it gives the moduli problem [Γ(N)] (Katz–Mazur, §3.1).
name: Drinfeld bases and the moduli problem [Γ(N)]

about: ⟨x, y, z⟩ is defined exactly when xy = yz = 0 and is a coset of x·H + H·z; the ternary operation m₃ of the transferred minimal model is one of its elements (Keller, *Introduction to A∞-algebras and modules*, §3.3).
name: Triple Massey products of A∞-algebras

about: over any field k, X ↦ k(X) is an anti-equivalence from regular proper curves over k with dominant k-morphisms to algebraic function fields of one variable over k, with inverse the normalisation of ℙ¹ in F (Stacks Project, Tag 0BXX).
name: The anti-equivalence between regular proper curves and function fields

about: for any scheme X, the relative spectrum of TauCeti#11787 and the pushforward of the structure sheaf are inverse anti-equivalences between quasi-coherent commutative 𝒪_X-algebras and schemes affine over X (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Ex. II.5.17).
name: The relative-Spec anti-equivalence

about: for any ring R, H₀(ℝPᴺ; R) ≅ R, Hₖ ≅ R/2R for odd k < N, Hₖ ≅ {r : 2r = 0} for even 0 < k ≤ N, H_N ≅ R for odd N, and zero above N (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Ex. 2.42).
name: The homology of real projective space

about: every linear map A between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces factors as A = U|A| with |A| = (A*A)^{1/2} and U a partial isometry with ker U = ker A, unique with that property (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*, VI.3).
name: The polar decomposition

about: for positive semidefinite real n × n matrices, det(A)^{1/n} + det(B)^{1/n} ≤ det(A + B)^{1/n}, so A ↦ det(A)^{1/n} is concave on the positive semidefinite cone (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §7.8).
name: Minkowski's determinant inequality

about: for a homeomorphism φ of any space F, the homology of the mapping torus T_φ sits in a long exact sequence ⋯ → Hₙ₊₁(T_φ) → Hₙ(F) → Hₙ(F) → Hₙ(T_φ) → ⋯ whose middle map is 1 − φ_* (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Ex. 2.48).
name: The Wang sequence of a mapping torus

about: now over every perfect constant field, not only algebraically closed ones as in TauCeti#14028: for a Kähler differential ω and prime elements t_P, Σ_P Tr_{F_P/k} res_{P,t_P}(ω/dt_P) = 0, with finitely many nonzero terms (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Cor. 4.3.3).
name: The residue theorem for function fields

about: for every elliptic curve E/S over any base, Drinfeld points of exact order N ≠ 0 on base changes of E are represented by a closed subscheme of E finite over S, with no invertibility of N assumed (Katz–Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, 3.6.0 and 5.1.1).
name: The Katz–Mazur moduli problem Γ₁(N) is relatively representable and finite

about: if k is the exact constant field of F and k′/k is separable algebraic, finite or infinite, then F·k′ over k′ has the same genus as F over k; so an algebraic closure of a perfect k preserves the genus (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.6.3).
name: The genus is invariant under separable algebraic constant field extensions

about: if |Δ_min(E)| ≪_ε N(E)^{6+ε} for all elliptic curves over ℚ, with N the conductor read off Tate's algorithm, then max(|a|, |b|, |c|) ≪_ε rad(abc)^{3/2+ε} for coprime a + b = c (Oesterlé, Sém. Bourbaki 694).
name: Szpiro's conjecture implies the abc conjecture with exponent 3/2

about: for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, ‖A‖_p is the ℓᵖ norm of the singular values of a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, a unitarily invariant norm with p = 1, 2, ∞ the nuclear, Frobenius and operator norms (Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, IV.2).
name: Schatten p-norms

about: u is a viscosity solution of det D²u = f when C² locally convex φ touching u from above at x₀ satisfy f(x₀) ≤ det D²φ(x₀), and dually from below; Aleksandrov solutions with continuous f ≥ 0 are viscosity solutions (Gutiérrez, *The Monge–Ampère Equation*, §1.3).
name: Viscosity solutions of the Monge–Ampère equation

about: on a Hilbert space, if A is self-adjoint and V is symmetric with ‖Vx‖ ≤ a‖x‖ + b‖Ax‖ on dom A for some b < 1, then A + V is self-adjoint on dom A (Reed–Simon II, Thm X.12).
name: The Kato–Rellich theorem

about: for a, b ∈ ℚˣ the Hilbert symbols (a, b)_v over all primes and the real place, written additively in ℤ/2, sum to zero; over a number field the law is proved whenever √b lies in a cyclotomic extension (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III §2).
name: Hilbert reciprocity over ℚ

about: for a cyclic extension L/K of number fields, the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L) has index at least [L : K] in the idele class group C_K (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII Cor. 4.4).
name: The first fundamental inequality

about: in characteristic zero, (kⁿ)^{⊗d} ≅ ⨁_{μ ⊢ d} k[S_d]c_μ ⊗ 𝕊^μ(kⁿ) as S_d × GLₙ(k)-representations, with c_μ the Young symmetrizers; the double-centralizer form was announced with TauCeti#5127 (Fulton–Harris, Thm 6.3).
name: The Schur–Weyl decomposition of (kⁿ)^{⊗d}

about: if max(|a|, |b|, |c|) ≪_ε rad(abc)^{1+ε} for coprime a + b = c, then max(|c₄|³, c₆²) ≪_ε N^{6+ε} for every elliptic curve over ℚ, with N the conductor computed by Tate's algorithm (Oesterlé, Sém. Bourbaki 694).
name: The abc conjecture implies the modified Szpiro conjecture

about: over a complete nonarchimedean field K, the residue field of every maximal ideal of K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩, and of every K-algebra topologically of finite type, is a finite extension of K (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, §6.1.2 Cor. 3).
name: The Nullstellensatz for Tate algebras

about: for the ring of integers 𝒪_F of a perfect nonarchimedean field F of characteristic p, the structure presheaf of 𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf) is a sheaf, so 𝒴 and 𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^ℤ are adic spaces with no remaining hypothesis (Fargues–Fontaine; Kedlaya, Thm 4.10).
name: 𝒪_𝒴 is a sheaf, so the Fargues–Fontaine curve is an adic space

about: a conformal map of the disc onto a bounded domain extends continuously to the closed disc exactly when the boundary of the domain is locally connected, extending the Jordan-domain case of TauCeti#5497 (Pommerenke, *Boundary Behaviour of Conformal Maps*, Thm 2.1).
name: Carathéodory's continuity theorem

about: if S, T ⊆ ℂ are closed and connected and S ∩ T is bounded and not connected, then S ∪ T separates the plane (Kuratowski, *Topology II*, §61).
name: Janiszewski's second theorem

about: for a Gelfand triple V ↪ H ↪ V* and A(t) bounded, measurable and satisfying Gårding's inequality, the problem u' + A(t)u = f, u(a) = u₀ has a unique weak solution in L²(a, b; V), now in full (Showalter, *Monotone Operators*, III §2).
name: Lions' theorem on linear parabolic equations

about: on a proper metric space and 1 ≤ p < ∞, every probability law on P_p(X) with finite p-th moment has a p-Wasserstein barycenter, extending the finitely supported case of TauCeti#15937 (Le Gouic–Loubes 2017, Thm 2).
name: Existence of population Wasserstein barycenters

about: on ℝⁿ, finitely many laws in P₂ have at most one quadratic barycenter when one of them has positive weight and is absolutely continuous; with TauCeti#15937 existence holds as well (Agueh–Carlier 2011, Prop. 3.5).
name: Agueh–Carlier uniqueness of Wasserstein barycenters

about: for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, μ ↦ Q_μ is an isometry from the Wasserstein space P_p(ℝ) onto the nondecreasing functions in Lᵖ(0, 1), so P₂(ℝ) is CAT(0) and every finite-second-moment population on it has a unique barycenter (Santambrogio, *Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians*, §2.2).
name: The quantile isometry of P_p(ℝ)

about: for symmetric A, B with invariant subspaces U, V, eigenvalues of A on U in [a, b] and of B on Vᗮ outside (a − δ, b + δ), δ‖P_{Vᗮ}P_U‖ ≤ ‖B − A‖ in every unitarily invariant norm, extending the operator-norm case of TauCeti#15976 (Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, VII.3).
name: The Davis–Kahan sin Θ theorem in unitarily invariant norms

about: a nonnegative matrix K has positive diagonal scalings D₁KD₂ with prescribed row and column sums exactly when some nonnegative matrix with those margins has the zero pattern of K, extending Sinkhorn's theorem of TauCeti#10733 to kernels with zero entries (Menon 1968; Brualdi 1968).
name: The Menon–Brualdi criterion for matrix scaling

about: for complex polynomials f₁, …, f_r whose product has degree d, ∏‖fᵢ‖ ≤ 2^d ‖∏fᵢ‖ and ‖∏fᵢ‖ ≤ 2^d ∏‖fᵢ‖ in the coefficient sup norm (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Lemma 1.6.11).
name: Gelfond's lemma

about: over any base scheme, an automorphism of an elliptic curve fixing a naive Γ(N)-structure, a pair of sections that is a basis of E[N] on every geometric fibre, is the identity for N ≥ 3; likewise Γ₁(N) for N ≥ 4 (Katz–Mazur, 2.7.2).
name: Rigidity of full level structures for N ≥ 3

about: for a metric measure space (X, d, m), the lower semicontinuous envelope on L²(m) of ½∫|Du|² dm over Lipschitz u, with |Du| the slope; it is convex and 2-homogeneous, and its finite domain is the Sobolev space W^{1,2}(X, d, m) (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Invent. Math. 2014, §4.1).
name: The Cheeger energy

about: Tan_μ P₂(ℝⁿ), the L²(μ)-closure of the gradients of test functions; its orthogonal complement is the divergence-free fields, and the projection onto it is the minimal-norm velocity with a given divergence (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, *Gradient Flows*, §8.4).
name: The tangent space of the Wasserstein space

about: Gohberg–Krein's symmetric gauges Φ on finitely supported sequences, with sup ≤ Φ ≤ sum and the extension to all sequences by truncation, the gauges that define symmetrically normed operator ideals (Gohberg–Krein, Ch. III).
name: Symmetric norming functions

about: for a, b ∈ ℚˣ the Hilbert symbols (a, b)_v over all primes and the real place, written additively in ℤ/2, sum to zero; over a number field the law is proved whenever √b lies in a cyclotomic extension (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III §2).
name: Hilbert reciprocity over ℚ

about: now in full: for ∂ₜu + L(t)u = f with u = 0 on ∂Ω, L(t) in divergence form with bounded measurable coefficients, each f ∈ L²(H⁻¹(Ω)) and u₀ ∈ L²(Ω) give exactly one weak solution in L²(H¹₀(Ω)) (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §7.1.2, Thms 3–4).
name: Existence and uniqueness of weak solutions of linear parabolic equations

about: now in full: for 1 < p < ∞ and X Polish, an absolutely continuous curve μ in P_p(X) of finite p-action is the marginals of a law η on absolutely continuous paths with |μ'|(t)ᵖ = ∫ |γ'|(t)ᵖ dη a.e. (Lisini 2007).
name: Lisini's superposition principle

about: for probability measures μ, ν and a bounded measurable cost c, the entropic cost inf_π ∫c dπ + ε KL(π‖μ⊗ν) equals max_{φ,ψ} ∫φ dμ + ∫ψ dν − ε∫(e^{(φ⊕ψ−c)/ε} − 1) d(μ⊗ν), attained by bounded potentials, unique up to constants (Nutz, *Introduction to Entropic Optimal Transport*).
name: Duality for entropic optimal transport

about: a well-oriented finite family of real polynomials in n variables has a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of ℝⁿ into analytic submanifolds on each of whose cells every member has constant order of vanishing (McCallum 1998, §5).
name: McCallum's projection theorem for cylindrical algebraic decomposition

about: real numbers α, β, γ are the interior angles of a convex hyperbolic triangle, ideal vertices allowed, exactly when α, β, γ ≥ 0 and α + β + γ < π (Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, Thm 7.16.2).
name: Hyperbolic triangles with prescribed angles

about: F_X is the identity on points and s ↦ sᵖ on sections when p = 0 on X; over a base S the relative Frobenius X → X ×_{S,F_S} S is natural, base-change compatible and a homomorphism for group schemes (Stacks, Tag 0CC6).
name: The absolute and relative Frobenius of a scheme

about: μ(ξ) ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of the p with |ξ − m/n| < C/nᵖ for infinitely many n; μ(ξ) = ∞ exactly for Liouville numbers, μ = 1 on ℚ, and μ is invariant under rational affine maps (Sondow 2004, Def. 2).
name: The irrationality exponent

about: over a field, the invariants of a finitely generated commutative algebra under a linearly reductive group, phrased as a comodule algebra over a linearly reductive bialgebra, form a finitely generated algebra (Mukai, *An Introduction to Invariants and Moduli*, Thm 4.51).
name: Hilbert's finiteness theorem for linearly reductive groups

about: if the commutator subgroup G′ of a group G is finitely generated of finite index, for instance G finite, the transfer G → G′/G″ is trivial, the group theory behind the principal ideal theorem (Artin–Tate, *Class Field Theory*, Ch. XIII).
name: Furtwängler's theorem

about: a complete local ring containing a field has a coefficient field: the reduction map onto its residue field has a ring-homomorphism section (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 28.3).
name: Cohen's theorem on coefficient fields

about: when N ≥ 4 is invertible on the base, elliptic curves with a point of naive exact order N are classified by maps to Y₁(N), cut out of the universal Tate normal form (Katz–Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, 2.2.3).
name: Y₁(N) is a fine moduli scheme for N ≥ 4

about: for an elliptic curve over any field K, P ↦ [𝒪(P − O)] is a group isomorphism from Mathlib's E(K) onto Pic⁰ of the projective Weierstrass scheme, upgrading the earlier set bijection (Silverman, *AEC*, III.3.4).
name: The points of an elliptic curve are Pic⁰ of its projective model

about: inside a fixed overfield, a number field K has only finitely many extensions of degree ≤ d unramified outside a finite set S of places; Mathlib has the bounded-discriminant form (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, III §2).
name: Hermite's theorem for extensions unramified outside S

about: for a real m×n matrix A and Q > 1, some nonzero integer vector y with |yⱼ| ≤ Q and integers xᵢ satisfy |∑ⱼAᵢⱼyⱼ − xᵢ| ≤ Q^(−n/m); Mathlib has the one-variable case (Schmidt, *Diophantine Approximation*, Ch. II).
name: Dirichlet's theorem for systems of linear forms

about: now in full: End(E) is an order in the imaginary quadratic field ℚ(π) generated by Frobenius, whose minimal polynomial is X² − a_qX + q (Silverman, *AEC*, V.3.1).
name: The endomorphism ring of an ordinary elliptic curve over a finite field

about: the inhomogeneous version: weak solutions of −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = f with measurable uniformly elliptic a and f ∈ Lʳ, r > max(1, n/2), are locally Hölder continuous, with the quantitative estimate (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thms 8.22 and 8.24).
name: De Giorgi's theorem with a right-hand side

about: if the target ν = gρ lives on a closed convex K with g > 0 a.e., some Brenier potential u has every subgradient in K and solves det D²u = g₀/g(∇u) in Aleksandrov's sense (Figalli, *The Monge–Ampère Equation*, §4.6).
name: Brenier solutions with a convex target are Aleksandrov solutions

about: the Dirichlet eigenvalues of −Δ on (a, b) are exactly (kπ/(b − a))², k ≥ 1, so (π/(b − a))² ∫u² ≤ ∫|u′|² on H¹₀(a, b) with the sharp constant, Wirtinger's inequality in its Dirichlet form (Brezis, *Functional Analysis*, §8.6).
name: The Dirichlet spectrum of −Δ on an interval, and the sharp Poincaré constant

about: for i.i.d. points with law μ of finite p-th moment in a separable metric space, almost surely every cluster point of any sequence of empirical Fréchet barycenters is a barycenter of μ (Bhattacharya–Patrangenaru, *Ann. Statist.* 31, 2003).
name: Strong consistency of Fréchet means

about: among orthonormal families w spanning the span of v, the minimum of ∑‖wⱼ − uⱼ‖² is 2∑(1 − cos θₖ) over the principal angles between the spans, attained by the aligned family (Schönemann, *Psychometrika* 31, 1966).
name: The orthogonal Procrustes problem for orthonormal frames

about: for an increasing filtration X_q of a space Y, the spectral sequence of the filtered singular chains, with E¹ = H_n(X_{q+1}, X_q), first differential the triple's connecting map, converging strongly to H_n(Y) for finite filtrations (McCleary, *A User's Guide*, §2.2).
name: The spectral sequence of a filtered space

about: filtering the total complex by rows gives a spectral sequence whose first page is the homology of the rows, converging to the homology of the total complex (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, §5.6).
name: The spectral sequence of a first-quadrant bicomplex

about: away from 3, a curve with an ordered basis (P, Q) of E[3] has a unique normal form Y²+3μXY+(μ³−1)Y = X³, P = (0, 0), giving the universal family over ℤ[1/3, ζ₃, μ, 1/(μ³−1)] (Katz–Mazur, 2.2.10).
name: The universal elliptic curve with a basis of its 3-torsion

about: the infimum of ‖d‖_{Lᵖ(π)} over couplings π of μ, ν and pseudometrics d on X ⊔ Y extending both metrics, an extended pseudodistance between metric-measure spaces, invariant under measure-preserving isometries (Sturm, *Acta Math.* 196, §3.1).
name: Sturm's transportation distance 𝔻

about: for an energy φ on P₂(E), the fields ξ ∈ L²(μ; E) with φ(ν) ≥ φ(μ) + ∫⟨ξ(x), y−x⟩ dγ + o(W₂(μ, ν)) along every optimal coupling γ: closed, convex, with a minimal selection (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, *Gradient Flows*, Ch. 10).
name: The Wasserstein subdifferential

about: S_N(μ | m) = −∫ρ^{1−1/N} dm of the curvature-dimension theory, with N(S_N(μ | m) + μ(X)) → Ent_m(μ), the Boltzmann entropy, as N → ∞ (Sturm, *Acta Math.* 196, II; Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Ch. 17).
name: Sturm's Rényi entropy functional

about: on an open star-convex subset of a real normed space, a closed C^r form of positive degree with values in a Banach space is the exterior derivative of a C^r form vanishing at the centre (Spivak, *Calculus on Manifolds*, Thm 4-11).
name: The Poincaré lemma for differential forms

about: now on Hilbert spaces of any dimension: every bounded T factors as T = U|T| with |T| = (T*T)^{1/2} and U the unique partial isometry vanishing on ker T (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*, VIII.3.11).
name: The polar decomposition of a bounded operator

about: now for two-line arrays, that is ℕ-matrices: row insertion of the bottom letters, recording the top letters, is a bijection onto pairs of semistandard tableaux of the same shape (Fulton, *Young Tableaux*, §4.1).
name: The Robinson–Schensted–Knuth correspondence

about: a finite-dimensional basic algebra over an algebraically closed field is a bound quiver algebra kQ/I, with Q a finite quiver and I an admissible ideal (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, Thm II.3.7).
name: Gabriel's presentation theorem for basic algebras

about: now in every dimension: for 1 < p < ∞ there is C with ‖D²u‖_p ≤ C‖Δu‖_p for every Schwartz function u on ℝⁿ (Stein, *Singular Integrals*, III §1.3).
name: The Calderón–Zygmund estimate for the Laplacian

about: now for locally Lipschitz coefficients: an H¹ weak solution of −div(a∇u) + b·∇u + cu = f with f ∈ L² and a uniformly elliptic lies in H²_loc (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 8.8).
name: Interior H² regularity for elliptic equations

about: in characteristic zero, a finite-dimensional Lie algebra has radical equal to its centre exactly when it is the direct sum of its centre and its derived ideal, the latter semisimple (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, I §6.4).
name: The structure theorem for reductive Lie algebras

about: over a field with admissible absolute values whose scalar height has the Northcott property, in particular any number field, Pⁿ(K) has finitely many points of bounded height (Hindry–Silverman, *Diophantine Geometry*, Thm B.2.3).
name: Northcott's theorem for projective heights

about: over any field with 2 invertible, the Spin group of three hyperbolic planes is SL₄, acting on the even half-spinors; for any nondegenerate six-dimensional form over a separably closed field, Spin(Q) ≅ SL₄ (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 20).
name: Spin₆ ≅ SL₄

about: over an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field, every point of Spa(K⟨T⟩, K⟨T⟩°) is classical, a Gauss-type point η_{a,r}, a nested-disc point, or a rank-two point η_{a,r⁺} or η_{a,r⁻} (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Ex. 7.57).
name: The five types of points of the adic closed unit disc

about: a holomorphic map of Riemann surfaces that is not locally constant at x is z ↦ z^k in suitable centred charts, k its local multiplicity, with the source chart inside any prescribed neighbourhood (Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, Thm 2.1).
name: The local normal form of a holomorphic map

about: over a Henselian local domain with finite residue field and 2 invertible, two symmetric forms are isometric exactly when their Jordan constituents are isometric index by index, so the Jordan invariants are unique (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 92:2).
name: Jordan splittings classify quadratic forms at odd residue characteristic

about: for an M × N matrix over 𝓞_K with entries of house at most A ≥ 1 and dM < N, d = [K:ℚ], the system ax = 0 has a nonzero solution in ℤᴺ with |xⱼ| ≤ (3NA)^{dM/(N−dM)} (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 3.20).
name: Siegel's lemma over a number field

about: the Grassmannian of rank-k locally free quotients of a finite module M over a ring R is proper over Spec R, by the valuative criterion, and separated for every M (EGA I, 9.7).
name: The Grassmannian scheme is proper

about: over a field of characteristic zero, polynomials g₁, …, g_m are linearly independent exactly when the Hasse Wronskian det(Dᵏgₗ) is nonzero (LeVeque, *Topics in Number Theory* II, Thm 4.7).
name: The Wronskian criterion for polynomials

about: on a Riemannian manifold, Δf = div grad f with the divergence the trace of the Levi-Civita derivative, and Δf(x) is the trace of the Hessian in any orthonormal basis of T_xM (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 2).
name: The Laplace–Beltrami operator

about: a decomposition of M into two subsets, each homeomorphic to the standard genus-g handlebody, meeting along their common frontier; the Heegaard genus is the least such g, a topological invariant, and S³ has genus 0 (Hempel, *3-Manifolds*, Ch. 2).
name: Heegaard splittings and the Heegaard genus

about: the closed subspace of L² of the circle spanned by the nonnegative Fourier modes; a function lies in it exactly when its negative Fourier coefficients vanish, and the modes eⁱⁿᶿ, n ≥ 0, form a Hilbert basis (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*).
name: The Hardy space H²

about: a compact connected Riemann surface with a finite holomorphic map to P¹ branched only over {0, 1, ∞}, their isomorphisms, and the isomorphism class of the monodromy permutation triple as an invariant (Girondo–González-Diez, *Dessins d'Enfants*, Ch. 3).
name: Analytic Belyi pairs

about: the minimisers of Σ wᵢ OT_ε(ν, μᵢ), each entropy taken against ν ⊗ μᵢ; as ε → 0 the costs Γ-converge to the weighted Wasserstein cost, and on compact spaces the barycenters converge to a unique Wasserstein barycenter (Chizat, arXiv:2303.11844).
name: Entropic Wasserstein barycenters

about: for a compactly supported C¹ n-form φ on an oriented smooth (n+1)-manifold with boundary, ∫_M dφ = ∫_∂M φ, with the induced boundary orientation (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 16.11).
name: Stokes' theorem on manifolds with boundary

about: for nonempty measurable A, B in ℝⁿ, |A + B|^{1/n} ≥ |A|^{1/n} + |B|^{1/n}, with outer measure on the sum, in every finite dimension (Gardner, *Bull. AMS* 39, 2002).
name: The Brunn–Minkowski inequality

about: if f(x)^{1−θ} g(y)^θ ≤ h((1−θ)x + θy) for measurable f, g, h ≥ 0 on ℝⁿ and 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1, then (∫f)^{1−θ} (∫g)^θ ≤ ∫h (Gardner, *Bull. AMS* 39, 2002, §7).
name: The Prékopa–Leindler inequality

about: for every group G, the orbit space of Milnor's countable join G ∗ G ∗ ⋯ has fundamental group G and trivial higher homotopy groups, so every group has a K(G,1) (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §1.B).
name: Milnor's classifying space is a K(G,1)

about: for a bounded operator T between Banach spaces, the range of T is closed exactly when the range of its adjoint T* is, and then range T* = (ker T)^⊥ (Rudin, *Functional Analysis*, Thm 4.14).
name: The closed range theorem

about: now in any field of characteristic zero: only finitely many algebraic numbers have degree at most d and absolute Weil height at most B (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Thm 1.6.8).
name: Northcott's theorem for the absolute height

about: for a differentiable k-form φ and vector field V on a manifold, the Lie derivative satisfies L_V φ = ι_V dφ + d(ι_V φ) (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 14.35).
name: Cartan's magic formula

about: if a sequence in a normed space converges weakly to x, then finite convex combinations taken from successive tails of the sequence converge to x in norm (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §2.5).
name: Mazur's lemma

about: the exponential map identifies such a group G with 𝔤/Λ as topological groups, where Λ = ker exp is a lattice of full rank in 𝔤 (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, I.(3.6)).
name: A compact connected commutative Lie group is its Lie algebra modulo a lattice

about: every nonzero affinoid algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field admits a finite injective algebra map from a Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §6.1.2).
name: Noether normalisation for affinoid algebras

about: for a closed absolutely continuous plane curve γ and a C¹ field (P, Q), ∮_γ P dx + Q dy = ∫ w_γ(z) (Q_x − P_y) dz, where w_γ is the winding number of γ (Cufí–Verdera, *Proc. AMS* 143, 2015).
name: Green's theorem for absolutely continuous curves

about: e_r · s_ν = Σ s_μ, the sum over the partitions μ with μ/ν a vertical strip of r cells, over any commutative semiring (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I.(5.17)).
name: The dual Pieri rule for Schur polynomials

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the absolute Galois group G_K is topologically finitely generated (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, (7.4.1)).
name: The absolute Galois group of a p-adic field is topologically finitely generated

about: now for absolutely continuous loops with square-integrable derivative, with its equality case: ∫‖f − f̄‖² ≤ ((b−a)/2π)² ∫‖f′‖², with equality exactly when f is its mean plus a first harmonic (Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya, *Inequalities*, Thm 258).
name: Wirtinger's inequality

about: every algebra homomorphism from a noetherian ultrametric Banach algebra into an affinoid algebra with a complete algebra norm is continuous; in particular homomorphisms of affinoid algebras are continuous (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, §6.1.3).
name: Automatic continuity for affinoid algebras

about: the de Rham complex of smooth forms on a manifold with corners under the exterior derivative, its cohomology as closed forms modulo exact forms, and pullback functoriality along smooth maps (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, Ch. I).
name: De Rham cohomology

about: Connes' complex of cyclic cochains with the Hochschild coboundary, its cohomology HCⁿ(A; M) for a unital algebra A, with HC⁰ the traces, functorial along algebra homomorphisms (Connes, *Noncommutative Geometry*, III.1).
name: Cyclic cohomology

about: the union of the ramified levels K⸨t^{1/n}⸩ inside Hahn series with rational exponents is a field, each level has degree n over K⸨t⸩, and the whole field is algebraic over K⸨t⸩ in every characteristic (Walker, *Algebraic Curves*, Ch. IV).
name: The field of Puiseux series

about: the irrationals ξ with q‖qξ‖ bounded below by a positive constant; they have irrationality exponent 2, and every real quadratic irrational is badly approximable (Cassels, *An Introduction to Diophantine Approximation*, Ch. I).
name: Badly approximable numbers

about: for a Lipschitz map f between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, ∫_A Jf·g dx = ∫ Σ_{x ∈ A ∩ f⁻¹(y)} g(x) dℋⁿ(y) for measurable A and g ≥ 0; with g = 1 the right side counts the fibre A ∩ f⁻¹(y) (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, §3.3).
name: The area formula

about: for every Tits system (G, B, N, S), the Weyl group W = N/(B ∩ N) with its simple reflections S is a Coxeter system, now in full after the exchange condition of TauCeti#9029 (Bourbaki, *Lie*, Ch. IV §2.4, Thm 2).
name: Tits' theorem for BN-pairs
