about: a ring that is complete for the adic topology of a finitely generated ideal I with R/I Noetherian is Noetherian; in particular the I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian for every ideal I (Atiyah–Macdonald, *Introduction to Commutative Algebra*, Thm 10.26).
name: Adic completions of Noetherian rings are Noetherian

about: for a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the absolute Galois group G_K has exactly [K : ℚ_p] + 2 topological generators, sharpening the finite generation announced from TauCeti#17192 (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, (7.4.1)).
name: The generator rank of a p-adic absolute Galois group

about: for any coefficient object R of an abelian category, H_k(ℂPⁿ; R) ≅ R for even k ≤ 2n, and H_k(ℂPⁿ; R) = 0 for odd k and for k > 2n (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §2.2).
name: The homology of complex projective space

about: two measured kernels on standard Borel probability spaces have Gromov–Wasserstein distance zero, for any exponent 0 < p ≤ ∞, exactly when they are weakly isomorphic, the converse of the pullback invariance in the earlier definition (Bauer–Mémoli–Needham–Nishino, *The Z-Gromov–Wasserstein distance*, 2025).
name: Zero Gromov–Wasserstein distance is weak isomorphism

about: for a bounded symbol a on the circle, T_a = P M_a|H² on the Hardy space, a bounded linear map in a with matrix entries ⟨e_i, T_a e_j⟩ = â(i − j), adjoint T_ā, and ‖T_a‖ ≤ ‖a‖_∞ (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*).
name: Toeplitz operators

about: for a C² real function f on a complex vector space, the Hermitian form whose matrix in holomorphic coordinates is (∂²f/∂z_j∂z̄_k), with sum, product and composition rules and the invariance L(f ∘ g)(v, w) = Lf(Dg·v, Dg·w) under holomorphic g (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, Ch. II).
name: The Levi form

about: integral lattices L and M on one rational quadratic space are p-neighbours when their intersection has index p in each; neighbours have equal determinants and, for p ∤ 2 det L, the same genus (Kneser–Scharlau, *Quadratische Formen*, §28).
name: Kneser neighbours

about: every finite-dimensional rational representation of a semisimple affine group over a field of characteristic zero is completely reducible, now for every semisimple group rather than those with nondegenerate Killing form (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Ch. 22).
name: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem for semisimple algebraic groups

about: in a real or complex locally convex space, the bipolar of any set A is the closed absolutely convex hull of A ∪ {0}; also being formalised in mathlib4#26345 (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §2.6).
name: The bipolar theorem

about: for a bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω and 1 ≤ p < ∞, ‖u − ⨍_Ω u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} ≤ C ‖∇u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} for every u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω), now for Sobolev functions on Lipschitz domains rather than C¹ functions on convex ones (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.8.1, Thm 1).
name: The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality on Lipschitz domains

about: over a Henselian discrete valuation ring, if v(F(y₀)) > 2 v(F′(y₀)) then F has a unique root z with v(z − y₀) > v(F′(y₀)), and v(F(y₀)) = v(F′(y₀)) + v(z − y₀); Mathlib has this over ℤ_p (Serre, *Local Fields*, Ch. II §4).
name: Hensel's lemma with an estimate

about: a point of projective space with algebraic coordinates has absolute height 1 exactly when every ratio of two nonzero coordinates is a root of unity (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Thm 1.5.9).
name: Kronecker's theorem for heights

about: a bounded set in n-dimensional Euclidean space has Lebesgue outer measure at most ω_n (diam s / 2)ⁿ, the volume of a ball of the same diameter (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, §2.2).
name: The isodiametric inequality

about: for subgroups U, V ≤ G and a representation ρ of U, the restriction to V of the tensor induction ⊗Ind_U^G ρ is the tensor product over the double cosets VsU of the tensor inductions from V ∩ sUs⁻¹ of the conjugates ρˢ (Evens 1963, §6.2).
name: The Mackey formula for tensor induction

about: for a connection on a Riemannian manifold, P = (Ric − Scal·g/(2(n−1)))/(n−2) and W = Rm − P ⊙ g, with the curvature symmetries, the first Bianchi identity, trace-freeness and vanishing on constant-curvature spaces (Besse, *Einstein Manifolds*, §1.G).
name: The Weyl tensor, the Schouten tensor and the Kulkarni–Nomizu product

about: |Du|(Ω) = sup{∫_Ω u div φ : φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω, ℝⁿ), ‖φ‖ ≤ 1} and De Giorgi's perimeter P(E; Ω) = |D𝟙_E|(Ω), with locality, lower semicontinuity under L¹_loc convergence and |Du|(Ω) ≤ ∫_Ω ‖∇u‖ for weakly differentiable u (Maggi, *Sets of Finite Perimeter and Geometric Variational Problems*, §12.1).
name: Perimeter and total variation by duality

about: the skew polynomial ring R[X; σ, δ] of an algebra endomorphism σ and a σ-derivation δ, with its monomial basis, the relation Xa = σ(a)X + δ(a) and its universal property (Cohn, *Free Rings and Their Relations*, Ch. 2).
name: Ore extensions

about: on the Hochschild cochains of a unital algebra, the cyclic operator λ, the cyclic norm N, the bar coboundary b′ and B = N s (1 − λ), with B² = 0 and bB + Bb = 0, the (b, B) mixed complex of cyclic cohomology (Loday, *Cyclic Homology*, §2.1).
name: Connes' operator B

about: a rigid monoidal category with a monoidal isomorphism X ≅ X^{∗∗}, with the Freyd–Yetter identity, left and right traces and dimensions, and the torsor of pivotal structures under Aut_⊗(𝟭); also being formalised in mathlib4#42150 (Etingof–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik, *Tensor Categories*, §4.7).
name: Pivotal categories

about: Noetherian rings all of whose finite-type algebras are catenary, stable under quotients, localisation and polynomial rings, with the criterion through polynomial rings and the local criterion over all primes (Stacks Project, Tag 00NL).
name: Universally catenary rings

about: the covolume of the S-unit lattice, the image of the S-logarithmic embedding, a full lattice of rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 + #S isomorphic to the S-units modulo torsion; the S-regulator is positive (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, §1.5).
name: The S-regulator

about: X ∧ Y = (X × Y)/(X ∨ Y) makes Mathlib's category of pointed types symmetric monoidal with unit S⁰, with associator, unitors and braiding (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Ch. 0).
name: The smash product of pointed sets

about: for an elliptic curve E over a number field K and every m ≥ 1, the m-Selmer group Sel_m(E/K), with local conditions at the finite places, is finite; earlier updates had only m = 2 (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.4.2).
name: Finiteness of the Selmer group

about: any two Borel subgroups of an affine algebraic group of finite type over an algebraically closed field, in any characteristic, are conjugate by a rational point (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, Thm 11.1).
name: Conjugacy of Borel subgroups

about: every uniformly convex real Banach space is reflexive (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, Thm 5.2.15).
name: The Milman–Pettis theorem

about: a normed space over ℝ or ℂ is reflexive if and only if its closed unit ball is weakly compact (Megginson, §2.6).
name: Kakutani's theorem on reflexivity

about: the image of the closed unit ball of a normed space under the canonical embedding into its bidual is weak-star dense in the closed unit ball of the bidual (Megginson, Thm 2.6.26).
name: Goldstine's theorem

about: a Banach space with a Schauder basis is reflexive if and only if the basis is both shrinking and boundedly complete (James 1950; Megginson, Thm 4.4.15).
name: James's basis criterion

about: for a semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the multiplicity of L(ν) in L(λ) ⊗ L(μ) is Σ_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) · dim L(μ)_{ν − w·λ}, where w·λ is the dot action (Humphreys, *Lie Algebras*, §24, Ex. 9).
name: The Racah–Speiser formula

about: if μ is minuscule, L(λ) ⊗ L(μ) is multiplicity-free: L(ν) occurs exactly once when ν − λ is a weight of L(μ), and not at all otherwise (Bourbaki, *Lie*, Ch. VIII §9, Ex. 2).
name: The minuscule Pieri rule

about: for a presentation ⟨S | R⟩, the fundamental group of its presentation complex is the presented group, the loop around the s-th circle going to the generator s (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Cor. 1.28).
name: The fundamental group of the presentation complex

about: over a field of characteristic zero, a geometrically connected affine group of finite type is reductive if and only if every finite-dimensional rational representation is completely reducible (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Ch. 22).
name: Reductive groups are linearly reductive in characteristic zero

about: a regular ring that is a domain is integrally closed, so every localization of a regular ring at a prime is an integrally closed domain (Stacks Project, Tag 0567).
name: Regular rings are normal

about: over a complete nonarchimedean field K, every Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ and every affinoid algebra is a Jacobson ring: each prime ideal is an intersection of maximal ideals (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §5.2.6).
name: Affinoid algebras are Jacobson rings

about: the symmetric decreasing rearrangement f* of a nonnegative function on a finite-dimensional normed space, radially non-increasing and equimeasurable with f, with the same Lᵖ seminorm for every p (Lieb–Loss, *Analysis*, §3.3).
name: The Schwarz rearrangement

about: the approximation, bounded approximation and metric approximation properties of a normed space, with the theorem that a Banach space with a Schauder basis has the bounded approximation property with its basis constant (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 1).
name: The approximation property

about: the Hankel operator H_a : H² → (H²)^⊥ of an L^∞ symbol a on the circle, with H_a = 0 iff a has no negative Fourier coefficients, and the Toeplitz identity T_a T_b − T_{ab} = −H_{ā}^* H_b (Conway, *A Course in Functional Analysis*).
name: Hankel operators

about: in a preadditive category with countable coproducts, if X is a retract of Y then X ⊕ ∐_{n ∈ ℕ} Y ≅ ∐_{n ∈ ℕ} Y (Neeman, *Triangulated Categories*, §1.6).
name: The Eilenberg swindle

about: the k-th order statistic of n iid real samples with cdf F has cdf Σ_{j ≥ k} C(n, j) F^j (1 − F)^{n−j}, and for uniform samples the law Beta(k, n + 1 − k) (David–Nagaraja, *Order Statistics*, §2.1).
name: Order statistics

about: T(h, a) = (2π)⁻¹ ∫₀^a e^{−h²(1+t²)/2} / (1+t²) dt, with its symmetries, both partial derivatives and the skew-normal identity ∫_{−∞}^x 2φ(t)Φ(αt) dt = Φ(x) − 2T(x, α) (Owen 1956).
name: Owen's T function

about: the logistic law with location m and scale s, with cdf (1 + e^{−(x−m)/s})⁻¹, its density, the quantile m + s log(u/(1−u)) and affine transport (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 2, Ch. 23).
name: The logistic distribution

about: for a real algebraic number α and κ > 2, only finitely many rationals ξ satisfy |ξ − α| ≤ H(ξ)^(−κ); so every real algebraic irrational has irrationality exponent two (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 6.2).
name: Roth's theorem

about: for a real algebraic number α of degree d ≥ 2 and κ > d/2 + 1, only finitely many rationals ξ satisfy |ξ − α| ≤ H(ξ)^(−κ) (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 6.9).
name: Thue's approximation theorem

about: in a real or complex Banach space, the continuous linear functionals that attain their norm on the closed unit ball are dense in the dual (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §2.11).
name: The Bishop–Phelps theorem

about: if φ is lower semicontinuous and bounded below on a complete metric space and ε > 0, every x admits y with φ(y) + ε·d(y, x) ≤ φ(x) and y the strict minimiser of φ + ε·d(·, y) (Phelps, *Convex Functions, Monotone Operators and Differentiability*, Ch. 3).
name: Ekeland's variational principle

about: for nonnegative measurable f, g on a finite-dimensional real normed space with Haar measure, ∫ f g ≤ ∫ f* g*, where f* is the Schwarz rearrangement (Lieb–Loss, *Analysis*, Thm 3.4).
name: The Hardy–Littlewood rearrangement inequality

about: for 1 < p < ∞ and every integer k ≥ 0, the weak-derivative Sobolev space W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) coincides with the Bessel-potential space H^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) (Stein, *Singular Integrals and Differentiability Properties of Functions*, Ch. V §3).
name: Calderón's theorem: W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) = H^{k,p}(ℝⁿ)

about: a bounded operator from a normed space into a Banach space is weakly compact if and only if its adjoint is weakly compact (Megginson, *An Introduction to Banach Space Theory*, §3.5).
name: Gantmacher's theorem

about: for p × n matrices A, B over a commutative ring, det(A Bᵀ) is the sum over p-element column sets S of det(A_S)·det(B_S), the products of corresponding maximal minors (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §0.8.7).
name: The Cauchy–Binet formula

about: a weak homotopy equivalence between arbitrary topological spaces, with no CW hypothesis, induces isomorphisms Hₙ(X; k) ≅ Hₙ(Y; k) for every ring k and every n (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Prop. 4.21).
name: Weak homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms on singular homology

about: at generic q, every finite-dimensional simple U_q(sl₂)-module is isomorphic to the highest-weight module L_m^ε for exactly one m ≥ 0 and sign ε (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, §VI.3).
name: Classification of the finite-dimensional simple U_q(sl₂)-modules

about: every C^n real vector bundle with finite-dimensional fibres over a σ-compact Hausdorff smooth manifold carries a C^n Riemannian metric; in particular every such manifold has a Riemannian metric (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Prop. 13.3).
name: Existence of Riemannian metrics

about: for any index set and real or complex scalars, a ↦ (x ↦ Σ aᵢxᵢ) is an isometric isomorphism from ℓ∞ onto the continuous dual of ℓ¹ (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 1).
name: The dual of ℓ¹ is ℓ∞

about: d(E, F) = inf ‖T‖‖T⁻¹‖ over isomorphisms T : E → F, with symmetry, the multiplicative triangle inequality, attainment in finite dimensions, and d = 1 exactly for isometric finite-dimensional spaces (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 12).
name: The Banach–Mazur distance

about: I_ν(x) for real order ν, with its power series, positivity, derivative, the recurrence I_{ν−1} − I_{ν+1} = (2ν/x) I_ν and small-argument asymptotics; a complex version is proposed in mathlib4#43070 (DLMF §10.25).
name: The modified Bessel function I_ν

about: of a real vector bundle and of a manifold, a two-sheeted covering with a free deck involution; a manifold is orientable iff the cover has a section, and a connected one iff the cover is disconnected (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Ch. 15).
name: The orientation double cover

about: pivotal categories whose left and right traces agree, with the resulting trace and quantum dimension, their cyclicity, duality invariance and multiplicativity under ⊗; also being formalised in mathlib4#42191 (EGNO, *Tensor Categories*, §4.7).
name: Spherical categories

about: the compositum of the abelian Galois subextensions of Ω/K, with Gal(K^{ab}/K) identified with the topological abelianization of Gal(Ω/K) whenever Ω/K is normal (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, Ch. I §1).
name: The maximal abelian extension K^{ab}

about: every finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is Morita equivalent to a bound quiver algebra kQ/I, with Q a finite quiver and I an admissible ideal, extending the basic-algebra case of TauCeti#16389 to all algebras (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, Cor. II.3.7).
name: Gabriel's presentation theorem

about: over a complete nonarchimedean field K the Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ has Krull dimension n, so a nonzero affinoid algebra A is finite over an embedded Tate algebra in exactly dim A variables (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §§5.2.2, 6.1.2).
name: Krull dimension of Tate algebras

about: for an integer binary form F of degree d with no repeated linear factor over ℂ and κ > 2, there is c > 0 with |F(x, y)| ≥ c·max(|x|, |y|)^(d − κ) whenever F(x, y) ≠ 0 (Evertse, *Diophantine Approximation*, Thm 6.3).
name: The Thue–Roth inequality for binary forms

about: a regular proper curve X over k with H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0, k integrally closed in k(X), and a k-rational point, or any divisor of degree one, is isomorphic to ℙ¹_k over k (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Prop. 1.6.3).
name: A genus-zero curve with a rational point is the projective line

about: for any index set ι and real or complex scalars, a ↦ (f ↦ Σᵢ aᵢ fᵢ) is an isometric isomorphism ℓ¹(ι) ≅ c₀(ι)*, so every functional Λ has norm Σᵢ |Λ(eᵢ)| (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Ch. 1).
name: The dual of c₀ is ℓ¹

about: for a convex set in P × F with finite-volume fibres over P, F a d-dimensional inner product space, the d-th root of the volume of the fibre over p is a concave function of p on the projection (Schneider, *Convex Bodies*, §7.1).
name: Brunn's concavity principle

about: over ℝ or ℂ, π_q(T) ≤ π_p(T) for 1 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ ∞, so every absolutely p-summing operator is absolutely q-summing, and π_∞(T) = ‖T‖ (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, *Absolutely Summing Operators*, Thm 2.8).
name: The inclusion theorem for absolutely summing operators

about: a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay when M = 0 or depth M = dim Supp M, and M is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when M/xM is, for x ∈ 𝔪 regular on M (Stacks 00N3).
name: Cohen–Macaulay modules

about: subalgebras Bᵢ are free with respect to a functional φ when φ vanishes on alternating products of centred elements from them; freeness and the restrictions of φ to the Bᵢ determine φ on the algebra they generate (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lecture 5).
name: Free independence

about: H^k_c(M), the cohomology of the complex of compactly supported smooth forms, with its comparison map to H^k_dR(M), an isomorphism for compact M, and pullback along smooth proper maps (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, §1).
name: Compactly supported de Rham cohomology

about: the least modulus 𝔪 of K whose ray subgroup of the idele class group lies in the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L); a modulus is admissible for L/K exactly when the conductor divides it (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, Ch. V).
name: The conductor of an abelian extension of number fields

about: B_k(δ) over any commutative ring: the free module on Brauer diagrams on k strands, multiplied by stacking with a factor δ per closed loop, of rank (2k − 1)‼ and containing the group algebra of S_k (Goodman–Wallach, *Symmetry, Representations, and Invariants*, §10.1).
name: The Brauer algebra

about: for a smooth symmetric nondegenerate metric g on an open set of ℝⁿ, the unique symmetric g-compatible bilinear map Γ, with Γ^k_ij = ½ Σ_l g^kl(∂_i g_jl + ∂_j g_il − ∂_l g_ij), the Levi-Civita connection for positive-definite g (O'Neill, *Semi-Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3).
name: Christoffel symbols

about: GEV(m, s, ξ) with its cdf and quantile, weak continuity in the parameters including the Gumbel limit at ξ = 0, and max-stability: the maximum of n copies is GEV with scale s·n^ξ and location m + s(n^ξ − 1)/ξ (Coles, *An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values*, Ch. 3).
name: The generalized extreme-value distribution

about: GPD(s, ξ) for every real shape, with density, cdf, quantile, the moments sⁿ n!/∏(1 − (j + 1)ξ) on nξ < 1, threshold stability for admissible thresholds, and the uniform, exponential and Pareto special cases (Coles, *An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values*, Ch. 4).
name: The generalized Pareto distribution

about: M(μ), the quotient of U_q(sl₂) by the left ideal (E, K − μ), with the basis F^j v₀ for q, μ ≠ 0 and the singular-vector criterion E·F^(j+1) v₀ = 0 ⟺ μ² = q^(2j) at generic q (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, §VI.3).
name: Verma modules of U_q(sl₂)

about: the law of the number of successes in independent Bernoulli trials with probabilities pᵢ, with its mass function, generating function ∏(1 − pᵢ + pᵢ z), and the binomial case for equal pᵢ (Wang, *Statistica Sinica* 3, 1993).
name: The Poisson binomial distribution

about: the law on ℤ of the difference of independent Poisson(r₁) and Poisson(r₂) counts, with its mass function, mean r₁ − r₂, variance r₁ + r₂, characteristic function and convolution by adding rates (Skellam, *J. Roy. Statist. Soc.* 109, 1946).
name: The Skellam distribution

about: for n ≥ 2 and a space with trivial homotopy groups below n, the Hurewicz homomorphism πₙ(X, x) → Hₙ(X; ℤ) is an isomorphism, now in full after the vanishing half of TauCeti#16017 (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 4.32).
name: The Hurewicz theorem

about: on a smooth manifold with boundary or corners, a C^r form of positive degree closed near a point is, near that point, the exterior derivative of a C^r form defined on all of M, extending the star-convex case of TauCeti#16833 (Lee, *Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 17.14).
name: The Poincaré lemma on manifolds

about: a closed C^r 2-form on an open subset of ℝⁿ, nondegenerate at x₀, is pulled back near x₀ by a C^r diffeomorphism fixing x₀ to its constant value ω(x₀) (Lang, *Fundamentals of Differential Geometry*, V Thm 8.1).
name: Darboux's theorem

about: for every finite Galois extension L/F of number fields, H¹(Gal(L/F), C_L) = 0 and |H²(Gal(L/F), C_L)| divides [L : F], C_L the idele class group (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VII Thm 5.1).
name: The second fundamental inequality

about: two structures in a relational language are potentially isomorphic, i.e. linked by a back-and-forth system of partial isomorphisms, exactly when they satisfy the same L_{∞ω} sentences; no countability is assumed (Karp 1965).
name: Karp's theorem

about: if 1, α₁, …, αₙ are linearly independent over ℚ, then for every θ ∈ ℝⁿ and ε > 0 infinitely many integers y and x ∈ ℤⁿ satisfy |yαᵢ − xᵢ − θᵢ| ≤ ε for all i (Hardy–Wright, Thm 442).
name: Kronecker's approximation theorem

about: a compact connected oriented n-manifold M has Hₙ(M; ℤ) ≅ ℤ, generated by the fundamental class [M], the unique class restricting to the given local orientation at every point (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 3.26).
name: The fundamental class of a compact oriented manifold

about: for open sets U, V of a σ-compact smooth manifold, 0 → Ω•(U ∪ V) → Ω•(U) ⊕ Ω•(V) → Ω•(U ∩ V) → 0 is a short exact sequence of de Rham complexes (Bott–Tu, Prop. 2.3).
name: The Mayer–Vietoris sequence for de Rham cohomology

about: πₖ(Sⁿ) = 0 for k < n, for the unit sphere of any (n+1)-dimensional real normed space, and πₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ for n ≥ 2 (Hatcher, Cor. 4.9 and 4.25).
name: Homotopy groups of spheres up to the dimension

about: the discounted risk-neutral expectation of a European call on a lognormal asset equals sΦ(d₊) − Ke^{−rτ}Φ(d₋), with d± = (log(s/K) + (r ± σ²/2)τ)/(σ√τ) (Shreve, *Stochastic Calculus for Finance II*, §5.2.5).
name: The Black–Scholes formula

about: for f K-Lipschitz on a subset A of a metric space into an m-dimensional normed space, ∫ ℋᵗ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dy ≤ ω_m K^m ℋ^{m+t}(A), as an upper integral with no measurability assumed (Mattila, *Geometry of Sets and Measures*, Thm 7.7).
name: Eilenberg's inequality

about: for a connected finite graph on at least two vertices and any orientation, the preprojective algebra is finite-dimensional iff the graph is of type A, D or E, completing the non-Dynkin direction of TauCeti#8970 (Reiten, *Notices AMS* 44, 1997).
name: Preprojective algebras are finite-dimensional exactly in Dynkin type

about: the marginal x ↦ ∫ f(x, y) dy of a measurable log-concave function f ≥ 0 on ℝⁿ × ℝᵐ is log-concave (Prékopa, *Acta Sci. Math.* 34, 1973).
name: Prékopa's theorem

about: if the spectra of self-adjoint operators A, B on finite-dimensional inner product spaces are at distance ≥ δ, then δ‖X‖ ≤ (π/2)‖AX − XB‖ for every unitarily invariant seminorm (Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, §VII.2).
name: The Bhatia–Davis–McIntosh bound

about: on a connected manifold without boundary, any point is carried to any other by a smooth isotopy of diffeomorphisms starting at the identity and fixed outside a compact set (Milnor, *Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint*, §4).
name: Milnor's homogeneity lemma

about: schemes whose local rings are all integrally closed domains; normality is local, normal schemes are reduced, and a locally noetherian normal scheme has discrete valuation rings at its codimension-one points (Stacks Project, Tag 033H).
name: Normal schemes

about: countably additive assignments of orthogonal projections on a Hilbert space to measurable sets, normalised to the identity, with the scalar measures E ↦ ⟨P(E)x, x⟩ (Reed–Simon I, §VII.2).
name: Projection-valued measures

about: for a strongly continuous ℝ-action on a C*-algebra and inverse temperature β, the states whose correlations ω(a αₜ(b)) continue analytically across a strip of width β to ω(αₜ(b) a); the 0-KMS states are the tracial states (Bratteli–Robinson II, Def. 5.3.1).
name: KMS states

about: the torsion of a based acyclic chain complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces, an alternating product of change-of-basis determinants, independent of the auxiliary boundary bases and lifts (Milnor, *Whitehead torsion*, §3).
name: Reidemeister torsion

about: the semicircle law on [−1, 1], the limiting eigenvalue distribution of Wigner matrices, built as an affine image of Beta(3/2, 3/2), with its moments, mean 0 and variance 1/4 (Anderson–Guionnet–Zeitouni, §2.1.1).
name: The Wigner semicircle distribution

about: Kashiwara's crystals over a root datum: a weighted set with partial raising and lowering operators whose string lengths satisfy φᵢ − εᵢ = ⟨wt, αᵢ∨⟩, with strict morphisms and duals; seminormal in Bump–Schilling's terminology (Kashiwara, *On crystal bases*, 1995).
name: Normal crystals

about: Gassmann equivalence: subgroups H, K of a finite group meeting every conjugacy class in equally many elements, equivalently |(G/H)^g| = |(G/K)^g| for every g; such H and K have the same index (Perlis, *J. Number Theory* 9, 1977).
name: Almost-conjugate subgroups

about: finitely generated modules whose localisation vanishes at every prime of height ≤ 1; over a two-dimensional noetherian local ring with finite residue field, such as ℤₚ⟦T⟧, these are exactly the finite modules (Washington, *Cyclotomic Fields*, §13.2).
name: Pseudo-null modules

about: for a number field K the localization map Br K → ⨁_v Br K_v over all places is injective: a central simple algebra over K that splits at every completion splits over K (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VIII Thm 4.2).
name: The Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem

about: in a countable relational language, every countable structure M has an L_{ω₁ω} sentence that holds in a countable structure exactly when that structure is isomorphic to M (Scott 1965; Marker, *Lectures on Infinitary Model Theory*).
name: Scott's isomorphism theorem

about: for a, b ∈ Kˣ in a number field K, the product of the Hilbert symbols (a, b)_v over all finite and real places of K is 1, now for every number field after the ℚ case of TauCeti#16252 (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI Thm 8.1).
name: Hilbert reciprocity

about: for a number field K and every x ∈ Br K, the local invariants inv_v(x) ∈ ℚ/ℤ sum to zero over all places of K (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, VIII Thm 4.2).
name: The sum formula for the local invariants of a Brauer class

about: every central section of the cube [−1, 1]ⁿ by a k-dimensional subspace V of ℝⁿ has k-dimensional volume at least 2ᵏ (Vaaler, *Pacific J. Math.* 83, 1979).
name: Vaaler's cube-slicing theorem

about: a function of finitely many complex variables that is continuous on an open set and holomorphic in each variable separately is analytic there (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, §2.2).
name: Osgood's lemma

about: for q ∈ ℂ nonzero and not a root of unity, every finite-dimensional module over the quantum group U_q(sl₂) is semisimple (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, Ch. VII).
name: Complete reducibility for U_q(sl₂)

about: for a flat morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes, the codimension of a point x of X is the codimension of f(x) plus the codimension of x in its fibre (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 15.1).
name: The dimension formula for flat morphisms

about: an s–t flow in a finite network is maximum exactly when it admits no augmenting path, exactly when its value equals the capacity of some cut separating s from t (Ford–Fulkerson, *Canad. J. Math.* 8, 1956).
name: The augmenting-path theorem

about: ℤ[aᵢⱼ] modulo the associativity and commutativity relations of X + Y + ∑ aᵢⱼ XⁱYʲ, carrying the universal commutative formal group law: ring maps L → R correspond to commutative formal group laws over R (Ravenel, *Complex Cobordism*, A2.1).
name: The Lazard ring

about: E is finitely representable in F when every finite-dimensional subspace of E embeds in F with distortion at most 1 + ε for every ε > 0; it is transitive and matches the Banach–Mazur-distance form (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Def. 11.1.1).
name: Finite representability of normed spaces

about: for T : E → F between topological modules, the fibre over 0 of the closure of the graph of T, the limits of T xₙ with xₙ → 0; between Banach spaces T is continuous exactly when it is zero (Dales, *Banach Algebras and Automatic Continuity*, §5.2).
name: The separating space of a linear map

about: every simplicial group is a Kan complex: if the simplices of a simplicial set form groups and all face and degeneracy maps are homomorphisms, every horn has a filler (May, *Simplicial Objects in Algebraic Topology*, Thm 17.1).
name: Moore's theorem

about: a finite free algebra over a commutative ring A is étale exactly when the discriminant of a basis is a unit of A; over a field, exactly when the trace form is nondegenerate (Stacks, Tag 0BJF).
name: The discriminant criterion for étaleness

about: every central slice of a product of Euclidean balls of volume one has volume at least one, so a k-dimensional complex slice of the unit polydisc has volume at least πᵏ; the cube case was TauCeti#19048 (Bombieri–Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Thm C.3.8).
name: Vaaler's slicing theorem for products of balls

about: for a continuous surjection from a profinite group G whose kernel lies in Φ(G), the intersection of the maximal open subgroups, every lift of a topologically generating family of the target generates G (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.8).
name: Generators lift along Frattini covers of profinite groups

about: over a complete ultrametric field, a bounded operator between null-sequence spaces C₀(J) → C₀(I) is a norm limit of finite-rank operators exactly when its matrix has bounded entries and row norms tending to zero (Serre, *Publ. Math. IHÉS* 12, 1962, §3 Prop. 4).
name: Serre's criterion for complete continuity

about: a bounded operator on a Banach space is absolutely summing exactly when it sends every unconditionally convergent series to an absolutely convergent series (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, *Absolutely Summing Operators*, Ch. 2).
name: Absolutely summing operators and unconditional convergence

about: for a polynomial or power series over a ring with a real additive valuation v, the lower convex envelope of the coefficient valuations n ↦ v(aₙ), with its behaviour under scaling, multiplication by Xᵏ and the substitution X ↦ cX (Cassels, *Local Fields*, Ch. 6).
name: Newton polygons

about: NC(n), the partitions of n ordered points with no a < b < c < d having a, c in one block and b, d in another, is a lattice under refinement, with join the least noncrossing common coarsening (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lecture 9).
name: The lattice of noncrossing partitions

about: a domain is N-1 when its normalization is finite over it, and Japanese (N-2) when its integral closure in every finite extension of its fraction field is finite; the two agree for Noetherian domains with perfect fraction field (Stacks, Tag 032F).
name: N-1 and Japanese domains

about: for a preadditive category D with a ℤ-shift, the category D/[n] with the objects of D and Hom(X, Y) = ⨁ⱼ Hom(X, Y⟦nj⟧), with its additive faithful projection from D and the periodicity isomorphism (Keller, *On triangulated orbit categories*, 2005, §1).
name: Keller's orbit category

about: two PSC metrics g₀, g₁ on M are concordant when some PSC metric on M × ℝ equals g₀ + dt² for t ≤ 0 and g₁ + dt² for t ≥ 1; concordance is an equivalence relation (Gromov–Lawson, *Ann. of Math.* 111, 1980).
name: Concordance of positive scalar curvature metrics

about: an elliptic curve over a nonarchimedean local field has good reduction exactly when inertia acts trivially on its ℓ-adic Tate module, for any prime ℓ different from the residue characteristic (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VII Thm 7.1).
name: The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion

about: for a finite-dimensional Lie algebra L with nondegenerate Killing form in characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional L-module M, every derivation L → M is inner and every 2-cocycle is a coboundary, so H¹(L, M) = H²(L, M) = 0 (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, §7.8).
name: Whitehead's lemmas

about: a weakly convergent sequence in ℓ¹(I), over ℝ or ℂ and for any index set I, converges in norm, so weak and norm convergence of sequences agree in ℓ¹ (Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Thm 2.3.6).
name: Schur's theorem for ℓ¹

about: two aspherical spaces of CW type are homotopy equivalent, by an equivalence inducing any prescribed isomorphism of fundamental groups up to basepoint change; in particular every K(G, 1) of CW type is homotopy equivalent to Milnor's classifying space (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 1B.8).
name: Uniqueness of K(G, 1) spaces of CW type

about: for a finite Cohen–Macaulay module M over a Noetherian local ring R, every associated prime p satisfies dim R/p = dim M, and the associated primes are exactly the minimal primes of the support, so M has no embedded primes (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 17.3).
name: Cohen–Macaulay modules are unmixed

about: for every continuous curve γ on [a, b] in a finite-dimensional inner product space, the total variation of γ equals the integral of the number of preimages of y against 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure, with no Lipschitz or bounded-variation hypothesis (Federer, *Geometric Measure Theory*, 2.10.13).
name: The Banach indicatrix formula

about: over an algebraically closed field, the orbit of a rational point under a finite-type group scheme acting on a finite-type scheme is locally closed: open in its closure, with boundary a closed set of strictly smaller dimension (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §1.8).
name: Orbits of algebraic group actions are locally closed

about: over a complete nonarchimedean field K, the Tate algebra K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩ of restricted power series is a unique factorisation domain, hence integrally closed (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, *Non-Archimedean Analysis*, §5.2.6).
name: Tate algebras are unique factorisation domains

about: for polynomials f and g over a ring with an additive valuation, the Newton polygon of fg is the Minkowski sum of the Newton polygons of f and g, and their multisets of finite slopes add (Koblitz, *p-adic Numbers, p-adic Analysis, and Zeta-Functions*, IV §3).
name: The Newton polygon of a product

about: over a field of characteristic zero, if ad e is nilpotent, [h, e] = 2e, h ≠ 0 and h ∈ [e, L], there is a unique f making (h, e, f) an sl₂-triple, with no finite-dimensionality assumed (Jacobson, *Lie Algebras*, III §11).
name: Morozov's lemma

about: for any finite simple graph Γ, its Artin braid group acts on the homotopy category of graded modules over the zigzag algebra of Γ, each generator acting by tensoring with the two-term complex Pᵢ ⊗ eᵢZ → Z (Huerfano–Khovanov, *A category for the adjoint representation*, §4.6).
name: The Khovanov–Seidel braid group action

about: over a complete ultrametric ring R with a pseudo-uniformiser, measures on ℤ_p correspond isometrically to their bounded moment sequences μ(x choose n), so the Amice transform is onto the power series with bounded coefficients; Mathlib master has the ℤ_p-coefficient case (Colmez, *Fonctions d'une variable p-adique*, §II.2).
name: Mahler duality for measures on ℤ_p

about: on the cotangent bundle T*M of a manifold with boundary or corners, the tautological one-form λ_p(v) = p(dπ v), which pulls back along any one-form α to α, and the closed nondegenerate form ω = −dλ, Σ dqᵢ ∧ dpᵢ in charts (Cannas da Silva, *Lectures on Symplectic Geometry*, §2).
name: The Liouville form and canonical symplectic form of a cotangent bundle

about: C : ℝ → ℝ, continuous and monotone with C(0) = 0, C(1) = 1, derivative 0 almost everywhere, total variation 1 and not absolutely continuous, whose Stieltjes measure is an atomless probability measure singular to Lebesgue measure (Folland, *Real Analysis*, §1.5).
name: The Cantor–Lebesgue function

about: a Noetherian ring R with R/p a Japanese domain for every prime p; finite algebras over Nagata rings are Nagata, and a Noetherian domain of dimension at most one is Nagata exactly when it is Japanese (Stacks, Tag 032R).
name: Nagata rings

about: a smooth closed subgroup of a finite-type affine group over a field that contains a Borel subgroup after base change to an algebraic closure; over an algebraically closed field, exactly the smooth subgroups with a conjugate containing a given Borel (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §11.2).
name: Parabolic subgroups of an algebraic group

about: a sequence a : ℕ → Δ is k-automatic when a finite automaton with output computes a(n) from the base-k digits of n; such sequences are closed under maps and pairing, take finitely many values, and include every eventually periodic sequence (Allouche–Shallit, *Automatic Sequences*, Ch. 5).
name: Automatic sequences

about: for a map g between complex normed spaces, ∂g and ∂̄g are the complex-linear and antilinear parts of its real derivative; ∂̄g = 0 when g is holomorphic, and ∂ⱼ∂̄ₖ f is the Levi form of a C² real function f (Hörmander, *An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, Ch. II).
name: Wirtinger derivatives

about: the overconvergent power series R⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩†, those restricted at some radius ρ > 1; dense in and, over a field, strictly smaller than the Tate algebra, and an overconvergent series is invertible exactly when it is in the Tate algebra (Große-Klönne, *J. reine angew. Math.* 519, 2000, §1.2).
name: The Monsky–Washnitzer algebra

about: in a regular local ring every regular system of parameters is a regular sequence, so the depth equals the Krull dimension (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 17.8).
name: Regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay

about: on ℝⁿ, if U(0) = 0 and s ↦ sⁿU(s⁻ⁿ) is convex and nonincreasing, the internal energy ∫U(dμ/dx) is convex along displacement interpolation, hence along W₂-geodesics from absolutely continuous measures (McCann 1997, Thm 2.2).
name: McCann's displacement convexity of internal energies

about: converse to TauCeti#14123: for 1 < p < ∞ on a complete separable X, every geodesic of P_p(X) is the marginal curve of a probability on paths carried by constant-speed geodesics with optimal endpoint coupling, and W_p^p is the least expected p-action (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Ch. 7).
name: Wasserstein geodesics come from optimal dynamic plans

about: for a simple Lie algebra 𝔤 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every 2-cocycle on 𝔤[t, t⁻¹] with trivial coefficients is a coboundary plus a multiple of the residue cocycle Res(f dg) κ(x, y), itself not a coboundary (Kac, *Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras*, Ch. 7).
name: The second cohomology of a loop algebra is one-dimensional

about: any two countable graphs in which, for disjoint finite s and t, some vertex is adjacent to all of s and none of t are isomorphic; the Rado graph on ℕ, i < j adjacent when bit i of j is set, is one (Cameron, *The random graph*, 1997).
name: The Rado graph is the unique countable graph with the extension property

about: for a completely continuous endomorphism u of c₀(I, K) over a complete nonarchimedean field, a nonzero μ lies in the spectrum of u exactly when μ⁻¹ is a zero of the Fredholm determinant det(1 − Tu) (Serre, *Endomorphismes complètement continus*, 1962, §§5–6).
name: The spectrum of a completely continuous p-adic operator

about: over any field and in every characteristic, a reductive group whose geometric points form a solvable group is a torus; hence the radical of a reductive group is a central torus and its derived group is semisimple (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §11.5).
name: Solvable reductive groups are tori

about: an integral proper curve over a field k whose local rings are discrete valuation rings, with k algebraically closed in its function field, is a closed subscheme of a projective space over k (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6.7).
name: Regular proper curves are projective

about: for q ≠ 0, multiplication p ⊗ r ⊗ s ↦ p(F) r(K) s(E) is a linear isomorphism ℂ[F] ⊗ ℂ[K, K⁻¹] ⊗ ℂ[E] ≃ U_q(sl₂), sending the monomial bases to the PBW basis F^a K^b E^c (Jantzen, *Lectures on Quantum Groups*, Ch. 1).
name: The triangular decomposition of U_q(sl₂)

about: a finite group of invertible order acting by C¹ maps near a common fixed point is conjugate by a local chart to its derivative representation there, and an element acts trivially nearby exactly when its derivative is the identity (Bochner 1945).
name: Bochner's linearization theorem for finite group actions

about: given a maximum s–t flow, the minimum cuts ordered by inclusion are order-isomorphic to the upper sets of the poset of free strongly connected components of the residual graph, so the minimum cut is unique exactly when there are none (Picard–Queyranne 1980).
name: The Picard–Queyranne theorem on minimum cuts

about: over any commutative ring R and n ≥ 2, a homogeneous symmetric additive 2-cocycle of degree n is r·C_n for a unique r ∈ R, with C_n = ((X + Y)ⁿ − Xⁿ − Yⁿ)/d_n, d_n = p if n is a power of the prime p, else 1 (Ravenel, *Complex Cobordism*, App. A2.1).
name: Lazard's symmetric 2-cocycle lemma

about: for ĝ = e^{2φ}g on an n-manifold, Ric^ĝ = Ric^g − (n − 2)(Hess φ − dφ ⊗ dφ) − (Δφ + (n − 2)|dφ|²) g and Scal^ĝ = e^{−2φ}(Scal^g − 2(n − 1)Δφ − (n − 1)(n − 2)|dφ|²), Δ = div grad (Besse, *Einstein Manifolds*, 1.159).
name: Ricci and scalar curvature under conformal change

about: two quadrilinear forms alternating in each argument pair and satisfying the first Bianchi identity agree once their values T(x, y, y, x) agree on independent pairs (6 ≠ 0), so constant sectional curvature κ forces R(w, u)v = κ(⟨u, v⟩w − ⟨w, v⟩u) (do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 4, Lemma 3.3).
name: Sectional curvature determines the curvature tensor

about: for a primitive integral form f = (a, b, c) of discriminant D, the stabiliser of f in SL₂(ℤ) is the group of norm-one units of ℤ[(D + √D)/2], x + y√D acting as (x − by, −2cy; 2ay, x + by) (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §7).
name: Automorphs of a binary quadratic form are the norm-one units of its order

about: the number of noncrossing partitions of n ordered points is the n-th Catalan number, by the recurrence on the block containing the first point (Kreweras 1972).
name: Noncrossing partitions are counted by the Catalan numbers

about: a complete Tate ring R with R° bounded and a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ R° with ϖ^p dividing p and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p bijective; such rings are reduced, ℂ_p is perfectoid and ℚ_p is not (Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, Def. 3.1).
name: Perfectoid Tate rings

about: K ⊆ ℂⁿ is polynomially convex when it contains every z with |p(z)| ≤ sup_K |p| for all polynomials p; compact subsets of ℝⁿ are polynomially convex, and a compact polynomially convex set has polynomial polyhedron neighbourhoods in any open set (Hörmander, *Complex Analysis in Several Variables*, §2.7).
name: Polynomially convex sets

about: for a plane domain U, the classes of null chains, sequences of disjoint crosscuts of chordal diameter tending to zero that cut off nested subdomains, two chains being equivalent when each domain of one contains a domain of the other (Pommerenke, *Boundary Behaviour of Conformal Maps*, §2.4).
name: Carathéodory's prime ends

about: for a number field K and every finite Galois layer L/F inside K̄, Tate's invariant H²(Gal(L/F), C_L) → ℚ/ℤ, the sum of the local invariants of an idelic lift, is injective with image the [L:F]-torsion, and H¹(Gal(L/F), C_L) vanishes (Tate, in Cassels–Fröhlich, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Ch. VII §11).
name: The idele class group is a class formation

about: on a Hausdorff σ-compact manifold, 0 → Ω_c(U ∩ V) → Ω_c(U) ⊕ Ω_c(V) → Ω_c(U ∪ V) → 0, with maps (ext, −ext) and ext + ext, is short exact, giving the long exact sequence of H_c (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, §2).
name: Mayer–Vietoris for compactly supported de Rham cohomology

about: for linear parabolic operators P with a ≥ 0 of bounded trace, bounded drift and c bounded above, classical u, v on [0, T] × ℝⁿ with Pu ≤ Pv, u ≤ v at t = 0 and u − v bounded above satisfy u ≤ v; bounded solutions of the Cauchy problem are unique (Friedman, *Partial Differential Equations of Parabolic Type*, Ch. 2 §4).
name: The comparison principle for parabolic equations on ℝⁿ

about: two elements of a free group are conjugate exactly when the cyclic reductions of their reduced words are cyclic permutations of each other (Lyndon–Schupp, *Combinatorial Group Theory*, Ch. I).
name: The conjugacy criterion for free groups

about: for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and a complete separable geodesic target Z, any two measured kernels modulo weak isomorphism are joined by a GW_p-geodesic, obtained by interpolating the kernels along geodesics of Z over an optimal coupling (Bauer–Mémoli–Needham–Nishino, *The Z-Gromov–Wasserstein distance*, 2025, Thm 45).
name: The Gromov–Wasserstein space is geodesic

about: at generic q, M(μ) is simple exactly when μ ≠ ±q^m; for μ = ±q^m its only proper nonzero submodule is generated by F^(m+1) v₀, with the signed (m+1)-dimensional simple module as quotient, sharpening the construction of TauCeti#18374 (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, §VI.3).
name: The simplicity criterion for Verma modules of U_q(sl₂)

about: G is amenable when the bounded uniformly continuous functions on G carry a left-invariant mean; amenability passes to images under surjective continuous homomorphisms, and Mathlib has Følner filters but no definition of amenability (Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, *Kazhdan's Property (T)*, App. G).
name: Amenable topological groups

about: for a number field with the n-th roots of unity and a prime P with N(P) prime to n, (x/P)ₙ is the unique n-th root of unity congruent to x^((N(P) − 1)/n) mod P, a residue-field character of order n (Ireland–Rosen, *A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory*, Ch. 14 §2).
name: The power residue symbol

about: for a positive functional φ on a unital C*-algebra and selfadjoint a, the unique finite measure μ_a on spectrum(a) with φ(f(a)) = ∫ f dμ_a for continuous f; its moments are φ(aⁿ) and μ_(g(a)) = g_*μ_a (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lecture 3).
name: The law of a selfadjoint element in a C*-probability space

about: for a binary code C, the Construction A vectors with coordinate sum ≡ 0 mod 4 under the halved dot product, an even lattice of index 2 in Construction A for doubly even C such as the Golay code (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 5).
name: Construction B

about: the law on count vectors k ∈ ℕ^ι with mass Γ(r + Σk)/(Γ(r) ∏kᵢ!) · p₀^r ∏pᵢ^(kᵢ) for real shape r > 0 and weights p₀ + Σpᵢ = 1, built as a Gamma(r, p₀) mixture of independent Poisson counts (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Discrete Multivariate Distributions*).
name: The negative multinomial distribution

about: for 0 < q < 1, the law on positive integers with mass −qᵏ/(k log(1 − q)), with generating function log(1 − qt)/log(1 − q), mean −q/((1 − q) log(1 − q)) and the matching variance (Johnson–Kemp–Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, Ch. 7).
name: The logarithmic distribution

about: in a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form over a field of characteristic zero, every nonzero ad-nilpotent element e is the nilpositive element of an sl₂-triple (h, e, f) (Jacobson, *Lie Algebras*, III §11).
name: The Jacobson–Morozov theorem

about: in characteristic zero, two sl₂-triples (h, e, f) and (h′, e, f′) with the same nilpositive element are conjugate by an automorphism fixing e, in the group generated by the exp(ad y) with y ∈ ker(ad e) ∩ [e, 𝔤] (Collingwood–McGovern, Thm 3.4.10).
name: Kostant's conjugacy theorem for sl₂-triples

about: for finite alphabets x and y, Σ_λ s_λ(x) s_λ(y) t^{|λ|} = ∏_{i,j} (1 − x_i y_j t)⁻¹ as power series, the degree-n part of the left side being h_n(x_i y_j) (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I.4 (4.3)).
name: The Cauchy identity for Schur polynomials

about: for a finite group G acting linearly on a finite-dimensional space M over a field in which |G| is invertible, the Hilbert series of Sym(M)^G is |G|⁻¹ Σ_g det(1 − t g)⁻¹ (Stanley 1979, Thm 2.1).
name: Molien's formula

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, an operator T has absolutely p-summing norm at most C exactly when ‖Tx‖ ≤ C (∫ |f(x)|^p dν(f))^{1/p} for some regular Borel probability measure ν on the weak-* dual unit ball (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, Thm 2.12).
name: The Pietsch domination theorem

about: on ℝⁿ with n ≥ 2, every integrable u satisfies ‖u‖_{n/(n−1)} ≤ C |Du|(ℝⁿ), extending Mathlib's inequality for compactly supported C¹ functions, with the same constant, to BV (Ambrosio–Fusco–Pallara, Thm 3.47).
name: The Sobolev inequality for functions of bounded variation

about: in a finite network with capacities in ℤd, d > 0, some flow with values in ℤd has value equal to the capacity of a cut, and every Ford–Fulkerson augmentation sequence terminates; rational capacities follow (Kleinberg–Tardos, *Algorithm Design*, §7.2).
name: The max-flow min-cut theorem for integer capacities

about: a graded algebra H over a field with HH^{n,2−n}(H, H) = 0 for all n ≥ 3 is intrinsically formal: every minimal A∞-structure with its grading and product is A∞-isomorphic to H (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §3.4).
name: Kadeishvili's intrinsic formality criterion

about: for A, B in a discrete subgroup of PSL(2, ℝ) with A hyperbolic or elliptic, unless B preserves the fixed-point set of A, |tr²A − 4| + |tr[A, B] − 2| ≥ 1; the parabolic case is Shimizu's lemma (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, Thm 2.4.6).
name: Jørgensen's inequality for Fuchsian groups

about: over a complete ultrametric field, a power series converging on the closed disc of radius c whose Gauss norm is last attained at index s has at most s zeros of norm ≤ c in any complete extension field (Strassmann 1928).
name: Strassmann's theorem

about: an even unimodular lattice containing L ⊥ M and meeting the two summands' spans in exactly L and M is the gluing of L and M along an anti-isometry q_L ≅ −q_M of discriminant forms (Nikulin 1979, Prop. 1.6.1).
name: Even unimodular overlattices of L ⊥ M are discriminant gluings

about: for a tower of modules A₀ ← A₁ ← ⋯ in which the images of A_k → A_n stabilise as k grows, lim¹ A_n = 0 (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, Prop. 3.5.7).
name: Mittag-Leffler towers have vanishing lim¹

about: every continuous f : ℤ_p → E, E a complete ultrametric normed group, is the uniform sum Σ a_n(f) e_n over indicators e_n of the balls n + p^{ℓ(n)}ℤ_p, and f ↦ (a_n(f)) is an isometry onto null sequences (Schikhof, *Ultrametric Calculus*, §62).
name: The van der Put basis of C(ℤ_p, E)

about: for an abelian sheaf F and closed S ⊆ X, 𝓗_S^n(F) is the sheafification of W ↦ H^n_S(W, F); 𝓗_S⁰(F) is the sheaf of sections supported in S, the stalks vanish off S, and 𝓗_S^{n+1}(F) = 0 for flasque F (Grothendieck, *Local Cohomology*, LNM 41, §1).
name: Local cohomology sheaves

about: Θ_L(τ) = Σ_{v∈L} exp(πi‖v‖²τ) for a lattice L in a finite-dimensional real normed space, with the series of a translate γ + L; both converge locally uniformly on ℍ and are holomorphic there (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §6).
name: The theta series of a lattice

about: κ_π = Σ_{σ≤π} μ(σ, π) φ_σ by Möbius inversion on the lattice of noncrossing partitions, κ_n = κ_{1_n}, with the moment–cumulant formula φ(a₁⋯a_n) = Σ_{π∈NC(n)} κ_π and its inverse (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Lectures 10–11).
name: Free cumulants

about: the meromorphic functions on a connected Riemann surface X, as holomorphic maps X → ℙ¹ other than the constant ∞, form a field and a ℂ-algebra, each operation determined by its values off the poles (Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, §1).
name: The field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface

about: for a root α, D_α on ℤ[M] sends e^x to e^x + e^{x−α} + ⋯ + e^{x−mα} when m = ⟨x, α^∨⟩ ≥ 0, with (1 − e^{−α})D_α f = f − e^{−α}s_α f and D_α² = D_α (Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, II.14).
name: Demazure operators

about: the raising and lowering operators e_α, f_α on piecewise-linear paths, reflecting the record segments of the coroot height and translating the rest by ±α, independent of the presentation of the path (Littelmann, *Ann. of Math.* 142 (1995), §1).
name: Littelmann's root operators

about: the law on (m, ∞) with density √(c/2π) (x − m)^{−3/2} exp(−c/(2(x − m))), the law of m + c/Z² for a standard Gaussian Z, with cdf erfc(√(c/(2(x − m)))) and |X − m|^q integrable exactly for q < 1/2 (Nolan, *Univariate Stable Distributions*, Ch. 1).
name: The Lévy distribution

about: the law with density p/(2sΓ(1/p)) exp(−|(x − m)/s|^p), Laplace at p = 1 and Gaussian at p = 2, with E|X − m|^q = s^q Γ((q+1)/p)/Γ(1/p) exactly for q > −1 (Nadarajah 2005).
name: The generalized normal distribution

about: a map between boundaryless topological manifolds of the same finite dimension that is continuous and injective on an open set has open image, so a continuous injection is an open embedding (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 2B.3).
name: Brouwer's invariance of domain

about: over an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, every nonconstant polynomial over K⸨X⸩ has a root in K⸨X^{1/n}⸩ for some n (Walker, *Algebraic Curves*, Ch. IV).
name: The Newton–Puiseux theorem

about: now in full: for every u locally integrable on an open set Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, |Du|(Ω) = ∫_ℝ P({u > t}; Ω) dt, both sides possibly infinite (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, Thm 5.9).
name: The coarea formula for BV functions

about: in a finite network with nonnegative capacities in any linearly ordered abelian group, including ℝ, some flow has value equal to the capacity of some cut, upgrading the integer case of TauCeti#19011 (Ford–Fulkerson, *Flows in Networks*, Ch. I).
name: The max-flow min-cut theorem

about: for a finite group acting on a finite-type algebra A over a Noetherian ring, A^G is of finite type and A is a finite A^G-module; over a ℚ-algebra, A^G is generated by orbit sums of monomials of degree at most |G| (Derksen–Kemper, *Computational Invariant Theory*, Ch. 3).
name: Noether's finiteness theorem for invariants of finite groups

about: for a smooth connection on a vector bundle and a torsion-free connection on the tangent bundle, (∇_X R)(Y, Z) + (∇_Y R)(Z, X) + (∇_Z R)(X, Y) = 0 (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Prop 7.5).
name: The second Bianchi identity

about: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ and a Banach target, π_p(T) ≤ C exactly when T = S ∘ j_p with j_p : E → Lᵖ(ν) the evaluation map for a probability measure ν on the weak-* dual ball and ‖S‖ ≤ C (Diestel–Jarchow–Tonge, Thm 2.13).
name: The Pietsch factorization theorem

about: for a scheme X and a graded 𝒪_X-algebra A with quasi-coherent components, the scheme glued from the Proj(⨁ₙ Γ(U, Aₙ)) over affine opens U, with that description over every affine open (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II §7).
name: The relative Proj of a graded quasi-coherent algebra

about: for a henselian pair (S, J) and a map of pairs (R, I) → (S, J), there is a unique R-algebra map from the henselization of (R, I) to S carrying the extended ideal into J (Stacks, Tag 0A02).
name: The henselization of a pair, with its universal property

about: the least number of open sets covering a subset of X whose inclusions into X are nullhomotopic, with monotonicity, subadditivity, the deformation inequality and homotopy invariance (Cornea–Lupton–Oprea–Tanré, *Lusternik–Schnirelmann Category*, Ch. 1).
name: The Lusternik–Schnirelmann category

about: λ_i(L, K) is the least t with i + 1 independent lattice vectors in tK; they are attained simultaneously, and some ℤ-basis b of L has b_i ∈ max(1, (i+1)/2) λ_i K (Cassels, *Geometry of Numbers*, Ch. V Lemma 8).
name: Successive minima of a lattice with respect to a convex body

about: MN(M, U, V), whose vectorisation is N(vec M, V ⊗ U), with entry covariances U_ik V_jl, Gaussian rows and columns, transposition and affine images (Gupta–Nagar, *Matrix Variate Distributions*, Ch. 2).
name: The matrix normal distribution

about: the law of m + X − Y for independent exponentials of rates r and l, with its two-sided exponential density, characteristic function, mean and variance (Kotz–Kozubowski–Podgórski, *The Laplace Distribution and Generalizations*, Ch. 3).
name: The asymmetric Laplace distribution

about: now in full: for distinct algebraic numbers α₁, …, αₙ the values e^{α₁}, …, e^{αₙ} are linearly independent over ℚ̄, so for ℚ-linearly independent algebraic αᵢ they are algebraically independent (Baker, *Transcendental Number Theory*, Ch. 1).
name: The Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem

about: for a cyclic extension L/K of number fields, a ∈ Kˣ is a norm from L exactly when it is a norm from K_v ⊗_K L at every finite and infinite place v (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §4).
name: The Hasse norm theorem

about: for a Schwartz function f on a Euclidean space and the lattice ℤⁿ of an orthonormal basis, Σ_{m∈ℤⁿ} f(v + m) = Σ_{m∈ℤⁿ} 𝓕f(m) e^{2πi⟨v, m⟩}, extending Mathlib's one-dimensional theorem (Stein–Weiss, *Fourier Analysis on Euclidean Spaces*, VII Cor. 2.6).
name: The Poisson summation formula on ℝⁿ

about: now in full: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ on a finite-dimensional normed space, W_p(μ₀, μ₁)^p is the least value of ∫₀¹∫‖v_t‖^p dν_t dt over narrowly continuous curves of measures from μ₀ to μ₁ solving ∂_tν + div(vν) = 0 (Santambrogio, *Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians*, Thm 5.28).
name: The Benamou–Brenier formula

about: for a field K with separable closure Ω, A ↦ Hom_K(A, Ω) is an anti-equivalence between finite étale K-algebras and finite sets with a continuous Gal(Ω/K)-action (Lenstra, *Galois Theory for Schemes*, §2; SGA 1, V §8).
name: Grothendieck's Galois correspondence for finite étale algebras

about: a smooth nondegenerate metric of any signature on a finite-dimensional manifold has a torsion-free metric connection, and it is smooth, extending the positive-definite case already in Mathlib (O'Neill, *Semi-Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3 Thm 11).
name: The fundamental theorem of pseudo-Riemannian geometry

about: smoothly homotopic maps f, g : M → M' induce the same map H^k_dR(M') → H^k_dR(M) in every degree, with M allowed boundary and corners (Bott–Tu, *Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology*, §4).
name: Homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology

about: for compact convex A, B ⊆ ℝⁿ of positive volume and c, d > 0, |cA + dB|^{1/n} = c|A|^{1/n} + d|B|^{1/n} exactly when B is a translate of a positive dilate of A (Schneider, *Convex Bodies*, Thm 7.1.1).
name: The equality case of the Brunn–Minkowski inequality

about: a distribution T on an open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ satisfies |T φ| ≤ C_K‖φ‖_∞ for test functions supported in each compact K exactly when T = ν₁ − ν₂ for regular Borel measures finite on compact sets (Hörmander, *ALPDO I*, Thm 2.1.7).
name: Distributions of order zero are measures

about: the field of meromorphic functions on ℙ¹(ℂ) is ℂ(z), by evaluation of rational functions at the coordinate (Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, Cor. 2.9).
name: Meromorphic functions on the Riemann sphere are rational

about: over a field with an integer-valued valuation, a polynomial of degree d with nonzero constant term whose Newton polygon is one segment of slope a/d with gcd(a, d) = 1 is irreducible (Dumas 1906; Prasolov, *Polynomials*, §2.2).
name: The Eisenstein–Dumas irreducibility criterion

about: over a ring containing ℚ, the inclusion of Connes' cyclic cochain complex into column zero of the total complex of the cyclic bicomplex is a quasi-isomorphism (Loday, *Cyclic Homology*, §2.1).
name: The cyclic bicomplex computes cyclic cohomology

about: in a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over a Noetherian ring, the scheme-theoretic centralizer of the image of a diagonalizable group D(X) is smooth (SGA 3, XI Cor. 5.3).
name: Centralizers of diagonalizable subgroups are smooth

about: for a linear functional φ on a module M, the complex ⋯ → ⋀²M → M → R with differential the contraction by φ, with H₀(K(φ)) ≃ R/φ(M), so H₀(K(x)) ≃ R/(x₁, …, xₙ) for a finite sequence x; also being formalised in mathlib4#43708 (Stacks, Tag 0621).
name: The Koszul complex

about: on E ⊗ F for normed spaces, π(u) = inf Σ‖xᵢ‖‖yᵢ‖ over decompositions and ε(u) = sup{|Σ f(xᵢ)g(yᵢ)| : ‖f‖, ‖g‖ ≤ 1}; both are cross norms and ε ≤ π (Ryan, *Introduction to Tensor Products of Banach Spaces*, §§2.1, 3.1).
name: The projective and injective tensor norms

about: a transitive ℤ₊-ring, such as the Grothendieck ring of a fusion category, has exactly one ring homomorphism to ℝ nonnegative on the basis; it is positive there and sends a simple object to the spectral radius of its fusion matrix (Etingof–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik, *Tensor Categories*, Prop. 3.3.6).
name: The Frobenius–Perron character of a fusion category

about: for a lattice L in a finite-dimensional complex vector space E, the quotient E/L is a compact connected complex Lie group with the projection a local biholomorphism (Birkenhake–Lange, *Complex Abelian Varieties*, §1.1).
name: Complex tori

about: g_r(τ) = −e^{πi B₂(r₁)τ} e^{πi r₂(r₁−1)} (1 − q_z) ∏_{n≥1}(1 − qⁿq_z)(1 − qⁿq_z⁻¹), q_z = e^{2πi(r₁τ+r₂)}, holomorphic and nonvanishing on ℍ for r ∉ ℤ², with its translation laws in r and in τ (Kubert–Lang, *Modular Units*, Ch. 2 §1).
name: Siegel functions

about: the law with mass k^{−s}/ζ(s) at k ≥ 1 for s > 1, whose m-th moment exists exactly when m < s − 1 and equals ζ(s − m)/ζ(s) (Johnson–Kemp–Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, Ch. 11).
name: The zeta (Zipf) distribution

about: the law on (0, ∞) with density √(λ/2πx³) exp(−λ(x − μ)²/2μ²x), cdf Φ(√(λ/x)(x/μ − 1)) + e^{2λ/μ} Φ(−√(λ/x)(x/μ + 1)), and bX ∼ IG(bμ, bλ) for b > 0 (Chhikara–Folks, *The Inverse Gaussian Distribution*, 1989).
name: The inverse Gaussian distribution

about: every module over any ring has an injective envelope, an injective module containing it as an essential submodule, and one is found inside any injective module containing it (Eckmann–Schopf 1953; Lam, *Lectures on Modules and Rings*, Thm 3.29).
name: Existence of injective envelopes

about: if f is bounded on [0, ∞) and its Laplace transform G(z) = ∫₀^∞ f(t)e^{−zt} dt extends holomorphically to a neighbourhood of Re z ≥ 0, then ∫₀^∞ f(t) dt converges to G(0) (Newman 1980; Zagier, *Newman's short proof of the prime number theorem*, 1997).
name: Newman's Tauberian theorem

about: for a tower of complexes of modules C₀ ← C₁ ← ⋯ with surjective transition maps, or Mittag-Leffler in each degree, 0 → lim¹ Hᵢ(Cₙ) → Hⱼ(lim Cₙ) → lim Hⱼ(Cₙ) → 0 is exact for consecutive degrees i, j (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, Thm 3.5.8).
name: The Milnor exact sequence

about: for a torsion-free metric connection on a connected manifold of dimension at least three, if the sectional curvature at each point is the same on every tangent two-plane, then it is constant (Kobayashi–Nomizu, *Foundations of Differential Geometry* I, Ch. V Thm 2.2).
name: Schur's theorem

about: for a finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L) has index exactly [L : K] in the idele class group C_K (Milne, *Class Field Theory*, Ch. VII; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §5).
name: The global norm index theorem

about: for a Riemannian metric g and smooth f > 0 in dimension n ≠ 2, the Weyl tensor of fg is f·W^g, so the (1,3) Weyl tensor is conformally invariant; the Schouten tensor transforms by the standard Hessian formula (Besse, *Einstein Manifolds*, Thm 1.159).
name: Conformal invariance of the Weyl tensor

about: for every nonsquare discriminant D, now including indefinite D > 0, the primitive integral forms of discriminant D fall into finitely many proper classes, each containing a form with |b| ≤ |a| ≤ |c|, so 3|ac| ≤ |D| (Lagrange 1773; Buell, *Binary Quadratic Forms*, Ch. 3).
name: Finiteness of classes of binary quadratic forms

about: two odd unimodular symmetric bilinear forms over the 2-adic integers of the same rank are isometric exactly when their determinants differ by a square and their oddities, the norms of characteristic vectors modulo 8, agree (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 15 §7).
name: Classification of odd unimodular forms over ℤ₂

about: for q nonzero and not a root of unity, the center of U_q(sl₂) is the polynomial algebra ℂ[Ω] on the Casimir element Ω = FE + (qK + q⁻¹K⁻¹)/(q − q⁻¹)² (Kassel, *Quantum Groups*, Thm VI.4.8).
name: The center of U_q(sl₂)

about: on an open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, a family of functions with ∫_Ω |u| ≤ M and |Du|(Ω) ≤ M is relatively compact in L¹(K) for every compact K ⊆ Ω (Ambrosio–Fusco–Pallara, *Functions of Bounded Variation and Free Discontinuity Problems*, Thm 3.23).
name: Compactness in L¹_loc for functions of bounded variation

about: K ∪ (s + K), with K the Construction B lattice of the binary Golay code and s = (−3/2, 1/2, …, 1/2): a positive definite even unimodular lattice of rank 24 with minimum norm 4, so rootless (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 4 §11).
name: The Leech lattice

about: the coproduct and conjugation on LB = L[b₁, b₂, …] over the Lazard ring L, satisfying all the Hopf algebroid identities, so that (L, LB) corepresents the groupoid of formal group laws and strict isomorphisms (Ravenel, *Complex Cobordism and Stable Homotopy Groups of Spheres*, A2.1).
name: The Hopf algebroid (L, LB) of formal group laws

about: the sphere symmetric sequence n ↦ (S¹)^∧n of pointed simplicial sets is a commutative monoid for Day convolution, and symmetric spectra are defined as the modules over it (Hovey–Shipley–Smith, *Symmetric spectra*, 2000, §§1.2, 2.2).
name: Symmetric spectra

about: subsets of a real normed space that near every point are finite Boolean combinations of sets f = 0 and f > 0 with f real analytic; a Boolean algebra stable under analytic preimages, containing the semialgebraic sets (Bierstone–Milman, *Semianalytic and subanalytic sets*, §2).
name: Semianalytic sets

about: for an sl₂-triple (h, e, f), the affine subspace e + ker(ad f), with the contracting action c ↦ c² Ad(λ(c⁻¹)) of Kˣ, which fixes e, preserves the slice, and has weights at least 2 on its direction (Slodowy, *Simple Singularities and Simple Algebraic Groups*, §7.4).
name: The Slodowy slice

about: a hypersurface in a symplectic manifold (M, ω) near which ω = dα with a Liouville vector field transverse to it; the unit cosphere bundle of a Riemannian manifold is of restricted contact type in T*M (Weinstein 1979; McDuff–Salamon, *Introduction to Symplectic Topology*, Ch. 3).
name: Hypersurfaces of contact type

about: the law of U/(U + V) for independent U ∼ noncentral χ²(2a; λ) and V ∼ χ²(2b), equal to the Poisson mixture Σⱼ e^{−λ/2}(λ/2)^j/j! · Beta(a + j, b); then (b/a)X/(1 − X) is noncentral F(2a, 2b; λ) (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions* 2, Ch. 30).
name: The noncentral beta distribution

about: every irreducible reduced crystallographic root system over ℚ is isomorphic to the model root system of exactly one Dynkin type, now independently of the chosen base and with every type realised by a model (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §11).
name: The Cartan–Killing classification of root systems

about: a map U : (Ω, m) → ℝⁿ with absolutely continuous law and finite quadratic cost to an absolutely continuous P factors as U = ∇u ∘ s, u convex, s of law P, s unique and minimising ∫‖s′ − U‖² among maps of law P (Brenier, CPAM 44 (1991), Thm 1.2).
name: Brenier's polar factorization theorem

about: over a regular local ring of dimension d every module, finitely generated or not, has projective dimension at most d, and the residue field has projective dimension exactly d (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 19.2).
name: The global dimension of a regular local ring is its Krull dimension

about: for a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω and 1 ≤ p < ∞ there is a unique bounded linear trace W^{1,p}(Ω) → Lᵖ(∂Ω, 𝓗ⁿ⁻¹) sending every function continuous up to the boundary to its restriction to ∂Ω (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.5 Thm 1).
name: The trace theorem on Lipschitz domains

about: a smooth function on a compact manifold without boundary has at least as many critical points, degenerate ones included, as the Lusternik–Schnirelmann category of the manifold (Cornea–Lupton–Oprea–Tanré, *Lusternik–Schnirelmann Category*, Ch. 1).
name: The Lusternik–Schnirelmann theorem

about: for an ordered abstract simplicial complex K and any coefficient ring, the homology of its ordered simplicial chain complex is the singular homology of the realization |K|, through the cellular chains of its CW structure (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 2.27).
name: Simplicial homology is singular homology

about: for every group G and commutative ring k, Hₙ(BG; k) of Milnor's classifying space is the group homology Hₙ(G, k) of the trivial module, in every degree (Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, II.4).
name: The homology of a classifying space is group homology

about: an integer p × n matrix A of rank p has n − p independent primitive integer kernel vectors x₁, …, x_{n−p} with ∏ ‖xₗ‖_∞ ≤ √det(AAᵀ) / g, g the gcd of the p × p minors of A (Bombieri–Vaaler, Invent. Math. 73 (1983), Thm 2).
name: Bombieri–Vaaler's theorem

about: an elliptic curve over a nonarchimedean local field has potential good reduction exactly when inertia acts on its ℓ-adic Tate module through a finite quotient, ℓ prime to the residue characteristic (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VII.7.3).
name: The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion for potential good reduction

about: if a Banach algebra A with a left approximate identity bounded by C acts boundedly on a Banach space E, every x in the closed span of A·E is a·y with ‖a‖ ≤ C and y ∈ closure(A·x) arbitrarily close to x (Dales, *Banach Algebras and Automatic Continuity*, Thm 2.9.24).
name: The Cohen–Hewitt factorization theorem

about: for a weakly regular sequence x₁, …, xₙ in a commutative ring R, the Koszul complex K(x) has vanishing homology in positive degrees, so it is a finite free resolution of R/(x₁, …, xₙ) (Stacks, Tag 062F).
name: The Koszul complex of a regular sequence is acyclic

about: two smooth embeddings of ℝⁿ into a boundaryless n-manifold with the same centre and derivatives there of the same orientation are smoothly isotopic through embeddings fixing the centre (Hirsch, *Differential Topology*, Ch. 4 Thm 6.6).
name: The disc theorem in a manifold

about: for every group G and module M over a commutative ring, Hⁿ(BG; M) of Milnor's classifying space is the group cohomology Hⁿ(G, M) of the trivial module M (Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, III.1).
name: The cohomology of a classifying space is group cohomology

about: on a Banach space over a complete nonarchimedean field, 1 − u is Fredholm of index zero for every completely continuous u, so it is invertible exactly when injective, exactly when surjective (Serre, *Endomorphismes complètement continus des espaces de Banach p-adiques*, 1962).
name: The Fredholm alternative for completely continuous operators

about: for modules M, N over a commutative ring, composition with the universal law γ_d is a linear equivalence between linear maps Γ^d(M) → N out of the degree-d divided power module and homogeneous polynomial laws M → N of degree d (Roby, Ann. ENS 1963, Thm IV.1).
name: Roby's representability theorem

about: a nonempty closed bounded set s ⊆ ℝⁿ has the volume of a ball of radius diam(s)/2 exactly when it is such a ball, and a bounded measurable set exactly when it agrees with one almost everywhere (Schneider, *Convex Bodies*, Thm 7.1.1).
name: Equality in the isodiametric inequality

about: the bilinear form on degree-n symmetric polynomials in which the Schur polynomials are orthonormal, with ⟨h_μ, m_ν⟩ = δ_{μν} and ⟨p_ρ, p_σ⟩ = z_ρ δ_{ρσ}, and the Frobenius characteristic carries the character pairing of Sₙ to it (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I §4, §7).
name: The Hall inner product, and the Frobenius characteristic is an isometry

about: a function from an open subset of ℂ into a complex Banach space is holomorphic as soon as its composite with every continuous linear functional is holomorphic (Rudin, *Functional Analysis*, Thm 3.31).
name: Dunford's theorem: weak holomorphy implies holomorphy

about: for a simple Lie algebra 𝔤 over an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, Φ ↦ [Res(f dg) Φ(x, y)] is a linear isomorphism from invariant symmetric forms on 𝔤 onto H²_cont(𝔤((t)), K) (Frenkel, *Langlands Correspondence for Loop Groups*, §1.3).
name: Central extensions of the formal loop algebra are classified by invariant forms

about: for any braid word w, the writhe-normalised Markov trace of the Jones representation of its braid equals −(a² + a⁻²) times the writhe-normalised Kauffman bracket of the closure of w, so both routes give the Jones polynomial (Jones, Ann. of Math. 126 (1987)).
name: The braid and diagram routes to the Jones polynomial agree

about: for a bounded convex open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, S ⊆ Ω of positive measure and u ∈ L¹(Ω), ∫_Ω |u − ⨍_S u| ≤ |B(0,1)| (diam Ω)^{n+1}/|S| · |Du|(Ω), now with the total variation of any integrable u in place of ‖∇u‖ (Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, §5.6).
name: The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality for BV functions

about: a regular proper curve over an arbitrary field k is a closed subscheme of a projective space over k, the earlier hypothesis that k be algebraically closed in the function field now removed (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.3.12, IV.3).
name: Regular proper curves are projective, over any field

about: for a commutative Noetherian ring R, every system of group equations in finitely many variables over GLₙ(R), hence over any subgroup of it, has a finite subsystem with the same solutions (Baumslag–Myasnikov–Remeslennikov, *Algebraic geometry over groups I*, Thm B1).
name: Linear groups over Noetherian rings are equationally Noetherian

about: the matrices [[1, 2], [0, 1]] and [[1, 0], [2, 1]] freely generate a free subgroup of SL₂(ℤ), so every free group of countable rank embeds in SL₂(ℤ) (de la Harpe, *Topics in Geometric Group Theory*, II.B).
name: Sanov's theorem

about: grouping consecutive letters of a word a₁⋯aₙ into products A₁⋯Aₘ, κₘ(A₁, …, Aₘ) = Σ κ_π(a₁, …, aₙ) over the noncrossing partitions π of n whose join with the grouping partition is the one-block partition (Nica–Speicher, *Lectures on the Combinatorics of Free Probability*, Thm 11.12).
name: Free cumulants with products as arguments

about: a connected open U ⊆ ℂ is simply connected if and only if every connected component of ℂ ∖ U is unbounded (Rudin, *Real and Complex Analysis*, Thm 13.11).
name: A plane domain is simply connected exactly when it has no holes

about: (Sₙ) asks depth M_𝔭 ≥ min(n, dim M_𝔭) at every prime 𝔭, (Rₙ) that R_𝔭 be regular whenever ht 𝔭 ≤ n; a Noetherian ring is reduced exactly when it satisfies (R₀) and (S₁) (Stacks, Tag 031R).
name: Serre's conditions (Sₙ) and (Rₙ)

about: for a formal group law F over a field of characteristic p, the h with [p]_F(T) = cT^{p^h} + ⋯, c ≠ 0, or ∞ when [p]_F = 0; invariant under field extension, with 𝔾ₐ of height ∞ and 𝔾ₘ of height 1 (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, IV.7).
name: The height of a formal group law

about: for a topological monoid G, the product H_p(G; R) ⊗ H_q(G; R) → H_{p+q}(G; R) given by the homology cross product followed by the multiplication of G; it is associative and, for commutative G, graded commutative (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §3.C).
name: The Pontryagin product

about: a ring map R → B is regular when B is flat over R and every fibre κ(𝔭) ⊗_R B is geometrically regular over κ(𝔭); smooth maps and localizations are regular (Stacks, Definition 15.42.1).
name: Regular ring maps

about: for measures on two extended pseudometric spaces, the infimum over metric couplings of the Lévy–Prokhorov distance of the two measures in the glued disjoint union; symmetric, satisfying the triangle inequality and invariant under isometries (Greven–Pfaffelhuber–Winter, PTRF 145 (2009), Def. 5.1).
name: The Gromov–Prokhorov distance

about: C(X, Y, Z) = (∇_Z P)(X, Y) − (∇_Y P)(X, Z) for the Schouten tensor P of a Riemannian manifold, antisymmetric in Y, Z, cyclically summing to zero, and vanishing in constant sectional curvature (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 7).
name: The Cotton tensor

about: the law on the circle with density e^{κ cos(θ − m)}/I₀(κ) against normalised Haar measure, κ ≥ 0, with Fourier moments E[e^{inθ}] = e^{inm} I_{|n|}(κ)/I₀(κ) and mean resultant length I₁(κ)/I₀(κ) (Mardia–Jupp, *Directional Statistics*, §3.5.4).
name: The von Mises distribution

about: the law of (Z + δ)/√(V/ν) for Z standard Gaussian and V an independent χ² with ν degrees of freedom, absolutely continuous, reducing to Student's t at δ = 0 and squaring to the noncentral F(1, ν; δ²) (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions* 2, Ch. 31).
name: The noncentral t distribution

about: the law on the circle of a Cauchy variable of scale γ reduced modulo 2π and shifted to m, with Fourier moments e^{inm}e^{−γ|n|}, mean resultant length e^{−γ}, and convolutions adding locations and scales (Mardia–Jupp, *Directional Statistics*, §3.5.7).
name: The wrapped Cauchy distribution
